words.definitionEn: to make small changes to a law, document or plan to improve it
words.situation: Changing the wording of a law, contract, report or plan, usually to correct or improve it.

examples.text: Parliament voted to [[amend]] the law so that it also covers online shopping.
We [[amended]] the contract to give freelancers thirty days to submit their invoices.
Please [[amend]] the spelling of my surname on the certificate before it is printed.

texts: The rules were [[amended]] to allow dogs in the park.
She [[amended]] her statement after seeing the video evidence.
The recipe has been [[amended]] to use less sugar.

badCollocation.noteRu: Технику чинят — repair или fix the washing machine. Amend — вносить правки в текст, закон или план.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Поправки в конституцию или закон вносят глаголом amend. Repair — «чинить», correct — «исправлять ошибку», edit — «редактировать текст».

nuance.text: The government plans to [[amend]] the tax code to support small farms.
nuance.explanationRu: Amend — официально изменить закон или документ, чтобы улучшить его. Correct — исправить ошибку, а налоговый кодекс здесь не ошибочен: его дополняют.

reverse.text: The teacher [[corrected]] the spelling mistakes in red ink.
reverse.explanationRu: Исправить ошибки — correct mistakes. Amend меняет документ или закон, а не отдельные ошибки учеников.

fixIt.text: The club decided to [[repair]] its rules so that members can vote online.
fixIt.explanationRu: Repair — «чинить» вещи. Внести изменения в правила — amend the rules.

reply.context: A customer emails: "Sorry, I put the wrong delivery address on my order yesterday."
options: No problem, I've amended your parcel, so it's now much heavier.
No problem at all. I've amended the address, so the parcel will go to the right place.
Yeah whatever, sorted it, chill.
reply.explanationRu: Amend — исправить или изменить данные, например адрес в заказе. Посылку «исправить» так нельзя, а третий ответ слишком грубый для письма клиенту.

rewrite.original: The government changed the law slightly last year.
rewrite.frame: The law ____ last year.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the law was amended.

words.definitionEn: a change or addition to a law, contract or official document
words.situation: Talking about an official change added to a law, constitution or contract after a vote or agreement.

examples.text: The opposition proposed an [[amendment]] that would protect small shops from the new tax.
Any [[amendments]] to this contract must be agreed in writing by both parties.
The editor accepted the article after I made a few minor [[amendments]] to the conclusion.

texts: The [[amendment]] was passed by a narrow majority.
Freedom of speech is protected by the First [[Amendment]] in the United States.
The tenant asked for an [[amendment]] allowing her to keep a cat.

badCollocation.noteRu: Поправка к закону — an amendment to the law, а не for the law.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Поправка к конституции — a constitutional amendment. Correction — исправление ошибки, repair — ремонт, patch — «заплатка»; с constitutional так не говорят.

nuance.text: The council voted to add an [[amendment]] banning cars from the old town.
nuance.explanationRu: Amendment — поправка к закону или документу. Amends (make amends) — «загладить вину», это совсем другое слово.

reverse.text: He bought her flowers to make [[amends]] for forgetting her birthday.
reverse.explanationRu: Загладить вину — make amends for something. Amendment — поправка к тексту, к извинениям отношения не имеет.

fixIt.text: The union asked for two [[corrections]] to the contract guaranteeing paid overtime.
fixIt.explanationRu: Correction — исправление ошибки. Поправки, которые меняют условия договора, — amendments.

wordFormation.text: The senator's [[amendment]] would raise the minimum wage for farm workers.

reply.context: In a meeting, your boss asks: "The client has read our proposal. Any news?"
options: They like it overall, but they've asked for a couple of amendments to the budget section.
They loved it so much that they sent us an amendment of flowers.
Affirmative. Amendments have been requested pertaining to the budgetary provisions thereof.
reply.explanationRu: Amendments — поправки, изменения в документе. «Поправка из цветов» — бессмыслица, а третий ответ звучит как юридическая справка, а не ответ начальнику.

words.definitionEn: during or surrounded by, especially a difficult or noisy situation
words.situation: Reporting that something happened while there was noise, tension, crisis or strong public feeling around it.

examples.text: The company's shares fell sharply [[amid]] fears of a global recession.
She managed to finish her essay [[amid]] the noise of builders drilling next door.
The team celebrated [[amid]] cheering crowds as the bus drove through the city.

texts: The minister resigned [[amid]] growing criticism of her decisions.
Flights were cancelled [[amid]] concerns about the approaching storm.
The talks ended [[amid]] angry scenes outside the building.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Среди друзей» — among my friends. Amid обычно ставят перед шумом, событиями и настроениями: amid the chaos, amid fears.

collocationTask.prompt: Prices rose ___ fears of a poor harvest.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Amid fears of — «на фоне опасений». Between — «между двумя», inside — «внутри», across — «через, по всей»; с fears так не говорят.

nuance.text: The festival went ahead [[amid]] heavy rain and strong winds.
nuance.explanationRu: Amid — «среди, на фоне» шума, погоды, событий и настроений. Among — «среди» людей или предметов, которых можно посчитать: among friends, among the trees.

reverse.text: The prize money was shared [[among]] the five winners.
reverse.explanationRu: Разделить что-то между несколькими людьми — share among them. Amid с людьми, между которыми что-то делят, не употребляют.

fixIt.text: Share prices fell [[among]] fears of a new trade war.
fixIt.explanationRu: Among ставят перед группой людей или предметов. «На фоне опасений» — amid fears.

rewrite.original: The festival was cancelled because people were worried about safety.
rewrite.frame: The festival was cancelled ____ safety concerns.
rewrite.explanationRu: Amid concerns — «на фоне опасений», типичный оборот новостей.

words.definitionEn: a comparison that explains one thing by showing how it resembles another
words.situation: Explaining a difficult idea by comparing it to something simpler that works in a similar way.

examples.text: Our teacher used the [[analogy]] of a busy motorway to explain how blood flows through arteries.
Comparing a start-up to a family is a weak [[analogy]], because employees can be fired.
Journalists often draw an [[analogy]] between the current crisis and the economic collapse of 1929.

texts: The author uses a cooking [[analogy]] to explain how computer programs work.
By [[analogy]] with other planets, scientists expect to find water there.
I don't think your football [[analogy]] really works for a business meeting.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Дешёвый аналог лекарства» — a cheaper equivalent (или analogue). Analogy — сравнение для объяснения, а не похожий товар.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Провести аналогию — draw (или make) an analogy. Pull, do и put с analogy не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The lecturer used an [[analogy]] to explain the idea: the brain as a busy airport.
nuance.explanationRu: Analogy — сравнение, которое мы специально используем, чтобы объяснить мысль. Similarity — просто сходство между вещами; «использовать сходство для объяснения» так не говорят.

reverse.text: There is a striking [[similarity]] between the two sisters' voices.
reverse.explanationRu: Сходство голосов — similarity. Analogy — не само сходство, а сравнение, которое кто-то проводит, чтобы что-то объяснить.

fixIt.text: The professor drew an interesting [[analogue]] between memory and a library.
fixIt.explanationRu: Analogue — «аналог», похожий предмет или продукт. Провести сравнение для объяснения — draw an analogy.

wordFormation.text: The situation is [[analogous]] to a traffic jam: everyone moves slowly because everyone else does.

reply.context: A friend who is learning to code says: "I still don't understand what a database actually is."
options: Here's an analogy: think of it as a huge, well-organised filing cabinet.
An analogy is when a database stores your passwords.
Allow me to furnish you with an illustrative analogy of considerable sophistication.
reply.explanationRu: Analogy — сравнение, которое помогает понять сложное через простое. Во втором ответе слово объяснено неверно, а третий звучит слишком напыщенно для разговора с другом.

words.definitionEn: to base something firmly on facts, experience or a fixed point
words.senseNote: Здесь — переносное «прочно опираться, основываться на чём-то» (be anchored in facts); морское «бросать якорь» — базовое значение.
words.situation: Saying that an idea, story, plan or price is firmly based on or tied to something solid.

examples.text: Although it contains magic, the novel is [[anchored]] in real events from the 1930s.
A good presentation [[anchors]] every claim in clear evidence from real customers.
The central bank has [[anchored]] the currency to the US dollar to keep prices stable.

texts: Her confidence is [[anchored]] in years of hard practice.
The film's fantasy world feels [[anchored]] in everyday family life.
Every decision we make is [[anchored]] in the needs of our patients.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Закрепить пройденный материал» — consolidate или reinforce what you've learned. Anchor в этом учебном смысле не употребляют.

collocationTask.explanationRu: О том, что прочно опирается на факты, говорят firmly anchored (или grounded) in reality. Fastened, nailed и glued — о креплении предметов.

nuance.text: Good policy should be [[anchored]] in evidence, not in guesswork.
nuance.explanationRu: Anchored in evidence — «опирается на факты». Attach — «прикреплять» предмет или «привязаться» к человеку; attached in evidence не говорят.

reverse.text: I've become very [[attached]] to my old car.
reverse.explanationRu: Эмоционально привязаться — become attached to. Anchored говорит об опоре и основании, а не о чувствах.

fixIt.text: His arguments are always [[fixed]] in solid data, which makes them hard to dismiss.
fixIt.explanationRu: Fixed — «закреплённый, неподвижный». Опираться на данные — be anchored in data.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

words.definitionEn: with a name that is not known or not made public
words.senseNote: Здесь — «анонимный, неназванный»; значение «безликий, невыразительный» (an anonymous hotel room) не тренируем.
words.situation: Describing a person, letter, gift or comment when nobody knows or reveals who it came from.

examples.text: The letter was [[anonymous]], so the police had no idea who had sent it.
The staff survey is completely [[anonymous]], so be honest about your manager.
Some people post cruel comments online because they feel safe being [[anonymous]].

texts: A generous [[anonymous]] donor paid for the new library.
The journalist spoke to an [[anonymous]] source inside the ministry.
Online reviews can be [[anonymous]], so treat them with caution.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Остаться анонимным» — remain или stay anonymous. Keep anonymous без дополнения звучит неестественно.

collocationTask.prompt: The winner has asked to ___ anonymous.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Остаться анонимным — remain (или stay) anonymous. Keep, hold и save в этом значении без дополнения не используют.

nuance.text: The donor asked to stay [[anonymous]], so the charity cannot reveal his name.
nuance.explanationRu: Anonymous — человек сознательно не называет своё имя. Unknown — «неизвестный, малоизвестный», и попросить «остаться unknown» по-английски так не говорят.

reverse.text: The film stars a young actor who was completely [[unknown]] until last year.
reverse.explanationRu: Никому не известный, не знаменитый — unknown. Anonymous значит, что имя скрыто, а не что человек не знаменит.

fixIt.text: The police received an [[incognito]] phone call about the stolen paintings.
fixIt.explanationRu: Incognito — о человеке, который скрывает, кто он (travel incognito). Звонок от неизвестного — an anonymous call.

wordFormation.text: Journalists must protect the [[anonymity]] of their sources.

reply.context: Your manager says: "We're running a survey about workload. Will you fill it in?"
options: Sure, as long as it's anonymous and has my name and photo on it.
Affirmative, provided that the anonymity of respondents is duly guaranteed.
Of course. Will it be anonymous? People might be more honest if it is.
reply.explanationRu: Anonymous — без имени, поэтому анкета «с именем и фото» анонимной не будет. Второй ответ звучит как договор, а не ответ начальнику.

rewrite.original: The person who gave the money did not want anyone to know her name.
rewrite.frame: The donor wanted to ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Remain anonymous — «остаться анонимным».

words.definitionEn: the study of human societies, cultures and how they develop
words.situation: Talking about the academic subject that studies how people live, their customs, beliefs and social groups.

examples.text: She studied [[anthropology]] and spent a year living with a fishing community in Indonesia.
Tech companies now hire experts in [[anthropology]] to understand how people really use their phones.
The museum's new [[anthropology]] gallery displays masks, tools and clothing from dozens of cultures.

texts: He took a course in [[anthropology]] to understand other cultures.
Her book combines history, [[anthropology]] and personal memories of the village.
Social [[anthropology]] looks at family, religion and power in different societies.

badCollocation.noteRu: Динозавров изучает palaeontology. Anthropology — наука о людях, их обществах и культуре.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Социальная антропология — social anthropology. Humanity — «человечество», astrology — «астрология», humanism — «гуманизм»; с social как название специальности они не работают.

nuance.text: For her [[anthropology]] project, she interviewed families about how they celebrate weddings today.
nuance.explanationRu: Anthropology изучает общества и культуры, в том числе современные, через наблюдение и интервью. Archaeology изучает прошлое по раскопкам и находкам, интервью о свадьбах — не её метод.

reverse.text: The [[archaeology]] team found Roman coins under the car park.
reverse.explanationRu: Раскопки и древние находки — это archaeology. Anthropology изучает людей и культуры, а не копает землю.

fixIt.text: She has a master's degree in social [[anthropologist]] from a university in Scotland.
fixIt.explanationRu: Anthropologist — это человек, специалист. Название науки и специальности — anthropology.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: The research team spent a year doing [[anthropological]] fieldwork on a remote island.

words.definitionEn: to shock and upset someone very much because something is so bad
words.situation: Reacting to something so bad, cruel or shocking that you feel horrified and angry.

examples.text: Customers were [[appalled]] to discover that the company had sold their personal data.
I was [[appalled]] by the state of the hotel bathroom: mould on the walls and hair in the sink.
It [[appals]] me that some children still go to school hungry in such a rich country.

texts: Viewers were [[appalled]] by the way the contestants were treated.
Her parents were [[appalled]] when she left university to join a band.
Doctors are [[appalled]] at the long waiting times for surgery.

badCollocation.noteRu: Appalled — только о возмущении и ужасе. Если вид поразил красотой — amazed или stunned by the view.

collocationTask.prompt: I was ___ by the terrible conditions.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Прийти в ужас от чего-то — be appalled by. Appealed, applauded и appeased только похожи внешне: «обращаться», «аплодировать», «умиротворять».

nuance.text: We were [[appalled]] at how rudely the waiter spoke to the elderly couple.
nuance.explanationRu: Appal — вызывать ужас и возмущение чем-то недопустимым. Frighten — пугать, вызывать страх; грубость официанта возмущает, а не пугает.

reverse.text: The thunder [[frightened]] the children, so they hid under the table.
reverse.explanationRu: Испугать громом — frighten. Appal — возмутить чем-то плохим или жестоким, гром здесь ни при чём.

fixIt.text: Everyone was [[offended]] by the pictures of dead fish on the beach after the oil spill.
fixIt.explanationRu: Offended — «обиженный, задетый» лично. Ужас и возмущение от экологической катастрофы — appalled.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: The service at the restaurant was [[appalling]]: we waited an hour for cold soup.

reply.context: Your friend says: "My landlord hasn't fixed the heating for three months, and it's January."
options: Oh, I'm appalled! What a lovely surprise for you.
One is appalled; kindly lodge a formal grievance with the relevant authority forthwith.
Three months? I'm appalled. You should report him to the council.
reply.explanationRu: Appalled — «в ужасе, возмущён», о приятных сюрпризах так не говорят. Второй ответ звучит как канцелярское письмо, а не поддержка друга.

words.definitionEn: a set of equipment or tools used for a particular scientific or technical job
words.senseNote: Здесь — «аппаратура, оборудование»; «государственный аппарат» (the state apparatus) — отдельное книжное значение.
words.situation: Talking about the special equipment used in laboratories, by firefighters, divers or in gym and science lessons.

examples.text: Firefighters wearing breathing [[apparatus]] searched the smoke-filled building for survivors.
Students must return all laboratory [[apparatus]] to the cupboard after the experiment.
The gymnasts warmed up on the floor before moving to the rings and other [[apparatus]].

texts: The divers checked their breathing [[apparatus]] before going under the ice.
Early photographers carried heavy [[apparatus]] up mountains to take a single picture.
The lab bought new [[apparatus]] for measuring air pollution.

badCollocation.noteRu: Фотоаппарат — a camera, телефонный аппарат — a phone. Apparatus — научное или техническое оборудование, а не бытовое устройство.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Apparatus — неисчисляемое, поэтому «один прибор» — a piece of apparatus. Device, instrument и appliance исчисляемые: a device, an instrument.

nuance.text: The researchers built special [[apparatus]] to measure tiny changes in temperature.
nuance.explanationRu: Apparatus — научное или техническое оборудование для особых задач. Appliance — бытовой электроприбор (холодильник, чайник); в лаборатории им ничего не измеряют.

reverse.text: Turn off every electrical [[appliance]] before you go on holiday.
reverse.explanationRu: Бытовые электроприборы — appliances. Apparatus — неисчисляемое слово для научного или технического оборудования.

fixIt.text: The chemistry teacher set up the [[aggregate]] for the experiment on the front bench.
fixIt.explanationRu: Aggregate — «совокупность, общая сумма», а не «агрегат». Лабораторное оборудование — apparatus.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

words.definitionEn: attractive or interesting, so that you want to have or do it
words.senseNote: Здесь — «привлекательный, заманчивый»; appealing как форма глагола appeal (обжаловать, обращаться) — другое.
words.situation: Describing an idea, offer, place or design that attracts you and makes you want to try it.

examples.text: A four-day working week sounds [[appealing]], but it may not suit every business.
After a long winter, the idea of a week on a warm beach was very [[appealing]].
The designers made the packaging more [[appealing]] to younger buyers with bright colours and bold fonts.

texts: The job offer was [[appealing]], but the salary was too low.
Fresh herbs make any dish look more [[appealing]].
Living in the countryside has never been [[appealing]] to me.

badCollocation.noteRu: Привлекательный для кого-то — appealing to someone: The idea is appealing to me. Предлог for здесь звучит неестественно.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Приятный на вид — visually appealing (или attractive). Attracting — форма глагола, а tasty и lovely с visually не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Lower fees make the online course more [[appealing]] than the classroom one.
nuance.explanationRu: Appealing — «заманчивый»: такой, что хочется выбрать. Charming — «обаятельный, очаровательный» о людях и местах; низкая цена курс обаятельным не делает.

fixIt.text: The idea of moving abroad seems very [[attracting]] to many young graduates.
fixIt.explanationRu: Attracting — форма глагола, в роли прилагательного «привлекательный» не работает. Нужно appealing.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: The flat is small, but its location makes it very [[appealing]] to commuters.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Do you fancy a weekend hiking trip in the mountains next month?"
options: That sounds really appealing. I haven't had a proper break in ages.
Sounds appealing! I hate hiking and I'm terrified of heights.
Your proposal is deemed appealing and will be duly considered.
reply.explanationRu: Appealing — «заманчивый», так говорят о том, чего хочется. Во втором ответе слово противоречит остальному, а третий звучит как ответ комиссии, а не другу.

words.definitionEn: a strong wish or demand for a particular activity or experience
words.senseNote: Здесь — переносное «тяга, интерес, спрос» (an appetite for risk); буквальный аппетит к еде — базовое значение.
words.situation: Talking about how much people want something, such as risk, adventure, change, gossip or new products.

examples.text: Young investors often have a bigger [[appetite]] for risk than people close to retirement.
The public's [[appetite]] for celebrity gossip seems impossible to satisfy.
After two elections in one year, voters have little [[appetite]] for another campaign.

texts: Travelling as a teenager gave her an [[appetite]] for adventure.
There is a growing [[appetite]] for plant-based food in supermarkets.
The board showed no [[appetite]] for another expensive merger.

badCollocation.noteRu: Тяга к чему-то — appetite for something: an appetite for risk. Предлог to здесь — калька с русского «к».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Тяга к приключениям — an appetite for adventure. Appeal for — «призыв», apathy — «безразличие», а addiction требует предлога to.

nuance.text: Teenagers have a huge [[appetite]] for short, funny videos.
nuance.explanationRu: У людей есть appetite for something — тяга к чему-то. Appeal — привлекательность самой вещи: short videos have huge appeal for teenagers, а не наоборот.

reverse.text: The film's [[appeal]] lies in its gentle humour.
reverse.explanationRu: Привлекательность фильма — its appeal. Appetite бывает у людей (тяга к чему-то), а не у фильма.

fixIt.text: After the crash, investors lost their [[wish]] for risky technology shares.
fixIt.explanationRu: Wish — «пожелание, мечта», с «потерять интерес к акциям» не сочетается. О готовности рисковать говорят appetite for risk.

cefrEvidence.label: B1
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

reply.context: Your colleague asks: "Management wants to relaunch the app next month. Will the team be up for it?"
options: Sure, the team's appetite is fine. They all had a big lunch today.
Honestly, after the last chaotic launch, there's not much appetite for another rush job.
The team's appetite for said relaunch shall be ascertained in due course.
reply.explanationRu: Здесь appetite — «желание, готовность» что-то делать, а не аппетит к еде. Третий ответ звучит как бюрократический отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

words.definitionEn: to publicly praise a decision, effort or quality you approve of
words.senseNote: Здесь — переносное «одобрять, приветствовать» (applaud a decision); «аплодировать, хлопать» — базовое значение.
words.situation: Saying publicly that you strongly approve of someone's decision, courage or effort, without actually clapping.

examples.text: I [[applaud]] your decision to tell the client the truth, even though it cost us the contract.
Environmental groups [[applauded]] the city's plan to ban cars from the centre, calling it long overdue.
Teachers should be [[applauded]] for keeping schools running during the floods.

texts: We [[applaud]] the council for finally fixing the roads.
Critics were quick to [[applaud]] the director's brave choice of ending.
I [[applaud]] anyone who learns a new language after sixty.

badCollocation.noteRu: Applaud — переходный глагол без предлога: applaud the singer, applaud her decision. Applaud to — калька с «аплодировать кому».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Похвалить кого-то за смелость — applaud someone for their courage. Clap — буквально «хлопать», approve требует of, а welcome — «приветствовать» гостя или новость.

nuance.text: Human rights groups [[applauded]] the court's decision.
nuance.explanationRu: Applaud может значить «одобрить, похвалить» без всяких хлопков. Clap — только буквально хлопать в ладоши, clap a decision не говорят.

reverse.text: The children [[clapped]] along to the music.
reverse.explanationRu: Хлопать в такт музыке — clap along. Applaud — аплодировать выступлению или одобрять решение, в такт так не хлопают.

fixIt.text: We [[applause]] your courage in speaking out about the problem.
fixIt.explanationRu: Applause — существительное («аплодисменты»). Нужен глагол: we applaud your courage.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B1
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: The decision to cut ticket prices drew [[applause]] from fans and players alike.

reply.context: Your colleague says: "I've finally told the boss I won't answer work emails at weekends any more."
options: Great! I'll come and applaud you every Saturday while you answer them.
Your assertiveness is hereby applauded by the undersigned.
Good for you! I applaud you for standing up for yourself.
reply.explanationRu: Applaud someone for something — похвалить, одобрить поступок. Первый ответ противоречит ситуации, а второй звучит как официальная грамота, а не реплика коллеги.

words.definitionEn: a machine used in the home, such as a fridge or washing machine
words.situation: Talking about fridges, cookers, dishwashers, kettles and other electrical machines people use at home.

examples.text: Old kitchen [[appliances]] like fridges and freezers can use a surprising amount of electricity.
The shop sells washing machines, cookers and other household [[appliances]] at discount prices.
Never use an electrical [[appliance]] with a damaged cable, as it could start a fire.

texts: Energy-efficient [[appliances]] cost more but save money over time.
The flat comes fully furnished, with all [[appliances]] included.
Our electricity bill dropped after we replaced two old [[appliances]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Приложение для телефона — an app (или application). Appliance — бытовой прибор: холодильник, чайник, пылесос.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Кухонная техника — kitchen appliances. Mechanisms — «механизмы», aggregates — не «агрегаты», а apparatus — научное оборудование.

nuance.text: Large kitchen [[appliances]], like fridges and cookers, are usually delivered free of charge.
nuance.explanationRu: Appliance — бытовой прибор для домашней работы: холодильник, плита, стиральная машина. Device — любое устройство, чаще небольшое и электронное; большие кухонные машины так обычно не называют.

reverse.text: Please switch off all electronic [[devices]], including phones and tablets, during the exam.
reverse.explanationRu: Телефоны и планшеты — electronic devices. Appliances — бытовые приборы вроде холодильника, а не гаджеты.

fixIt.text: We bought all our kitchen [[technics]] from one shop to get a bigger discount.
fixIt.explanationRu: Technics — не «бытовая техника». Холодильники, плиты и чайники — kitchen appliances.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

words.definitionEn: relevant to or officially affecting a particular person, group or situation
words.situation: Saying whether a rule, law, fee or question is relevant to a particular person or case.

examples.text: If a question on the form is not [[applicable]] to you, simply write N/A.
The new dress code is [[applicable]] to all staff, including senior managers.
The findings of this small study may not be [[applicable]] to older patients.

texts: Delivery charges are [[applicable]] only to orders under thirty euros.
This discount is not [[applicable]] during the summer sale.
Her advice is [[applicable]] to almost any job interview.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Подходящий для работы» (о кандидате) — suitable for the job. Applicable — о правилах и законах: применимый, относящийся к кому-то.

collocationTask.explanationRu: В анкетах пишут delete (или tick) where applicable — «где применимо». Applicant — «кандидат», application — «заявление», applied — форма глагола.

nuance.text: The rules on overtime are not [[applicable]] to part-time staff.
nuance.explanationRu: Applicable to — «распространяется на кого-то» (о правилах, законах, тарифах). Suitable — «подходящий, годный» для цели или человека; о действии правил так не говорят.

reverse.text: This film is not [[suitable]] for young children.
reverse.explanationRu: «Не подходит для детей» — not suitable for children. Applicable говорит о том, на кого распространяется правило, а не о том, что кому подходит.

fixIt.text: The new safety rules are [[usable]] to all visitors, not just employees.
fixIt.explanationRu: Usable — «пригодный для использования» о вещах. Правила, которые распространяются на кого-то, — applicable to them.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: Critics questioned the [[applicability]] of the study to real classrooms.

rewrite.original: These rules do not concern people who work part-time.
rewrite.frame: These rules are not ____ part-time workers.
rewrite.explanationRu: Applicable to — «распространяется на, относится к».

words.definitionEn: to officially choose someone for a job or position of responsibility
words.situation: Talking about a company, government or committee officially giving someone a job, title or role.

examples.text: The board has [[appointed]] a new chief executive after months of searching.
She was [[appointed]] as the country's first female ambassador to Japan.
The school [[appoints]] two older students each year to represent pupils at staff meetings.

texts: The club [[appointed]] a former player as head coach.
A judge was [[appointed]] to lead the investigation.
She has just been [[appointed]] head of marketing.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Назначить встречу» — arrange или schedule a meeting. Appoint — назначать человека на должность.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ someone as head of the department
collocationTask.explanationRu: Назначить кого-то руководителем — appoint someone as head. Set, put и place значат «поставить» предмет; о должности так не говорят.

nuance.text: Judges in this country are [[appointed]] by the president, not chosen by voters.
nuance.explanationRu: Appoint — назначить: решение принимает руководитель или комиссия. Elect — выбрать голосованием; президент судей не «избирает», а назначает.

reverse.text: The town [[elected]] a new mayor with sixty per cent of the vote.
reverse.explanationRu: Если было голосование — elect. При назначении голосов и процентов нет, поэтому appointed здесь не подходит.

fixIt.text: The company has [[nominated]] a new finance director, who starts work in May.
fixIt.explanationRu: Nominate — выдвинуть кандидатом, а не назначить. Если человек уже получил должность и выходит на работу, нужно appointed.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B1
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: The [[appointment]] of a new head teacher was announced this morning.

reply.context: A friend asks: "I heard your department finally has a new boss?"
options: Yes, and we appointed a meeting with her for Tuesday at ten.
Yes, they've appointed someone from outside the company. She starts on Monday.
Indeed, an appointment has been effected with regard to the vacant managerial position.
reply.explanationRu: Appoint — назначить на должность. «Назначить встречу» — arrange a meeting, а не appoint. Третий ответ звучит как приказ отдела кадров, а не разговор с другом.

rewrite.original: They made her the new team leader last week.
rewrite.frame: She ____ the new team leader last week.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: she was appointed (as) team leader.

words.definitionEn: understanding and recognition of the real value, quality or importance of something
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «понимание ценности, умение ценить», а не базовое «благодарность».
words.situation: You recognise how good, valuable or serious something really is, often after learning more about it.

examples.text: A year of piano lessons gave me a much deeper [[appreciation]] of classical music.
The investors clearly had little [[appreciation]] of the risks, so the losses came as a shock.
Guided walks can really increase visitors' [[appreciation]] of the city's old buildings.

texts: Travel gave her a fresh [[appreciation]] of home.
The film shows little [[appreciation]] of how complex the war really was.
Wine tasting classes can sharpen your [[appreciation]] of good food.

badCollocation.noteRu: С appreciation не сочетается big: говорят a deep, real или great appreciation of music.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Понимание приходит постепенно, поэтому говорят develop (или gain) an appreciation. Make, do и take с этим существительным не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Living abroad gave her a deeper [[appreciation]] of her own culture.
nuance.explanationRu: Appreciation — понимание ценности чего-то, умение это ценить. Assessment — оценка, вывод проверяющего или эксперта; «глубокая оценка своей культуры» здесь не по смыслу.

reverse.text: The teacher's [[assessment]] of my essay was fair but quite harsh.
reverse.explanationRu: Оценку работы (балл, вывод проверяющего) называют assessment. Appreciation — не «оценка», а понимание ценности чего-то.

fixIt.text: Working in a hospital gave me a real [[estimation]] of what nurses do every day.
fixIt.explanationRu: Понимание и уважение к чужому труду — appreciation. Estimation — расчёт или приблизительная оценка, а не понимание ценности.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B1
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: The trip gave the students a real [[appreciation]] of how hard farmers work.

reply.context: A colleague says: "I used to find opera boring, but after that evening course I actually love it."
options: That makes sense — they probably gave you an appreciation for finishing the course.
That makes sense — knowing the background gives you a real appreciation of the music.
Indeed, one's appreciation of the operatic form is thereby greatly enhanced.
reply.explanationRu: Курс помог понять и полюбить оперу — это appreciation. В первом ответе слово понято как награда за курс, третий звучит как научная статья, а не реплика коллеге.

rewrite.original: Few voters really understand how serious the problem is.
rewrite.frame: Few voters have a real ____ how serious the problem is.
rewrite.explanationRu: Have an appreciation of something — ясно понимать, насколько это важно или серьёзно.

words.definitionEn: based on chance or personal whim rather than on reason or a clear system
words.situation: A decision or rule seems to be made without any good reason, often unfairly, just because someone chose it.

examples.text: The new dress code feels completely [[arbitrary]] — nobody can explain why jeans are banned but trainers aren't.
Human rights groups have condemned the [[arbitrary]] arrest of journalists without charge.
The pass mark of 60% is fairly [[arbitrary]]; it could just as easily be 55%.

texts: Some of the club's rules seem totally [[arbitrary]].
Choosing that date was [[arbitrary]]; any Friday would work.
Citizens must be protected from [[arbitrary]] decisions by officials.

badCollocation.noteRu: Случайная встреча — a chance meeting. Arbitrary — не «случайный» вообще, а «ничем не обоснованный»: an arbitrary rule, decision.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Решение без разумных причин — an arbitrary decision. Optional — необязательный, occasional — редкий, accidental — случайный, по ошибке.

nuance.text: The court ruled that his detention without trial had been [[arbitrary]] and unlawful.
nuance.explanationRu: Arbitrary — сделанный по чьему-то произволу, без законных оснований; это типичный юридический термин. Random — случайный, выбранный наугад, и к решению суда о задержании не подходит.

reverse.text: Winners will be chosen by [[random]] selection from all the entries.
reverse.explanationRu: Выбор наугад, как в лотерее, — random selection. Arbitrary selection означало бы выбор по чьей-то прихоти, то есть нечестный.

fixIt.text: Staff complain that bonuses are handed out in a completely [[accidental]] way.
fixIt.explanationRu: Премии раздают без понятных причин — это arbitrary. Accidental значит «случайный, произошедший по ошибке», как accidental damage.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: Critics attacked the [[arbitrariness]] of the new visa rules.

reply.context: Your friend complains: "My landlord says I can't have guests after 10 p.m., but he never explains why."
options: That sounds completely arbitrary — ask him to show you where it says that in the contract.
That sounds completely arbitrary — at least he explained his reasons so clearly.
Such a regulation would appear to be of an arbitrary nature, one must concede.
reply.explanationRu: Правило без объяснений — arbitrary, первый ответ точен. Во втором противоречие: если причины объяснены, правило не arbitrary. Третий слишком официальный для разговора с другом.

words.definitionEn: connected with the design, style and construction of buildings
words.situation: You talk about the style, design or structure of buildings, for example on a city tour.

examples.text: The old railway station is one of the city's finest [[architectural]] treasures.
The competition asks young designers to submit [[architectural]] drawings of a new library.
Critics say the new shopping centre has no [[architectural]] merit whatsoever.

texts: The castle is a true [[architectural]] gem.
Students spend five years on their [[architectural]] training.
The report praises the [[architectural]] quality of the new schools.

badCollocation.noteRu: Архитектурный факультет — the faculty (или school) of architecture. Architectural описывает здания и стиль: architectural style.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Наследие в виде зданий — architectural heritage. Structural — «несущий, конструкционный», constructive — «полезный», architect — существительное.

nuance.text: With its arches and painted ceilings, the palace is an [[architectural]] masterpiece.
nuance.explanationRu: Architectural — про стиль, красоту и замысел здания. Structural — про несущие конструкции и прочность, а арки и росписи хвалят не за прочность.

reverse.text: After the earthquake, engineers found serious [[structural]] damage in the bridge.
reverse.explanationRu: Повреждения несущих конструкций — structural damage. Architectural описывает стиль и дизайн, а не прочность моста.

fixIt.text: The museum won an award for the bold [[architecture]] design of its new wing.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед design нужно прилагательное: architectural design. Architecture — существительное, «архитектура».

wordFormation.text: The street is lined with houses of great [[architectural]] interest.

reply.context: On a city tour, a friend asks: "Why is everyone taking photos of that plain grey building?"
options: Apparently it's very architectural — they sell nice souvenirs inside.
Its architectural significance is considerable, as the scholarly literature attests.
Apparently it's an architectural landmark — the first building of its kind in the country.
reply.explanationRu: Architectural landmark — здание, важное для архитектуры. «Very architectural» из-за сувениров — бессмыслица, а второй ответ звучит как научная статья, а не реплика другу.

words.definitionEn: a collection of historical records or documents, or the place where they are kept
words.situation: Historians or journalists search through old letters, photos and official papers stored together in one place.

examples.text: She spent six months in the national [[archives]], reading old letters and official reports.
The newspaper has put its entire [[archive]] of articles since 1900 online.
Historians were thrilled when a lost letter by the composer turned up in a church [[archive]].

texts: The agency's photo [[archive]] is now online.
He found the original contract in the company [[archive]].
Our digital [[archive]] holds every issue since 1985.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Поднять архивы» — не raise, а go through или search the archives.

collocationTask.prompt: rare ___ footage of the city in the 1920s
collocationTask.explanationRu: Старые кадры из архива — archive (или archival) footage. Memory, record и history так с footage не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The film [[archive]] holds more than ten thousand silent movies.
nuance.explanationRu: Archive — целое собрание документов, фильмов или фото (или место, где оно хранится). Record — одна запись или документ о чём-то; тысячи фильмов в record не хранятся.

reverse.text: There is no [[record]] of his arrival in the city.
reverse.explanationRu: Запись или документ о событии — record. Archive — большое собрание таких документов, а не одна запись о приезде.

fixIt.text: The museum's photo [[fund]] contains over a million images from the 1920s.
fixIt.explanationRu: Русское «фонд» (собрание документов или фото) по-английски — archive или collection. Fund — это деньги.

wordFormation.text: The historian based her book on years of careful [[archival]] research.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How did you find out that your great-grandmother was an actress?"
options: I found her name in a theatre archive — there were even photos of her on stage.
I found it in my archive — I have a very good memory for family stories.
Consultation of the relevant archive yielded the pertinent information.
reply.explanationRu: Archive — собрание документов и фото, в нём и нашлось имя. Archive не значит «память», а третий ответ звучит как отчёт, а не разговор с другом.

words.definitionEn: an area of public life, such as politics, where people compete for power or influence
words.senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение («политическая арена», «поприще»), а не «крытый стадион».
words.situation: You describe politics, business or international relations as a place of competition and conflict.

examples.text: After twenty years as a doctor, she decided to enter the political [[arena]].
Small start-ups often struggle to survive in the global business [[arena]].
Social media has turned into a noisy [[arena]] where politicians fight for attention.

texts: She has been active in the political [[arena]] for decades.
The court case moved the debate into the legal [[arena]].
Few women competed in the business [[arena]] back then.

badCollocation.noteRu: По-русски «на арене», но по-английски — in the political arena, с предлогом in.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Начать карьеру в политике — enter the political arena. Area — «район, область», square — площадь, ground — земля; с political так не говорят.

nuance.text: After retiring from football, he moved into the political [[arena]] and ran for mayor.
nuance.explanationRu: Arena — поле борьбы и соперничества: the political arena. Area — «район» или «область знаний» (my area of research); о политике как о борьбе так не говорят.

reverse.text: Her main [[area]] of research is child psychology.
reverse.explanationRu: Область исследований — area of research. Arena — поле борьбы и соперничества, к науке в таком значении не подходит.

fixIt.text: Many actors have stepped into the political [[area]], with mixed results.
fixIt.explanationRu: Политика как поле борьбы — the political arena. Area — «район» или «область»; the political area звучит неестественно.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Why did that famous surgeon suddenly quit medicine?"
options: He's bought an arena for his hospital, so he's very busy now.
He wants to enter the political arena — he's running for mayor next year.
He hath resolved to enter the arena of public affairs, it is said.
reply.explanationRu: Enter the political arena — «выйти на политическую арену», пойти в политику. В первом ответе arena понято буквально как здание, третий звучит архаично.

words.definitionEn: used when giving an opinion that you believe can be supported with good reasons
words.situation: You give a strong opinion, often with a superlative, while admitting that other people might disagree.

examples.text: Penicillin was [[arguably]] the most important medical discovery of the twentieth century.
Her second novel is [[arguably]] her best, though some critics still prefer her first.
For a new manager, clear communication is [[arguably]] more important than technical skill.

texts: It is [[arguably]] the best pizza in town.
She was [[arguably]] the greatest tennis player of her era.
This is [[arguably]] the most important decision you'll ever make.

badCollocation.noteRu: Arguably не значит бытовое «может быть»: так говорят о мнении, которое можно обосновать (arguably the best). «Может, приду» — maybe I'll come.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ one of the greatest writers of all time
collocationTask.explanationRu: Arguably ставят перед превосходной степенью: arguably one of the greatest. Accordingly, respectively и consequently — связки «соответственно, следовательно».

nuance.text: It's [[arguably]] the best album of the decade, though some critics prefer her earlier work.
nuance.explanationRu: Arguably — «пожалуй, можно утверждать»: вы высказываете смелое мнение. Admittedly — «надо признать»: вы уступаете собеседнику. Здесь главное мнение, а не уступка.

reverse.text: [[Admittedly]], I haven't read the whole report, but the summary looks convincing.
reverse.explanationRu: Говорящий признаёт слабое место своей позиции — это admittedly. Arguably вводит смелое утверждение, а не признание.

fixIt.text: He is [[controversially]] the greatest goalkeeper the club has ever had.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Пожалуй, величайший» — arguably the greatest. Controversially значит «вызывая споры, скандально» и не смягчает оценку.

reply.context: In a book club chat, someone asks: "Which of her novels should I start with?"
options: Try the second one — it's arguably 300 pages long, so you'll finish it quickly.
Try the second one — it's arguably her best, and it's quite short.
One would arguably be best served by commencing with her second effort.
reply.explanationRu: Arguably смягчает оценку, которую можно обосновать: arguably her best. Число страниц — факт, о нём не спорят. Третий ответ слишком напыщенный для чата.

words.definitionEn: to give yourself or someone the knowledge, tools or information needed for a challenge
words.senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение «вооружить знаниями, фактами, инструментами», а не буквальное «вооружать оружием».
words.situation: Before a difficult meeting or task, you prepare by collecting the facts, skills or tools you will need.

examples.text: Before the salary talks, she [[armed]] herself with data on what competitors pay.
The course [[arms]] students with the practical skills that employers are looking for.
[[Arm]] yourself with a good map before you explore the old town.

texts: She arrived at the meeting [[armed]] with charts and graphs.
Tourists came [[armed]] with cameras and guidebooks.
Parents went to the school [[armed]] with a list of complaints.

badCollocation.noteRu: После arm нужен предлог with: arm yourself with the facts. Русский творительный падеж здесь передаётся через with, а не by.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Запастись терпением» — arm yourself with patience. Stock up on говорят о продуктах, а fill и load с терпением не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Before facing the board, she [[armed]] herself with every figure she could find.
nuance.explanationRu: Arm yourself with — подготовиться к трудной ситуации, «вооружиться» фактами или аргументами. Supply — поставлять товары и материалы; supply yourself with figures звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: A local farm [[supplies]] the restaurant with fresh vegetables.
reverse.explanationRu: Регулярно поставлять продукты — supply. Arm говорят, когда человека готовят к трудной задаче или борьбе, а не о поставках овощей.

fixIt.text: The queue at the visa office is long, so [[stock]] yourself with patience and a good book.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Запастись терпением» — arm yourself with patience. Stock так не употребляется: говорят stock up on food.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "I've got my salary review with the boss tomorrow. Any tips?"
options: Just arm your boss first and then ask him for a raise.
It would be prudent to arm oneself with pertinent performance metrics.
Arm yourself with numbers — list every project you delivered this year.
reply.explanationRu: Arm yourself with numbers — заранее запастись цифрами и фактами. «Arm your boss» звучит как «выдай начальнику оружие», а второй ответ слишком официальный для чата с коллегой.

rewrite.frame: Before the debate, he ____ all the relevant statistics.
rewrite.explanationRu: Arm yourself with something — заранее запастись фактами или инструментами.

words.definitionEn: a large and often impressive collection or range of different things
words.senseNote: Выбрано общее значение «большое разнообразие, множество», а не «массив» в программировании.
words.situation: You describe a large, varied and often impressive range of objects, choices or people.

examples.text: The market sells a dazzling [[array]] of spices from all over the world.
The job requires a wide [[array]] of skills, from coding to public speaking.
The hotel offers an impressive [[array]] of activities, from yoga to wine tasting.

texts: The shop stocks a huge [[array]] of teas.
Doctors now have a wide [[array]] of treatments available.
She faced a bewildering [[array]] of choices after graduation.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Лесной массив» — a large area of forest или woodland. Array — множество разных предметов или вариантов: an array of dishes.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Широкий выбор» — a wide array (или range) of options. Number сочетается с large, а не wide; amount — с неисчисляемыми; row — ряд в пространстве.

nuance.text: The report identifies a whole [[array]] of problems with the new payment system.
nuance.explanationRu: «Целый ряд проблем» — a whole array (или range) of problems. Row — ряд в пространстве: ряд кресел, домов; о множестве проблем так не говорят.

reverse.text: We sat in the front [[row]] and could see every expression on the actors' faces.
reverse.explanationRu: Ряд кресел в зале — row. Array — разнообразное множество чего-то, а не линия мест в театре.

fixIt.text: The new phone comes with a wide [[spectre]] of useful features.
fixIt.explanationRu: Русское «спектр» здесь — array или range. Spectre — ложный друг, по-английски это «призрак».

reply.context: A friend asks: "How was the food festival on Saturday?"
options: Brilliant — I had an array of soup and then went home.
Brilliant — there was a huge array of street food from about thirty countries.
It was agreeable; an array of comestibles was presented for consumption.
reply.explanationRu: Array — большое разнообразие: a huge array of street food. «An array of soup» бессмысленно — это одна тарелка, а третий ответ звучит слишком книжно для разговора с другом.

words.definitionEn: to express an idea or feeling clearly and effectively in words
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «чётко выразить мысль словами»; есть ещё прилагательное articulate — «красноречивый».
words.situation: You manage to put complicated thoughts or feelings into clear words so that other people understand them.

examples.text: Many patients find it hard to [[articulate]] exactly what is wrong with them.
In her email, she [[articulated]] the team's concerns calmly and clearly.
A good essay [[articulates]] a clear argument and supports it with evidence.

texts: Children often can't [[articulate]] why they feel upset.
The new CEO needs to [[articulate]] a clear vision for the company.
It took me years to [[articulate]] what I really wanted from life.

badCollocation.noteRu: Articulate — переходный глагол: articulate your concerns, без about.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ a clear vision for the future
collocationTask.explanationRu: Чётко изложить видение — articulate a vision. Pronounce — произносить звуки, а tell и speak с vision не сочетаются.

nuance.text: She finally found the words to [[articulate]] her fears about the move.
nuance.explanationRu: Articulate — выразить мысль или чувство словами. Pronounce — произносить звуки и слова; «произнести свои страхи» по-английски не говорят. Русское «артикулировать» — ложный друг.

fixIt.text: At the meeting, she clearly [[sounded]] what most of us had been thinking for weeks.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Озвучить мысль» — articulate или voice, но не sound. Sound значит «звучать»: it sounds great.

wordFormation.text: The report praised the clear [[articulation]] of the company's goals.

reply.context: After a failed project, your manager asks: "So what do you think went wrong?"
options: It's hard to articulate in one sentence, but mostly we never agreed on the goals.
I articulated the budget twice, but the numbers still didn't add up.
Allow me to articulate, if I may, a most comprehensive account of our failings.
reply.explanationRu: Articulate — чётко сформулировать мысль. Бюджет не articulate, его пересчитывают (check, recalculate). Третий ответ звучит напыщенно для рабочего разговора.

rewrite.original: It's hard for me to put my feelings into words.
rewrite.frame: I find it hard to ____ my feelings.
rewrite.explanationRu: Articulate your feelings — выразить чувства словами.

words.definitionEn: the soft grey powder left after something burns, or thrown into the air by a volcano
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «пепел, зола» (в том числе вулканический пепел и rise from the ashes), а не «ясень».
words.situation: A fire has gone out or a volcano has erupted, and everything is covered in soft grey powder.

examples.text: Hundreds of flights were cancelled because of a huge cloud of volcanic [[ash]].
Many gardeners mix wood [[ash]] into the soil as a natural fertiliser.
When the fire finally went out, all that was left of the barn was a heap of [[ash]].

texts: The old mill was reduced to [[ashes]] in a single night.
The city rose from the [[ashes]] after the great fire.
She searched through the [[ashes]] for her grandmother's ring.

badCollocation.noteRu: Пепел — неисчисляемое существительное: some ash, a pile of ash. An ash — это ясень.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение — reduced to ashes, «обращён в пепел». Made, brought и cut в нём не используются.

nuance.text: Grandad tapped his pipe, and a little [[ash]] fell onto the carpet.
nuance.explanationRu: Ash — то, что остаётся после горения: пепел из трубки, зола в печи. Dust — пыль, которая сама оседает на полках; из трубки она не сыплется.

reverse.text: The books on the top shelf were covered in [[dust]].
reverse.explanationRu: Пыль на полках — dust. Ash — пепел или зола после горения; книги покрываются им только после пожара.

fixIt.text: Wait until the stove is cold, then shovel the [[dust]] into a metal bucket.
fixIt.explanationRu: То, что остаётся в печи после горения, — ash (зола). Dust — это пыль, огонь её не оставляет.

words.definitionEn: a strong wish to achieve something important in your life or career
words.situation: You talk about what someone hopes to achieve in their career or life, often something ambitious.

examples.text: The survey asked teenagers about their career [[aspirations]] and their fears about the future.
The new mayor promised to listen to the [[aspirations]] of young families who can't afford homes.
Her lifelong [[aspiration]] to run her own restaurant finally came true last year.

texts: Many graduates have no clear [[aspirations]] yet.
The novel explores the hopes and [[aspirations]] of immigrant families.
Parents often project their own [[aspirations]] onto their children.

badCollocation.noteRu: Aspiration — серьёзная жизненная цель (карьера, образование). О желании что-то купить говорят want: I want to buy new shoes.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Осуществить стремления — fulfil (или realise, achieve) your aspirations. Execute и perform — про задачи и действия, complete — про работу.

nuance.text: Her [[aspiration]] is to open a small bakery by the sea.

reverse.text: The painter found [[inspiration]] in the landscapes of her childhood.
reverse.explanationRu: Источник творческих идей — inspiration. Aspiration — цель, к которой стремишься; её не «находят в пейзажах».

fixIt.text: She has serious [[pretensions]] to become a professional singer.
fixIt.explanationRu: Стремление стать кем-то — aspirations. Pretensions — ложный друг русского «претензии»: это «притязания, претенциозность».

wordFormation.text: The charity works to raise the [[aspirations]] of children from poor families.

reply.context: At a job interview, you're asked: "Where do you see yourself in five years?"
options: My aspiration is that I was born in a small town near Kazan.
Aspirations? No idea, mate — whatever happens, happens.
My aspiration is to lead a small team and help shape the product.
reply.explanationRu: Aspiration — цель на будущее, поэтому подходит третий ответ. Место рождения — факт из прошлого, а не стремление. Второй ответ слишком фамильярный для собеседования.

words.definitionEn: to have a strong wish to achieve something or to become a particular kind of person
words.situation: Someone has a big goal, such as becoming a writer or a manager, and hopes to reach it one day.

examples.text: Like many young actors, she [[aspired]] to work in film rather than theatre.
Anyone who [[aspires]] to a management role needs strong people skills.
The programme helps students from poor areas [[aspire]] to careers in medicine and law.

texts: Most young musicians [[aspire]] to play in a major orchestra.
We [[aspire]] to be the most trusted bank in the region.
What kind of life do you [[aspire]] to?

badCollocation.noteRu: Aspire не бывает переходным: aspire to a promotion, aspire to become a manager.

collocationTask.prompt: She aspires ___ a career in law
collocationTask.explanationRu: Aspire всегда с предлогом to: aspire to a career, aspire to become. At, on и in с этим глаголом не используются.

nuance.text: She [[aspires]] to a senior position within the next five years.
nuance.explanationRu: Русское «претендовать на должность» — aspire to (или apply for) a position. Pretend — ложный друг: это «притворяться».

reverse.text: He [[pretended]] to be asleep when his boss called.
reverse.explanationRu: Притворяться — pretend. Aspire значит «стремиться к цели», к притворству оно отношения не имеет.

fixIt.text: As a teenager, he [[inspired]] to play for the national team.
fixIt.explanationRu: Стремиться к цели — aspire to do something. Inspire — «вдохновлять кого-то»: The coach inspired him to play.

wordFormation.text: The workshop is open to all [[aspiring]] writers, whatever their age.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Do you want to be a manager one day?"
options: Not really — I aspire to be great at what I do, not to manage people.
Not really — I aspire my manager every day, and that's enough.
Negative. Managerial positions are not that to which I aspire.
reply.explanationRu: Aspire to be — «стремиться быть». Во втором ответе aspire употреблено как «восхищаться» (это admire) и без to. Третий звучит канцелярски для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: She has always dreamed of becoming a judge.
rewrite.frame: She has always ____ a judge.
rewrite.explanationRu: Aspire to do something — стремиться, мечтать стать кем-то.

words.definitionEn: the crime of attacking someone physically, or an act of this kind
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «нападение на человека (преступление)»; ещё бывает военный штурм и переносное «атака на права».
words.situation: Someone is accused in court of hitting or physically attacking another person.

examples.text: He was arrested and charged with [[assault]] after a fight outside a bar.
Hospitals report that [[assaults]] on nurses and doctors have risen sharply this year.
The footballer was cleared of [[assault]] after the video showed he never touched the fan.

texts: She was the victim of a serious [[assault]] last year.
Two men will stand trial for [[assault]] next month.
Any [[assault]] on staff will be reported to the police.

badCollocation.noteRu: С assault не говорят do: нужно commit an assault, а в суде — be charged with assault.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Обвинение в нападении — be charged with assault. Attack, aggression и violence в юридическом языке так не используются: это не названия статей.

nuance.text: The man was found guilty of [[assault]] and given six months in prison.
nuance.explanationRu: Assault — юридическое название преступления «нападение, побои». Attack — нападение вообще, но не статья закона: guilty of assault, а не of attack.

reverse.text: My uncle had a heart [[attack]] while he was playing tennis.
reverse.explanationRu: Сердечный приступ — heart attack. Assault — нападение одного человека на другого, к болезни не относится.

fixIt.text: The driver was charged with [[aggression]] after he punched a cyclist.
fixIt.explanationRu: Статья за нападение — assault: be charged with assault. Aggression — агрессивное поведение, а не название преступления.

words.definitionEn: to bring people or things together in one place, or to gather as a group
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «собирать людей или сведения вместе», а не «собирать мебель или механизм из деталей».
words.situation: A leader brings experts together into a team, or a crowd of people gathers in one place.

examples.text: The director [[assembled]] a team of top engineers to design the new bridge.
By nine o'clock, a small crowd had [[assembled]] outside the court.
It took the journalist two years to [[assemble]] enough evidence to publish the story.

texts: Journalists [[assembled]] outside the hotel, waiting for news.
She [[assembled]] a small but loyal team.
The museum has [[assembled]] a remarkable collection of Roman coins.

badCollocation.noteRu: Деньги на подарок collect (или raise), а не assemble. Assemble — собирать людей, команду, доказательства.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Собрать команду — assemble (или put together) a team. Collect — собирать вещи или забирать кого-то, compose — сочинять, accumulate — накапливать.

nuance.text: The coach [[assembled]] a strong squad of young players for the tournament.
nuance.explanationRu: Собрать команду из людей — assemble. Collect — собирать предметы (марки, мусор) или забирать кого-то (collect the kids from school); collected a squad звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: Could you [[collect]] the kids from school today?
reverse.explanationRu: Забрать детей из школы — collect. Assemble — собрать людей в группу или команду, а не забрать кого-то.

fixIt.text: The government has [[composed]] a team of experts to investigate the crash.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Собрать команду» — assemble a team. Compose значит «сочинять» (музыку, текст), а «составить команду» так не переводится.

wordFormation.text: The constitution guarantees freedom of speech and freedom of [[assembly]].

reply.context: Your manager says: "We need to launch the app in three months. Can we do it?"
options: Only if we assemble the deadline and make it a bit longer.
Only if we assemble a small team right now and give them full control.
Affirmative; a team shall be assembled forthwith, in accordance with your wishes.
reply.explanationRu: Assemble a team — собрать команду, это естественный ответ. Срок (deadline) не assemble, его переносят (extend). Третий вариант звучит как старинный приказ.

rewrite.original: About two hundred people gathered outside the town hall.
rewrite.frame: A crowd of about two hundred people ____ outside the town hall.
rewrite.explanationRu: Assemble — собраться вместе (о толпе, группе людей).

words.definitionEn: a group of people elected to make laws or decisions for a country or region
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «выборный орган власти» (National Assembly), а не школьная линейка или сборка деталей.
words.situation: Elected representatives meet regularly to debate and vote on new laws for their country or region.

examples.text: The regional [[assembly]] voted to ban single-use plastic bags from next year.
In history class we learned how the country's first elected [[assembly]] was formed.
My cousin works as an adviser to a member of the national [[assembly]].

texts: The [[assembly]] meets every Tuesday and Thursday.
She was elected to the [[assembly]] at just twenty-six.
The bill was rejected by the [[assembly]] after a long debate.

badCollocation.noteRu: Собрание акционеров — a shareholders' meeting или annual general meeting. Assembly — выборный законодательный орган.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Избраться в региональный парламент — be elected to the regional assembly. Meeting — встреча, gathering — сборище, audience — зрители; туда не избирают.

nuance.text: The national [[assembly]] passed the new law by 210 votes to 95.
nuance.explanationRu: Assembly — выборный орган, который принимает законы. Meeting — любое собрание или встреча, например совещание на работе; законы на нём не принимают.

reverse.text: We have a team [[meeting]] every Monday at ten.
reverse.explanationRu: Рабочее совещание — meeting. Assembly в этом значении — парламент или выборный орган, а не встреча коллег.

fixIt.text: Members of the regional [[gathering]] voted against the new tax.
fixIt.explanationRu: Выборный орган, который голосует за налоги, — assembly. Gathering — просто сборище людей, встреча.

words.definitionEn: to state firmly and confidently that something is true
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «твёрдо утверждать»; assert yourself («проявить твёрдость») — отдельное значение.
words.situation: Someone states strongly that a claim is true, often in a debate, an article or in court.

examples.text: The company [[asserts]] that its products are completely safe, despite several complaints.
In her essay, she [[asserted]] that social media had made politics more extreme.
Throughout the trial, he has continued to [[assert]] his innocence.

texts: The author [[asserted]] that the painting was a fake.
Several witnesses [[asserted]] that the driver had been speeding.
The report [[asserted]] that prices would fall, but they rose.

badCollocation.noteRu: Утвердить бюджет — approve the budget. Assert — «утверждать, заявлять», что что-то правда; путаница из-за русского «утверждать/утвердить».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Настаивать на своей невиновности — assert (или maintain) your innocence. Confess и admit — про признание вины, approve — «одобрять».

nuance.text: In court, the witness [[asserted]] that she had never met the defendant.
nuance.explanationRu: Assert — твёрдо заявлять, что что-то правда. Assure — заверять кого-то, чтобы успокоить, и требует дополнения: assure the court that. Без него assured здесь неверно.

reverse.text: The pilot [[assured]] the passengers that there was no danger.
reverse.explanationRu: Успокоить людей обещанием — assure somebody that. Assert не принимает дополнение-человека: asserted the passengers — ошибка.

fixIt.text: He [[approves]] that he was at home all evening, but nobody believes him.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Он утверждает, что» — he asserts (или claims) that. Approve — «одобрять, утверждать документ»: approve a plan.

wordFormation.text: Since becoming a manager, she has learned to be more [[assertive]] in meetings.

reply.context: In a seminar, a classmate asks: "The article says remote workers are less productive. Is that true?"
options: The author asserted the article to the editor last week.
I would hereby assert that the aforementioned claim lacks empirical grounding.
The author asserts it, but she doesn't give any real data to support it.
reply.explanationRu: Assert — твёрдо заявлять, что что-то правда, часто без доказательств. Статью редактору не assert, а send или submit. Второй ответ слишком напыщенный для разговора с однокурсником.

rewrite.original: The minister said firmly that the figures were correct.
rewrite.frame: The minister ____ the figures were correct.
rewrite.explanationRu: Assert that — твёрдо заявить, что что-то правда.

words.definitionEn: a statement that something is true, made firmly and often without proof
words.situation: Someone states firmly that something is true, and others question whether there is any evidence for it.

examples.text: Several scientists have challenged her [[assertion]] that the drug has no side effects.
The manager's [[assertion]] that the project was on schedule turned out to be false.
There is no evidence for the widely repeated [[assertion]] that we only use 10% of our brains.

texts: Her [[assertion]] was not supported by any facts.
I strongly disagree with the [[assertion]] that money brings happiness.
The judge rejected the lawyer's [[assertion]] as pure speculation.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Сделать утверждение» — make an assertion, а не do.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Подтвердить утверждение доказательствами — support (или back up) an assertion. Carry, keep и lift с assertion не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Critics dismissed the author's [[assertion]] that grammar no longer matters.
nuance.explanationRu: Assertion — заявление, что что-то правда, часто спорное. Assurance — заверение, которое дают кому-то, чтобы успокоить; мнение автора о грамматике не assurance.

reverse.text: The bank gave us its [[assurance]] that our savings were safe.
reverse.explanationRu: Заверение, данное клиентам, чтобы их успокоить, — assurance. Assertion — просто твёрдое заявление, его не «дают» кому-то.

fixIt.text: Few experts accept the minister's [[approval]] that the economy has fully recovered.
fixIt.explanationRu: Русское «утверждение» в смысле «заявление» — assertion. Approval — «одобрение, утверждение документа»: approval of the budget.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: His [[assertion]] that he had never been to Paris was quickly proved false.

words.definitionEn: a promise or firm statement that something is true or will happen, meant to remove doubt
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «заверение, гарантия»; в британском английском assurance бывает и «страхование жизни», а self-assurance — «уверенность в себе».
words.situation: Someone promises you that something will definitely happen, so that you stop worrying about it.

examples.text: The minister gave an [[assurance]] that no jobs would be lost at the factory.
Despite repeated [[assurances]] from the landlord, the heating still doesn't work.
Before signing, the client wanted some [[assurance]] that the software would be delivered on time.

texts: Can you give me your [[assurance]] that this won't happen again?
Voters want [[assurance]] that their personal data is safe.
He received a written [[assurance]] from the bank.

badCollocation.noteRu: Заверение дают и получают: give an assurance, receive (или get) an assurance. Калька «взять обещание» — take — здесь не работает.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ an assurance that no jobs will be lost
collocationTask.explanationRu: Дать заверение — give (или provide) an assurance. Say и tell не сочетаются с этим существительным, а do здесь вообще не подходит.

nuance.text: Despite [[assurances]] from the airline that the plane was safe, many passengers refused to board.
nuance.explanationRu: Assurance — заверение, обещание, что всё будет хорошо. Insurance — страховка, договор со страховой компанией; ею пассажиров не успокаивают перед посадкой.

reverse.text: Don't forget to buy travel [[insurance]] before your trip.
reverse.explanationRu: Туристическая страховка — travel insurance. Assurance как «страхование» встречается только в британском life assurance, в остальных случаях это «заверение».

fixIt.text: The manager gave us his personal [[warranty]] that the problem would be fixed by Friday.
fixIt.explanationRu: Личное обещание, чтобы нас успокоить, — assurance. Warranty — гарантия на товар (two-year warranty), а не слово человека.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B2
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: We have received an [[assurance]] from the builders that the work will be finished in May.

reply.context: An email from a client asks: "Can you guarantee the order will arrive before the conference?"
options: Yeah, no worries, total assurance, mate!
I can give you my personal assurance that it will be delivered by Tuesday.
Yes — we've bought assurance for the conference, so everything is covered.
reply.explanationRu: Give someone your assurance — дать слово, заверить. В третьем ответе assurance спутано со страховкой (insurance), а первый слишком фамильярный для письма клиенту.

words.definitionEn: protection that a country gives to people who have fled danger in their own country
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «политическое убежище»; устаревшее значение «психиатрическая лечебница» здесь не рассматривается.
words.situation: A person who faces persecution at home asks another country for legal protection and permission to stay.

examples.text: After receiving threats at home, the journalist applied for [[asylum]] in Canada.
Thousands of people who fled the war are still waiting to be granted [[asylum]].
During the war, the famous painter was given [[asylum]] by a neutral country.

texts: He was granted [[asylum]] after a long legal battle.
The family is seeking [[asylum]] in Germany.
Her [[asylum]] application was finally approved in March.

badCollocation.text: give [[asylum]] to a homeless man for the night
badCollocation.noteRu: Приютить бездомного — give someone shelter. Asylum — политическое убежище, которое даёт государство.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Политическое убежище — political asylum. Shelter — приют или укрытие, housing — жильё, hiding — «укрытие, прятки».

nuance.text: The opposition leader applied for [[asylum]] at the embassy.
nuance.explanationRu: Asylum — официальный статус, о нём подают заявление: apply for asylum. Refuge — укрытие от опасности, его «находят» (take refuge), а не оформляют.

reverse.text: During the storm, the hikers took [[refuge]] in a mountain hut.
reverse.explanationRu: Укрыться от бури — take refuge. Asylum — юридическая защита, которую даёт государство, а не укрытие в хижине.

fixIt.text: The court ruled that she should be given political [[shelter]] in the UK.
fixIt.explanationRu: Политическое убежище — political asylum. Shelter — укрытие или приют (a homeless shelter), а не правовой статус.
