corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

reply.context: A friend asks about a film you've just seen: "So what's it about?"
options: A young doctor who flees her country and applies for asylum in Norway.
A young doctor who takes asylum from work to travel around Norway.
It concerns a medical practitioner's petition for asylum; most edifying.
reply.explanationRu: Apply for asylum — просить политического убежища. «Asylum from work» — ошибка: отпуск — leave или a break. Третий ответ звучит чопорно для разговора с другом.

words.definitionEn: creating a strong mood or feeling, often mysterious, romantic or exciting
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «создающий особое настроение» (о музыке, фильме, месте), а не научное «атмосферный» (atmospheric pressure).
words.situation: You describe music, a film, a photo or a place that creates a special, often mysterious or romantic feeling.

examples.text: The film's [[atmospheric]] soundtrack, all low strings and distant bells, makes every scene feel haunted.
We had dinner in a tiny, [[atmospheric]] restaurant lit only by candles.
Her [[atmospheric]] black-and-white photos of foggy streets have won several prizes.

texts: The old castle is wonderfully [[atmospheric]] at night.
Their new album is dark, slow and very [[atmospheric]].
The novel opens with an [[atmospheric]] description of a winter village.

badCollocation.noteRu: Atmospheric описывает места, музыку, фильмы и свет, но не людей. О человеке скажут charismatic или charming.

collocationTask.prompt: an ___ little café lit by candles
collocationTask.explanationRu: Место с особым настроением — an atmospheric café. Atmosphere — существительное, emotional описывает чувства людей, athletic — «спортивный».

nuance.text: The ruined abbey, wrapped in fog, looked wonderfully [[atmospheric]].
nuance.explanationRu: Atmospheric — место, музыка или фильм создают настроение. Emotional — о людях и их чувствах или о трогательном событии; руины не бывают emotional.

reverse.text: The wedding speech was so [[emotional]] that half the guests were crying.
reverse.explanationRu: Трогательная речь, от которой плачут, — emotional. Atmospheric описывает обстановку и настроение места, а не силу чувств.

fixIt.text: The director uses fog and silence to create a very [[atmosphere]] opening scene.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед существительным scene нужно прилагательное: a very atmospheric scene. Atmosphere — существительное.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: Candles and old jazz records give the bar a wonderfully [[atmospheric]] feel.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Where should we go for our anniversary dinner?"
options: There's a very atmospheric place near the airport — the air there is really fresh.
I propose an establishment of considerable atmospheric merit.
There's an atmospheric little place by the river — candles, brick walls, live piano.
reply.explanationRu: Atmospheric — место с особым настроением: свечи, кирпич, живая музыка. Свежий воздух тут ни при чём, а второй ответ звучит слишком чопорно для разговора с другом.

words.definitionEn: a situation or area in which groups compete or argue fiercely
words.senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение — сфера острой борьбы или споров; буквальное «поле боя» проще.
words.situation: You describe a topic, market or place where rival groups compete or argue with great intensity.

examples.text: School history lessons have become a political [[battlefield]], with each new government rewriting the textbooks.
Every evening our living room turns into a [[battlefield]] over who gets the TV remote.
Their divorce quickly became a legal [[battlefield]], with each side accusing the other of hiding money.

texts: For years, the kitchen was a [[battlefield]] between my two teenage sons.
The smartphone market is a crowded [[battlefield]] where only the biggest players survive.
Online comment sections often turn into a [[battlefield]] of insults and angry opinions.

badCollocation.noteRu: Побеждают в битве — win the battle. Battlefield — это место или сфера борьбы, его не «выигрывают».

collocationTask.prompt: the meeting quickly ___ into a battlefield
collocationTask.explanationRu: Превратиться во что-то — turn into: the meeting turned into a battlefield. Become into — ошибка, made into требует дополнения, went into значит «вошёл».

nuance.text: Every family dinner turns into a [[battlefield]] once my uncles start shouting about football.
nuance.explanationRu: Battlefield — открытая борьба и споры. Minefield — ситуация со скрытыми опасностями, где легко ошибиться. Когда все уже кричат и спорят, это battlefield.

reverse.text: Employment law is a [[minefield]]: one tiny mistake can cost a company thousands.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о скрытом риске ошибиться, а не об открытой борьбе, поэтому minefield.

fixIt.text: Three rival coffee shops opening at once turned our quiet street into a [[battle]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Улица — это место, поэтому она превращается в battlefield (поле битвы), а не в battle (саму битву).

reply.context: A colleague messages you: "How did the budget meeting go?"
options: Great, it was a real battlefield — everyone agreed with everything.
Honestly, it was a battlefield. Every department fought for every penny.
It constituted a battlefield of considerable magnitude, one might say.
reply.explanationRu: Battlefield — место острой борьбы, а не согласия. Третий вариант слишком книжный для сообщения коллеге.

words.definitionEn: a narrow line of light or energy coming from a torch, lamp or laser
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «луч (фонаря, фар, лазера)»; не путайте с beam — «балка, брус».
words.situation: A torch, car headlight, lighthouse or laser sends out a narrow line of light.

examples.text: When the lights went down, a single [[beam]] lit up the singer in the centre of the stage.
The alarm goes off as soon as anyone breaks the infrared [[beam]] across the doorway.
Every ten seconds, the lighthouse sent a bright [[beam]] sweeping across the dark sea.

texts: The surgeon used a laser [[beam]] to correct the patient's short sight.
The fox froze in the [[beam]] of our torch, then vanished into the bushes.
On empty country roads at night, it's safe to drive on full [[beam]].

badCollocation.noteRu: «Луч надежды» — a ray of hope. Beam — физический луч от фонаря, фар, маяка или лазера.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Дальний свет фар — full beam (в американском варианте — high beams). Ray, shine и glow в этом выражении не используются.

nuance.text: The security guard swept the [[beam]] of his torch across the empty car park.
nuance.explanationRu: Beam — направленный луч от фонаря, фар, маяка или лазера. Ray — солнечный луч или излучение (UV rays), а также a ray of hope. У фонаря — beam.

reverse.text: Sunscreen protects your skin from the sun's harmful [[rays]].
reverse.explanationRu: Об излучении солнца говорят rays: UV rays, the sun's rays. Beams — лучи от фонаря, фар или лазера.

fixIt.text: At last the lost hikers saw the [[ray]] of a searchlight moving across the hillside.
fixIt.explanationRu: Луч прожектора, фонаря или фар — beam. Ray — о солнечных лучах и в выражении a ray of hope.

cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

reply.context: You're a passenger in a car at night. The driver says: "I can hardly see the road. There are no street lights here."
options: Why not put the headlights on full beam? There's nobody coming.
Just hold on to a beam of hope. We'll get there eventually.
It would be advisable to activate the vehicle's maximum beam function forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: Дальний свет — full beam. «Beam of hope» — ошибка (нужно ray of hope), а третий вариант звучит как инструкция, а не как слова пассажира.

words.definitionEn: a thing or situation of a particular kind, especially a difficult or powerful one
words.senseNote: Здесь — разговорное «штука, вещь (особого рода)», как в a different beast; значение «зверь, животное» проще.
words.situation: You compare two activities or systems and stress that one is much harder or quite unlike the other.

examples.text: Managing people is a completely different [[beast]] from writing good code.
His new motorbike is a powerful [[beast]] that can reach 100 km/h in three seconds.
Live television is an unpredictable [[beast]]: anything can go wrong at any moment.

texts: Running a marathon is a very different [[beast]] from jogging round the park.
Late nights before a launch are simply the nature of the [[beast]] in advertising.
Our old car was a noisy [[beast]], but it never once broke down.

badCollocation.noteRu: Устойчивое выражение — the nature of the beast («такова специфика»). Character в нём не используется.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Совсем другое дело» — a different beast altogether (или entirely). At all бывает только в отрицаниях и вопросах, а fully и absolutely так не ставят.

nuance.text: If you work in retail, weekend shifts are just the nature of the [[beast]].
nuance.explanationRu: The nature of the beast («такова специфика») — неизменное выражение, animal в нём не используется, хотя a different animal (амер.) и a different beast — синонимы.

reverse.text: My brother is a real party [[animal]]: he's out every weekend.
reverse.explanationRu: Party animal — устойчивое выражение о любителе вечеринок; party beast так не говорят.

fixIt.text: Writing a novel is a completely different [[case]] from writing short stories.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Совсем другое дело» — a completely different beast (разг.) или matter. Case — это «случай», в таком значении не используется.

reply.context: A friend who has just started managing a team messages you: "Leading people is so much harder than doing the actual work!"
options: Your team must be a real beast. Do they bite?
Totally different beast, right? It gets easier with time.
Indeed, managerial duties constitute a separate beast entirely.
reply.explanationRu: A different beast — «совсем другое дело», разговорное выражение. В первом ответе beast понят буквально как зверь, третий слишком официален для чата.

words.definitionEn: used after 'on' to mean acting for someone or as their representative
words.senseNote: Употребляется только в выражениях on behalf of someone и on someone's behalf.
words.situation: You speak, sign or act for another person or an organization, as their official representative.

examples.text: I'm writing on [[behalf]] of my manager, who is away until Monday.
The actor was ill, so his daughter accepted the award on his [[behalf]].
Volunteers collected money on [[behalf]] of a local children's hospital.

texts: The lawyer spoke on her [[behalf]] because she was too upset to talk.
On [[behalf]] of the whole team, thank you for your hard work this year.
Parents often have to make decisions on [[behalf]] of very young children.

badCollocation.noteRu: «От имени» — только on behalf of. Предлог from здесь — калька с русского «от».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Правильно только on behalf of («от имени»). From — калька с «от», in behalf of — устаревший американский вариант, by здесь невозможно.

nuance.text: Thank you for talking to the landlord on my [[behalf]] while I was away.
nuance.explanationRu: On my behalf — от моего имени, вместо меня. On my part — «с моей стороны», то есть то, что сделал я сам: a mistake on my part.

reverse.text: Sorry, that was a mistake on my [[part]]: I sent you the wrong file.
reverse.explanationRu: Ошибку совершил я сам, значит on my part («с моей стороны»). On my behalf — когда кто-то действует за меня.

fixIt.text: I'm writing on [[the part]] of all the tenants to complain about the broken heating.
fixIt.explanationRu: «От имени» жильцов — on behalf of. On the part of значит «со стороны» и указывает, кто совершил действие.

reply.context: Your manager calls: "I'm stuck in traffic. Can you start the client meeting without me?"
options: Sure. I'll welcome them on my behalf and tell them you're late.
No problem. Your behalf shall be duly represented forthwith.
Of course. I'll welcome them on your behalf and explain you're running late.
reply.explanationRu: Вы действуете за начальника, поэтому on your behalf. On my behalf — «от моего имени», а второй вариант звучит странно и слишком официально.

rewrite.original: My colleague spoke for me at the meeting because I was ill.
rewrite.frame: My colleague spoke ____ at the meeting because I was ill.
rewrite.explanationRu: Говорить за кого-то, от его имени — speak on someone's behalf.

words.definitionEn: loved very much and deeply valued by a person or by many people
words.situation: You describe a person, place or thing that someone, or a whole community, cares about deeply.

examples.text: The whole village came to the funeral of the [[beloved]] teacher who had taught three generations of local children.
The café has been a [[beloved]] part of the neighbourhood since 1952, and regulars are furious about its closure.
The finale killed off the show's most [[beloved]] character, and fans still haven't forgiven the writers.

texts: He took his [[beloved]] old guitar with him to every gig.
The park is [[beloved]] by joggers, dog walkers and families alike.
After thirty years abroad, she finally returned to her [[beloved]] Scotland.

badCollocation.noteRu: О любимом цвете, блюде или фильме говорят favourite. Beloved — глубоко любимый человек, место или вещь, звучит торжественно.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Beloved by — «любимый кем-то». Lovely — милый, lovable — обаятельный, loving — любящий; с by в этом смысле они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The singer is still [[beloved]] by fans who first heard her songs in the 1980s.
nuance.explanationRu: Beloved — тот, кого любят: beloved by fans. Loving — тот, кто любит сам: a loving mother. «Loving by fans» — ошибка.

reverse.text: She gave her son a [[loving]] hug before he got on the train.
reverse.explanationRu: Объятие выражает любовь, поэтому loving hug. Beloved описывает того, кого любят, а не действие.

fixIt.text: The old cinema, [[loving]] by students for its cheap tickets, is closing down next month.
fixIt.explanationRu: Кинотеатр любят студенты, значит он beloved by students. Loving — «любящий», так описывают того, кто любит сам.

reply.context: A friend messages: "They're closing the old bookshop on the corner!"
options: Oh no! The owner was always so beloved to customers. He gave everyone discounts.
Oh no, not that place! It's beloved by the whole neighbourhood.
Alas! My beloved emporium of literature shall be no more.
reply.explanationRu: Beloved by — «любимый кем-то», так и надо. В первом ответе beloved ошибочно значит «добрый к людям», а третий звучит как пародия на старинный роман.

rewrite.original: Millions of readers love her detective novels.
rewrite.frame: Her detective novels are ____ millions of readers.
rewrite.explanationRu: Beloved by + те, кто любит: beloved by millions of readers.

words.definitionEn: a standard or reference point used for measuring or judging quality or performance
words.situation: You compare results or products with an accepted standard to see how good they really are.

examples.text: Many schools use national exam results as a [[benchmark]] for measuring their own performance.
In independent tests, the new laptop scored well above the industry [[benchmark]] for battery life.
Her marathon time of 2 hours 20 minutes became the [[benchmark]] that every young runner aimed for.

texts: Last year's sales figures will serve as a [[benchmark]] for the new team.
This novel remains the [[benchmark]] against which all crime fiction is judged.
Investors compare their returns with a [[benchmark]] such as the national stock index.

collocations: the [[benchmark]] against which something is judged

badCollocation.noteRu: Планку или эталон устанавливают глаголом set: set a benchmark. Put с benchmark не сочетается.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Установить новый эталон — set a benchmark (как set a record или set a standard). Put, do и install с benchmark не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Her study became the [[benchmark]] against which all later research was measured.
nuance.explanationRu: Benchmark — эталон, с которым сравнивают и по которому измеряют. Landmark — ориентир на местности или поворотное событие (a landmark decision); им ничего не измеряют.

reverse.text: The court's [[landmark]] ruling changed the law on privacy.
reverse.explanationRu: Решение стало историческим, поворотным, поэтому landmark. Benchmark — только эталон для сравнения.

fixIt.text: We use last year's figures as a [[sample]] to measure how much we have improved.
fixIt.explanationRu: Эталон для сравнения — benchmark. Sample — «образец, проба» (a blood sample, a free sample), им прогресс не измеряют.

wordFormation.text: Regular [[benchmarking]] against competitors helps the firm spot its weaknesses early.

reply.context: In a meeting, your manager asks: "How will we know if the new training programme is actually working?"
options: We could put a benchmark in the training room so people have somewhere to sit.
Let's use last year's customer scores as a benchmark and compare the results every month.
Yeah, we could, like, do a benchmark thing or whatever.
reply.explanationRu: Benchmark — эталон для сравнения, это и нужно. Первый ответ путает его со скамейкой (bench), а третий звучит небрежно для совещания.

words.definitionEn: not suitable for someone because it is too low for their status or character
words.senseNote: Здесь — «ниже достоинства» (it's beneath you); значение «под, внизу» — базовое.
words.situation: Someone refuses a task or behaviour because they think it is too low for their status or character.

examples.text: He thinks making coffee for visitors is [[beneath]] him, even though he's the newest intern.
Answering those rude comments would be [[beneath]] you, so just ignore them.
The senator said that responding to personal insults was [[beneath]] the dignity of her office.

texts: Cheating to win a board game against children is [[beneath]] you.
She considered a small part in a TV advert [[beneath]] her and turned it down.
Such cheap personal attacks are [[beneath]] a serious journalist.

collocations: feel that a job is [[beneath]] you

badCollocation.noteRu: С уровнями, оценками и цифрами используют below: below average, below zero. Beneath в переносном смысле — «ниже достоинства».

collocationTask.prompt: Lying about something so small is ___ you.
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Ниже твоего достоинства» — beneath you. Under и underneath — только о физическом положении, а lower than you — калька с русского.

nuance.text: Spreading gossip about a colleague is [[beneath]] you, and you know it.
nuance.explanationRu: Beneath someone — «ниже чьего-то достоинства». Below — про уровни, числа и положение: below zero, below average; в значении «недостойно» звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: Last night the temperature dropped to ten degrees [[below]] zero.
reverse.explanationRu: О температуре и числах говорят below: below zero. Beneath так не используется.

fixIt.text: Replying to anonymous insults online is [[under]] your dignity.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Ниже достоинства» — beneath your dignity. Under — «под» в прямом смысле, с dignity не сочетается.

reply.context: A colleague complains: "The manager asked me to help sort the post today. I have a master's degree!"
options: Come on, no job is beneath you when the team is short-staffed.
Oh, then sorting post is beneath you, so you'll love it!
One observes that sorting post is situated beneath your qualifications.
reply.explanationRu: Beneath you — «ниже твоего достоинства»: никакая работа не зазорна. Во втором ответе смысл перепутан, третий звучит неестественно книжно.

rewrite.original: She thought that cleaning the office was not good enough for someone like her.
rewrite.frame: She thought that cleaning the office was ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Beneath someone — «ниже чьего-то достоинства».

words.definitionEn: a person or group that gains an advantage as a result of something
words.situation: A new law, trend or event helps a particular group, which ends up better off than before.

examples.text: Small farmers will be the main [[beneficiaries]] of the new trade agreement, which cuts taxes on their exports.
Children from low-income families were the biggest [[beneficiaries]] of the free school meals scheme.
Delivery companies were among the clearest [[beneficiaries]] of the lockdowns, as online orders doubled.

texts: The local economy was the main [[beneficiary]] of the music festival.
Every pupil in the school is a [[beneficiary]] of the new reading programme.
In the end, the only real [[beneficiary]] of the price war was the customer.

badCollocation.noteRu: После beneficiary нужен предлог of: the beneficiary of the reform. From сочетается с глаголом benefit: benefit from.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Главные выгодоприобретатели — the main (biggest, chief) beneficiaries. Large, strong и general с beneficiaries не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Ironically, the main [[beneficiary]] of the train strike was a small bike shop near the station.
nuance.explanationRu: Beneficiary — тот, кто выиграл от ситуации. Recipient — получатель чего-то конкретного (письма, награды, органа); от забастовки ничего не «получают».

reverse.text: At nineteen, she was the youngest [[recipient]] of the award.
reverse.explanationRu: Награду получают, поэтому recipient. Beneficiary — тот, кому ситуация принесла выгоду, а не получатель премии.

fixIt.text: Tourists will be the main [[benefactors]] of the new airport, as flights will get cheaper.
fixIt.explanationRu: Тот, кто получает выгоду, — beneficiary. Benefactor — наоборот, благотворитель, который даёт деньги.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

reply.context: A friend asks: "So who actually gains from the new four-day week at your company?"
options: Our CEO is the main beneficiary. She's the one paying for all of it.
The beneficiary aspect is super beneficiary for all of us, basically.
Honestly, the biggest beneficiaries are parents with young kids.
reply.explanationRu: Beneficiaries — те, кто выигрывает, например родители. Тот, кто платит, не beneficiary, а второй ответ бессмысленно повторяет слово.

rewrite.original: The new policy helps first-time buyers more than anyone else.
rewrite.frame: First-time buyers are ____ of the new policy.
rewrite.explanationRu: Главные выгодоприобретатели — the main (biggest) beneficiaries.

words.definitionEn: not harmful or dangerous, especially of a growth in the body that is not cancer
words.senseNote: Здесь — «безвредный, доброкачественный» (медицина, экология, IT); значение «добрый, мягкий» встречается реже.
words.situation: A doctor tells a patient that a lump is not cancer, or scientists say a substance causes no harm.

examples.text: Luckily, the tests showed that the lump on her neck was [[benign]].
The detergent is sold as eco-friendly because it contains only [[benign]] ingredients.
The antivirus flagged the file, but it turned out to be completely [[benign]].

texts: Most moles on the skin are [[benign]] and need no treatment at all.
Scientists believe the chemical is [[benign]] at such low doses.
Security software sometimes blocks perfectly [[benign]] programs by mistake.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Доброкачественный товар» — a high-quality product. Benign значит «не опасный» (об опухоли, веществе), а не «качественный».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Доброкачественная опухоль — a benign tumour. Kind, good и gentle — калька с «добро-», в медицине так не говорят.

nuance.text: Doctors removed the growth, and tests later confirmed it was [[benign]].
nuance.explanationRu: Benign — безвредный, доброкачественный (об опухоли, веществе). Benevolent — доброжелательный, щедрый; так говорят о людях, а не об опухолях.

fixIt.text: The scan showed that the tumour was [[good-quality]], so she didn't need chemotherapy.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Доброкачественная опухоль» — benign tumour. Good-quality значит «высокого качества» и говорится о товарах.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

reply.context: Your friend texts: "Just got my test results. The doctor says the lump is nothing to worry about."
options: Oh no, it's benign? I'm so sorry. When does the treatment start?
Excellent. The benignity of your lump is hereby noted.
What a relief! So it's benign? That's the best news all week.
reply.explanationRu: Benign — «доброкачественная, не опасная», это хорошая новость. В первом ответе смысл перепутан, второй звучит как официальный протокол.

words.definitionEn: to show a feeling or fact that someone wants to hide, without meaning to
words.senseNote: Здесь — «невольно выдавать» (чувства, мысли); основное значение «предавать» проще.
words.situation: Someone tries to look calm, but their voice, face or hands show what they really feel.

examples.text: She answered every question calmly, but her shaking hands [[betrayed]] her nerves.
He claimed to be a local, but his accent [[betrayed]] his foreign origins.
Although she said she loved the gift, her face [[betrayed]] a hint of disappointment.

texts: His trembling voice [[betrayed]] how nervous he really was.
Not a single muscle in her face [[betrayed]] her surprise.
A slight hesitation [[betrayed]] his doubts about the plan.

badCollocation.noteRu: Благодарность выражают сознательно — express gratitude. Betray — невольно выдать то, что хочешь скрыть.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Голос её выдал» — her voice betrayed her (или gave her away). Showed, issued и told без дополнения так не употребляются.

nuance.text: He tried to act confident, but his voice [[betrayed]] him.
nuance.explanationRu: Betray someone — невольно выдать человека, его истинные чувства: his voice betrayed him. Reveal требует, что именно раскрыто (revealed his fear), и часто делается намеренно.

reverse.text: At the press conference, the company [[revealed]] its plans for a new factory.
reverse.explanationRu: Планы объявили намеренно, поэтому revealed. Betray — выдать невольно или раскрыть чужой секрет.

fixIt.text: She smiled and said she was fine, but her red eyes [[discovered]] that she had been crying.
fixIt.explanationRu: Невольно выдать чувство или факт — betray. Discover значит «обнаружить, найти» что-то новое, а не показать то, что скрываешь.

reply.context: After a job interview, your friend says: "I tried so hard to look calm, but I'm not sure it worked."
options: Why? Did you betray your calm face on purpose?
Why, did your voice betray you? Honestly, everyone gets nervous.
Did your countenance betray any trepidation whatsoever?
reply.explanationRu: Your voice betrayed you — голос невольно выдал волнение. Betray не бывает «нарочно», а третий вариант слишком книжный для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: Her face showed how disappointed she was, although she tried to hide it.
rewrite.frame: Her face ____ her disappointment, although she tried to hide it.
rewrite.explanationRu: Betray — невольно выдать чувство, которое пытаешься скрыть.

words.definitionEn: to make someone legally or morally obliged to follow an agreement or rule
words.senseNote: Здесь — «обязывать» (договором, правилами, обещанием); значение «связывать верёвкой» проще.
words.situation: A contract, law or promise means that people must do certain things and cannot simply change their minds.

examples.text: All employees are [[bound]] by a strict confidentiality agreement, even after they leave the company.
The treaty [[binds]] member states to cut their emissions by half before 2040.
Once you sign the tenancy agreement, you are [[bound]] to pay rent for the full twelve months.

texts: Doctors are [[bound]] by a duty to keep patients' information private.
As a member of the club, you are [[bound]] by its rules.
Neither country felt [[bound]] by the old agreement any longer.

badCollocation.noteRu: Обязан соблюдать договор — be bound by a contract. С with так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Юридически обязан соблюдать договор» — be legally bound by it. Tied, connected и linked — калька со «связан», в этом значении не используются.

nuance.text: Both sides are [[bound]] by the terms of the agreement.
nuance.explanationRu: Be bound by — связан условиями, правилами: bound by the terms. Oblige требует продолжения to + глагол: obliged to follow the terms; «obliged by the terms» без него звучит неестественно.

fixIt.text: Once you sign, you are [[connected]] by every clause in the contract, so read it carefully.
fixIt.explanationRu: Обязательства по договору — be bound by. Connected значит «соединён, связан» физически или логически, но не обязательством.

cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

wordFormation.text: The agreement is legally [[binding]], so neither side can simply walk away from it.

reply.context: A friend says: "I want to quit my gym, but they say I have to pay for another six months."
options: That's annoying, but if you signed a contract, you're probably bound by it.
Just bind the contract with some string and throw it in the bin.
One is, regrettably, contractually bound in perpetuity, I fear.
reply.explanationRu: Bound by a contract — «обязан соблюдать договор». Во втором ответе bind понят буквально (связать верёвкой), третий звучит нелепо официально.

rewrite.original: The contract says that both companies must keep the price the same for three years.
rewrite.frame: Under the contract, both companies ____ keep the price the same for three years.
rewrite.explanationRu: Be bound to do something — быть обязанным что-то делать по договору.

words.definitionEn: an account of a person's life written by someone else
words.situation: A writer researches someone's life and tells the whole story of it in a book.

examples.text: Her new [[biography]] of the composer draws on hundreds of letters that have never been published.
For the history project, each student had to research and write a short [[biography]] of a famous scientist.
The singer's lawyers are trying to stop an unauthorised [[biography]] from being published.

texts: I'm reading a [[biography]] of the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
The actor's official [[biography]] leaves out his two failed marriages.
Writing a good [[biography]] takes years of research in archives and libraries.

badCollocation.noteRu: Биографический фильм — a biopic или a biographical film. Biography — обычно книга.

collocationTask.prompt: an ___ biography, approved by the family
collocationTask.explanationRu: Биография, одобренная героем или его семьёй, — an authorised biography. Allowed, admitted и enabled так не используются.

nuance.text: The [[biography]] runs to 900 pages and took its author twelve years to write.
nuance.explanationRu: Biography — книга о жизни человека. Biopic — художественный фильм о реальном человеке; у фильма нет страниц.

reverse.text: The [[biopic]] won its lead actor several major awards.
reverse.explanationRu: Главный актёр бывает у фильма, поэтому biopic. Biography — книга.

fixIt.text: The historian spent ten years on her [[autobiography]] of the explorer, based on his letters and diaries.
fixIt.explanationRu: Историк пишет о жизни другого человека, значит это biography. Autobiography человек пишет о себе сам.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

wordFormation.text: Her [[biographer]] spent ten years tracking down old friends and former colleagues.

reply.context: A friend asks: "What are you reading at the moment?"
options: My biography! I'm writing it myself, all about my own life.
An elegant tome of biographical erudition, should you wish to know.
A biography of a jazz pianist. The author interviewed over a hundred people who knew him.
reply.explanationRu: Biography — книга о чьей-то жизни, написанная другим человеком. О своей жизни пишут autobiography или memoir, а второй ответ звучит напыщенно.

rewrite.original: A former journalist wrote the story of the singer's life.
rewrite.frame: A former journalist wrote ____ of the singer.
rewrite.explanationRu: История жизни человека, написанная другим, — a biography of someone.

words.definitionEn: a senior Christian priest who is in charge of the churches in a large area
words.senseNote: Здесь — «епископ»; в шахматах bishop — «слон».
words.situation: You talk about the senior church leader who is responsible for all the churches in a region.

examples.text: The [[bishop]] will lead a special service in the cathedral to mark the town's 900th anniversary.
In the Middle Ages, a [[bishop]] often had as much power as a local lord.
Only a [[bishop]] can ordain new priests in the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

texts: The new [[bishop]] was welcomed by crowds outside the cathedral.
She wrote to the [[bishop]] to complain about the closure of the village church.
The [[bishop]] visits every parish in his diocese at least once a year.

badCollocation.noteRu: У небольшого прихода (parish) — priest или vicar. Bishop управляет целой епархией (diocese).

collocationTask.explanationRu: Территория, которой управляет епископ, — diocese (епархия). Parish — небольшой приход со своим священником, а district и county — светские округа.

nuance.text: The [[bishop]] is responsible for more than two hundred churches across the region.
nuance.explanationRu: Bishop — епископ, руководит всеми церквями и священниками епархии. Priest — священник одного прихода; двести церквей ему не подчиняются.

reverse.text: Every Sunday, the village [[priest]] greets his parishioners at the church door.
reverse.explanationRu: У деревенского прихода свой священник — priest. Епископ отвечает за целую епархию, а не за одну деревню.

fixIt.text: As head of the diocese, the [[priest]] has authority over every parish in the region.
fixIt.explanationRu: Глава епархии, которому подчиняются все приходы, — bishop. Priest служит в одном приходе.

words.definitionEn: very strange, unusual and difficult to explain
words.situation: Something happens, or someone behaves, in a way so strange that it is almost impossible to explain.

examples.text: In a [[bizarre]] twist, the stolen painting was returned by post with a note saying sorry.
My manager has a [[bizarre]] habit of wearing sunglasses during video calls.
The festival is famous for its [[bizarre]] events, including a race in which runners chase a wheel of cheese downhill.

texts: It's [[bizarre]] that nobody noticed the mistake for three whole years.
He told us a [[bizarre]] story about a parrot that could order pizza.
The film's ending was so [[bizarre]] that half the audience laughed.

badCollocation.noteRu: Непривычные заморские фрукты — exotic fruits. Bizarre — «очень странный, нелепый», это не комплимент.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Bizarre уже значит «очень странный», поэтому его усиливают словами absolutely, utterly, truly. Strongly, much и a lot так с прилагательными не сочетаются.

nuance.text: By a [[bizarre]] coincidence, my new boss turned out to be my old neighbour's twin brother.
nuance.explanationRu: Bizarre — о странных событиях, ситуациях и поступках. Eccentric — о человеке с чудаковатым характером: an eccentric professor. Совпадение не бывает eccentric.

fixIt.text: The police called the robbery [[exotic]]: the thieves took nothing but forty left shoes.
fixIt.explanationRu: Очень странное, необъяснимое событие — bizarre. Exotic значит «экзотический, из далёких стран».

reply.explanationRu: Bizarre — «очень странный», и это не похвала. Во втором ответе его путают с «элегантный», третий звучит вычурно для разговора с коллегой.

words.definitionEn: one of the flat wide parts that spin round on a fan, propeller or turbine
words.senseNote: Здесь — «лопасть» (вентилятора, винта, турбины); значение «лезвие» более базовое.
words.situation: You talk about the parts of a fan, helicopter or wind turbine that spin round very fast.

examples.text: Each of the turbine's three [[blades]] is almost as long as a football pitch.
The ceiling fan was so dusty that grey fluff flew off its [[blades]] when I switched it on.
The helicopter's rotor [[blades]] were still spinning when the paramedics jumped out.

texts: Engineers inspect the turbine [[blades]] for cracks after every storm.
Keep children's fingers away from the [[blades]] of the electric fan.
The boat's propeller [[blades]] were tangled in an old fishing net.

badCollocation.noteRu: Бытовой вентилятор — fan. Ventilator по-английски — аппарат ИВЛ, лопастей у него нет.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Лопасти ветряка или вертолёта — blades. Wings — крылья самолёта или птицы, paddles — вёсла, shovels — лопаты.

nuance.text: The wind turbine's huge [[blades]] turn slowly even in a light breeze.
nuance.explanationRu: У вентилятора, винта и ветряка — blades (лопасти), они вращаются. Wings — крылья самолёта или птицы, которые не вращаются.

reverse.text: Ice on the plane's [[wings]] delayed our flight by two hours.
reverse.explanationRu: Крылья самолёта — wings. Blades — лопасти, которые вращаются.

fixIt.text: The desk fan makes a horrible noise because one of its plastic [[wings]] is cracked.
fixIt.explanationRu: Лопасти вентилятора — blades. Wings — крылья самолёта или птицы.

words.definitionEn: a sudden strong rush of air, wind or heat
words.senseNote: Здесь — «порыв, поток (воздуха, жара)»; значение «взрыв» и разговорное have a blast — другие.
words.situation: You open a door, window or oven and suddenly feel very cold or very hot air hit you.

examples.text: Forecasters warn that an Arctic [[blast]] will bring heavy snow and freezing temperatures this weekend.
Stepping off the plane in Dubai, we were hit by a [[blast]] of hot, dry air.
Can you close the window? There's an icy [[blast]] coming in and I'm freezing.

texts: A [[blast]] of cold air hit us as soon as we left the station.
The hand dryer gives out a powerful [[blast]] of warm air.
Skiers were caught by a sudden [[blast]] of wind near the top of the mountain.

badCollocation.noteRu: Долгая жара — a heatwave. Blast of heat — короткий горячий поток воздуха, например из духовки.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Порыв ветра — a blast (или gust) of wind. Flash — вспышка света, splash — всплеск воды, crash — грохот.

nuance.text: When I opened the oven door, a [[blast]] of heat made me step back.
nuance.explanationRu: Blast — мощный поток воздуха, жара или холода, в том числе из духовки или кондиционера. Gust — короткий порыв ветра на улице; из духовки gust не бывает.

reverse.text: The weather service recorded [[gusts]] of up to 90 kilometres per hour.
reverse.explanationRu: Порывы ветра, скорость которых измеряют, — gusts; это метеорологический термин.

fixIt.text: Every time the front door opens, a [[blow]] of icy wind sweeps through the whole shop.
fixIt.explanationRu: Порыв ледяного ветра — a blast of icy wind. Blow — «удар», калька с «удар ветра» здесь не работает.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Why are you wearing a scarf in the office?"
options: The atmospheric blast in my vicinity is, alas, suboptimal.
My desk is right under the air conditioner, so I get an icy blast all day.
I had a blast of a cold yesterday, so I'm keeping warm.
reply.explanationRu: An icy blast — поток ледяного воздуха из кондиционера. «Blast of a cold» — бессмыслица (простуда — a cold), а первый ответ звучит нелепо официально.

words.definitionEn: to lose money, customers or staff steadily over a period of time
words.senseNote: Здесь — переносное «терять (деньги, клиентов)»; прямое значение «кровоточить» проще.
words.situation: A business keeps losing money or customers month after month and cannot stop the losses.

examples.text: The airline has been [[bleeding]] cash since fuel prices doubled, and it may not survive the winter.
The club has been [[bleeding]] fans after three seasons of dull, defensive football.
Since the supermarket opened next door, our little shop has been [[bleeding]] customers.

texts: The newspaper is [[bleeding]] readers to free news websites.
Experts say the company is [[bleeding]] money and needs a buyer fast.
Our department is [[bleeding]] talent because salaries are so low.

badCollocation.noteRu: Время не bleed: говорят lose time или waste time. Bleed — о деньгах, клиентах, сотрудниках, которые постепенно уходят.

collocationTask.prompt: The business has been ___ money for months.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Постоянно терять деньги — bleed money: the business has been bleeding money. Flow, drip и spill так с деньгами не употребляются.

nuance.text: The magazine has been [[bleeding]] subscribers since it doubled its price.
nuance.explanationRu: Bleed subscribers/money — сам теряешь подписчиков или деньги. Drain — «истощать» что-то: the project drained our budget; у drain подлежащее — причина потерь.

reverse.text: Months of legal fees have [[drained]] our savings.
reverse.explanationRu: Судебные расходы «истощили» сбережения — это drain. Bleed говорят о том, кто сам теряет деньги или людей.

fixIt.text: Since the price rise, the gym has been [[falling]] members every single month.
fixIt.explanationRu: Fall — непереходный глагол, «fall members» сказать нельзя. Постоянно терять клиентов — bleed members.

reply.context: A friend who works in retail says: "Online sales are fine, but our high-street shops lose money every single month."
options: So the shops are bleeding cash? Maybe it's time to close a few.
Oh no, is anyone hurt? Bleeding can be really dangerous.
The shops are, one presumes, fiscally exsanguinating.
reply.explanationRu: Bleed cash — постоянно терять деньги. Во втором ответе bleed понят буквально как кровотечение, третий звучит нелепо книжно.

rewrite.original: The company has been losing a lot of money for two years.
rewrite.frame: The company has been ____ for two years.
rewrite.explanationRu: Постоянно терять деньги — bleed money или bleed cash.

words.definitionEn: a mixture of different things or qualities that combine well together
words.senseNote: Акцент на удачном сочетании качеств, стилей или вкусов, а не на простой «смеси».
words.situation: Two or more styles, flavours or qualities are combined so well that they feel like one thing.

examples.text: The band's sound is an unusual [[blend]] of Irish folk and electronic dance music.
Our house [[blend]] combines beans from three different countries.
Good teachers need a [[blend]] of patience, humour and firmness.

texts: The hotel offers a perfect [[blend]] of old-world charm and modern comfort.
Her novel is a clever [[blend]] of comedy and tragedy.
The perfume is a delicate [[blend]] of rose, vanilla and sandalwood.

collocations: a clever [[blend]] of old and new

badCollocation.noteRu: Blend — удачное, гармоничное сочетание. О неприятностях говорят a combination или a mix of problems.

collocationTask.prompt: a perfect ___ of old and new
collocationTask.explanationRu: Удачное сочетание — a perfect blend of. Blender и mixer — кухонные приборы, stir — «помешивание».

nuance.text: This tea is a special [[blend]] created by our master tea taster.
nuance.explanationRu: О чае, кофе, духах и стилях говорят blend — продуманное, удачное сочетание. Mixture — любая смесь, часто химическая или кулинарная.

reverse.text: Pour the [[mixture]] into a baking tin and bake for forty minutes.
reverse.explanationRu: Тесто или смесь для выпечки — mixture. Blend — удачное сочетание вкусов или стилей, а не масса в миске.

fixIt.text: The film is a clever [[mixing]] of documentary and fiction.
fixIt.explanationRu: Удачное сочетание жанров — a blend (или mix). Mixing — процесс смешивания, а не результат.

wordFormation.text: Put the bananas, milk and honey in the [[blender]] and mix until smooth.

reply.context: A friend asks about a restaurant you went to: "So, was the food Italian or Japanese?"
options: It was a blend. The chef put everything in a blend and pressed a button.
A blend, I would posit, of a most harmonious disposition.
Neither, really. It was a clever blend of both, like sushi with pesto.
reply.explanationRu: Blend — удачное сочетание, здесь двух кухонь. Кухонный прибор — blender, а второй ответ звучит вычурно.

words.definitionEn: to give someone or somewhere a special talent, quality or advantage (usually passive)
words.senseNote: Здесь — be blessed with («посчастливилось иметь»); религиозное «благословлять» и «Bless you!» проще.
words.situation: You say that a person or place is lucky to have a natural gift, good health or beautiful surroundings.

examples.text: The region is [[blessed]] with mild winters, fertile soil and miles of sandy beaches.
She was [[blessed]] with a beautiful voice, but she never took singing lessons.
We were [[blessed]] with perfect sunshine for the whole wedding weekend.

texts: Our team is [[blessed]] with some very talented young players.
The town is [[blessed]] with a beautiful old harbour.
He's [[blessed]] with an amazing memory for faces.

badCollocation.noteRu: Blessed with — только о хорошем. О неприятностях говорят cursed with или plagued by.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Be blessed with — «посчастливилось иметь»: blessed with good health. By, of и in здесь не используются.

nuance.text: We were [[blessed]] with warm sunshine for the whole trip.
nuance.explanationRu: Gifted — «одарённый», о таланте человека. Be blessed with — о любой удаче: погоде, здоровье, природе. С погодой gifted не сочетается.

reverse.text: She's a [[gifted]] pianist who started performing at the age of six.
reverse.explanationRu: Талантливый пианист — gifted pianist. A blessed pianist звучит как «святой, благословенный», а не «талантливый».

fixIt.text: The north of the country is [[rewarded]] with beautiful lakes and ancient forests.
fixIt.explanationRu: Природные богатства не заслужены как награда: посчастливилось иметь — be blessed with. Rewarded значит «вознаграждён» за что-то.

reply.context: A friend shows you photos of her new flat by the sea: "Look at the view from the kitchen!"
options: Wow, you're really blessed with that view. I'm so jealous!
Oh no, you're blessed with that view? I hope you can move soon.
Verily, thy dwelling is blessed with a most splendid vista.
reply.explanationRu: Blessed with — «посчастливилось иметь», это о хорошем. Во втором ответе смысл перевёрнут, третий звучит как старинная проза.

rewrite.original: The country is lucky to have a lot of natural resources.
rewrite.frame: The country ____ a lot of natural resources.
rewrite.explanationRu: Be blessed with — «посчастливилось иметь».

words.definitionEn: approval or support for a plan, especially from someone with authority
words.senseNote: Здесь — «одобрение, согласие» (with someone's blessing); значения «благо» и религиозное «благословение» проще.
words.situation: Before going ahead with a plan, you need the approval of your boss, your parents or the authorities.

examples.text: The merger can only go ahead with the [[blessing]] of the competition authorities.
They got married in secret, without their parents' [[blessing]].
The head teacher gave her [[blessing]] to the students' plan for a vegetable garden.

texts: The city council has given its [[blessing]] to the new cycling routes.
He asked her father for his [[blessing]] before proposing.
The project went ahead with the full [[blessing]] of senior management.

badCollocation.noteRu: Одобрение получают: get или receive someone's blessing. С take так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Одобрить план — give your blessing to it. Put, make и say с blessing не сочетаются.

nuance.text: They were both adults and could marry anyway, but they still wanted her parents' [[blessing]].
nuance.explanationRu: Permission — формальное разрешение, взрослым оно не нужно. Blessing — одобрение и поддержка, которые хочется получить от близких.

reverse.text: You need written [[permission]] from the landlord to keep a pet in the flat.
reverse.explanationRu: Письменное разрешение по правилам — permission. Blessing — моральное одобрение, его не оформляют письменно.

fixIt.text: After months of debate, the mayor finally gave her [[good]] to the new skate park.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Дать добро» — give your blessing (или approval, the go-ahead). Дословное give your good — ошибка.

wordFormation.text: The plan to open a café in the library now has the [[blessing]] of the local council.

reply.context: Your colleague says: "I'd love to work from home on Fridays, but I'm not sure the boss will agree."
options: Ask her for a blessing. Maybe she'll pray for your Fridays.
Petition the superior for her formal blessing forthwith.
Just ask her! She gave her blessing to my flexible hours last month.
reply.explanationRu: Give your blessing — «дать добро», одобрить. В первом ответе blessing понят как церковное благословение, второй звучит слишком официально.

rewrite.original: The council has approved the plan for the new market.
rewrite.frame: The council has given ____ to the plan for the new market.
rewrite.explanationRu: Одобрить план — give your blessing to it.

words.definitionEn: the act or ceremony of putting a dead person's body into a grave
words.situation: Talking about how and where a dead person's body is placed in the ground, often during a ceremony.

examples.text: My grandfather didn't want to be cremated; he asked for a simple [[burial]] beside his wife.
The soldier's remains were finally brought home for [[burial]] eighty years after the war.
Hundreds of fans waited outside the cemetery gates during the private [[burial]] of the singer.

texts: Archaeologists have found an ancient royal [[burial]] site under a car park.
Some religions require [[burial]] within a day of death.
The council now charges over two thousand pounds for a [[burial]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Похоронный марш — funeral march. Burial — само погребение, а церемония, процессия и музыка — это funeral.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Burial ground — место древних захоронений. Funeral — церемония, а graveyard и cemetery сами значат «кладбище», слово ground к ним не добавляют.

nuance.text: After the church service, only close family went to the cemetery for the [[burial]].
nuance.explanationRu: Funeral — вся церемония прощания, со службой и речами. Burial — сам момент погребения. Служба уже прошла, на кладбище остаётся только burial.

reverse.text: She was cremated after a small [[funeral]] attended by close friends.
reverse.explanationRu: Кремация исключает погребение в землю, поэтому burial здесь невозможно. Funeral — похороны как церемония, при любом обряде.

fixIt.text: Because of their religious beliefs, the family chose [[funeral]] rather than cremation.
fixIt.explanationRu: Кремации противопоставляют burial — погребение в землю. Funeral — похороны вообще, они бывают и при кремации.

wordFormation.text: The exact place of her [[burial]] remained a family secret for decades.

reply.context: A friend texts: "Grandad died on Sunday. We're flying to Ireland for the funeral."
options: I'm so sorry. I hope the trip isn't too much of a burial for you.
I'm so sorry. Will the burial be in his home village?
Kindly inform me of the burial arrangements at your earliest convenience.
reply.explanationRu: Burial — погребение, вопрос о месте естественен. В первом ответе burial спутано с burden (тяжесть), третий звучит как деловое письмо, а не сочувствие другу.

words.definitionEn: to suddenly start crying, laughing, singing or burning
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение burst into tears / burst out laughing — «разразиться, вдруг начать», а не базовое «лопнуть».
words.situation: Someone hears news and, without any warning, starts crying or laughing loudly.

examples.text: When the doctor said the operation had gone well, his wife [[burst]] into tears.
The whole audience [[burst]] out laughing when the actor's fake moustache fell off.
Luckily nobody was hurt when the old van suddenly [[burst]] into flames on the motorway.

texts: The kids [[burst]] into song as soon as the school bus left.
She read his text and [[burst]] out laughing in the middle of the meeting.
The hall [[burst]] into applause when her name was announced.

badCollocation.noteRu: После burst into нужно существительное (tears, laughter), а после burst out — форма на -ing: burst out crying.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Внезапно расплакаться — burst into tears. Explode и fall с tears не сочетаются, а после start нужен глагол: start crying.

nuance.text: Reading her late mother's letters, she [[burst]] into tears.
nuance.explanationRu: Burst into tears — внезапно расплакаться. Start так не сочетается: можно started crying, но не started into tears.

reverse.text: She [[started]] crying quietly so that nobody would notice.
reverse.explanationRu: Тихо и незаметно — это started crying. Burst значит внезапно и бурно, и после него нужно into tears или out crying.

fixIt.text: When the teacher's chair suddenly collapsed, the children [[exploded]] out laughing.
fixIt.explanationRu: Разразиться смехом — burst out laughing. Explode out laughing так не говорят; с explode возможно только explode with laughter.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How did your sister react when she got into medical school?"
options: She burst into a calm, polite smile and said thank you.
She burst into crying, and then she burst into laughing.
She burst into tears — happy ones, luckily!
reply.explanationRu: Burst into tears — бурно расплакаться, это естественный ответ. Спокойная улыбка с burst не сочетается, а burst into crying — ошибка: нужно burst into tears или burst out crying.

rewrite.original: When she heard the joke, she suddenly started laughing loudly.
rewrite.frame: When she heard the joke, she ____ laughing.
rewrite.explanationRu: Внезапно рассмеяться — burst out laughing.

words.definitionEn: to avoid a usual rule, process or person in order to act faster
words.senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение «обходить правила, процедуру или начальство», а не «объезжать город».
words.situation: Someone skips the official procedure or goes over their manager's head to get something done quickly.

examples.text: To save time, she [[bypassed]] her line manager and emailed the director directly.
Hackers found a way to [[bypass]] the bank's security checks and access customer accounts.
Patients who can pay privately can often [[bypass]] the long waiting lists for surgery.

texts: You can't just [[bypass]] the approval process because you're in a hurry.
Some apps let children [[bypass]] age checks far too easily.
Good leaders don't [[bypass]] their team when making big decisions.

badCollocation.noteRu: Обойти лужу или человека на улице — walk around или step around. Bypass — про дороги, правила и процедуры.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Официальный порядок в организации — channels: go through или bypass the usual channels. Canals — водные каналы, pipes — трубы, streams — ручьи.

nuance.text: To test the airport, an undercover reporter [[bypassed]] security by walking in through a staff entrance.
nuance.explanationRu: Pass security — пройти досмотр как положено. Bypass — обойти его стороной. Через служебный вход досмотр не проходят, а обходят.

reverse.text: All passengers must [[pass]] through security before boarding.
reverse.explanationRu: Пройти через досмотр — pass through security. Bypass значило бы, что пассажиры обходят досмотр, а это противоположный смысл.

fixIt.text: The manager [[overtook]] the normal approval process and signed the contract himself.
fixIt.explanationRu: Overtake — обогнать (машину, конкурента). Действовать в обход процедуры — bypass.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

reply.context: In a meeting, your manager says: "IT approval takes three weeks, but we need the new software by Friday."
options: Could we bypass the usual approval just this once and let IT check it later?
Great, then let's bypass Friday and install it on Thursday.
Whatever, just bypass the lot, mate, nobody cares.
reply.explanationRu: Bypass — обойти процедуру, поэтому естественно предложить обойти согласование. «Bypass Friday» бессмысленно, а третий ответ слишком грубый для совещания.

rewrite.original: She went straight to the CEO without talking to her manager first.
rewrite.frame: She ____ her manager and went straight to the CEO.
rewrite.explanationRu: Действовать в обход руководителя — bypass.

words.definitionEn: the group of senior ministers who make the main decisions in a government
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «кабинет министров», а не «шкаф»; кабинет начальника по-английски — office.
words.situation: The prime minister meets the most senior ministers to agree on important government decisions.

examples.text: The [[cabinet]] meets every Tuesday morning to discuss government policy.
After winning the election, she gave three women key jobs in her new [[cabinet]].
My brother follows politics closely and can name every minister in the [[cabinet]].

texts: She was the youngest woman ever to sit in the [[cabinet]].
The [[cabinet]] approved the plan after a long debate.
He was sacked from the [[cabinet]] for leaking secret documents.

badCollocation.noteRu: Кабинет директора — the director's office. Cabinet — это кабинет министров или шкаф, но не комната.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Перестановки в правительстве — a cabinet reshuffle (буквально «перетасовка»). Rotation, remix и reshaping в этом сочетании не употребляются.

nuance.text: The president has chosen a new [[cabinet]], with women in half of the top jobs.
nuance.explanationRu: Cabinet — кабинет министров, то есть группа людей. Office — комната или учреждение; назначить туда министров на половину постов нельзя.

reverse.text: Could you come to my [[office]] after lunch? We need to talk.
reverse.explanationRu: Кабинет как комната — office. Cabinet — правительство или шкаф, туда не приходят поговорить.

fixIt.text: The new prime minister will present her [[office]] of ministers to parliament on Monday.
fixIt.explanationRu: Кабинет министров — cabinet (of ministers). Office — кабинет-комната, к правительству это слово не относится.

options: Really? Did they move the cabinet into a bigger kitchen?
Really? Who's going to join the new cabinet, then?
Indeed? One trusts the cabinet shall be reconstituted forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: Cabinet здесь — кабинет министров, поэтому уместно спросить о новых министрах. Первый ответ путает его со шкафом, третий звучит архаично и чопорно.

words.definitionEn: careful planning to get what you want, often without caring about others
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «холодный расчёт, расчётливость», а не математическое вычисление.
words.situation: Someone acts kindly or makes a choice only because they expect to gain something from it.

examples.text: Critics said the minister's visit to the flooded town was cold [[calculation]], not real concern.
Her friendliness towards the new boss was pure [[calculation]]: she wanted the promotion.
The decision to raise prices was based on the [[calculation]] that loyal customers would not leave.

texts: Was it love or [[calculation]] that made her marry him?
Politicians rarely admit that [[calculation]] guides their choices.
His generosity was never entirely free of [[calculation]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Брак по расчёту — a marriage of convenience. Calculation в этом выражении не используют.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Холодный расчёт — cold calculation. Counting, computing и estimation — про подсчёт и вычисления, а не про расчётливость в поступках.

nuance.text: His apology sounded less like real regret and more like cold [[calculation]].
nuance.explanationRu: Calculation может значить корыстный расчёт в поступках людей. Computation — только вычисления (в математике, у компьютеров), о мотивах человека так не говорят.

fixIt.text: Her sudden kindness to her rich old aunt was pure [[prudence]]: she hoped to inherit the house.
fixIt.explanationRu: Prudence — благоразумие, это похвала. Корыстный расчёт — calculation.

wordFormation.text: Everyone could see that his tears on the talk show were a matter of [[calculation]], not feeling.

reply.context: A friend says: "Tom only started visiting his grandmother after he heard about her will."
options: Sounds like pure calculation to me. Poor woman!
Wow, his calculation must be excellent. Was he good at maths?
One discerns a certain degree of calculation in his conduct, I'm afraid.
reply.explanationRu: Calculation — корыстный расчёт, первый ответ точно передаёт мысль. Второй путает его с вычислениями, третий слишком книжный для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: She only married him because she wanted his money.
rewrite.frame: Her marriage was a matter of ____, not love.
rewrite.explanationRu: Корыстный расчёт — calculation.

words.definitionEn: a piece of strong cloth used for oil painting, or a painting done on it
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «холст, полотно (картина)»; значение «брезент, парусина» не рассматриваем.
words.situation: An artist prepares the surface for an oil painting, or a gallery shows several large paintings.

examples.text: She stretched a new [[canvas]] over the wooden frame and started sketching.
An unknown buyer paid two million pounds for a small [[canvas]] by a little-known Dutch painter.
The gallery's largest [[canvas]] is six metres wide and took the artist three years to paint.

texts: The paint had cracked, so the [[canvas]] needed careful repair.
He prefers painting on [[canvas]] rather than on wood.
Each [[canvas]] in the show depicts the same lighthouse at a different hour.

badCollocation.noteRu: По-русски картину «пишут», а по-английски — paint: paint a canvas, paint a picture.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Натянуть холст на подрамник — stretch a canvas. Extend и lengthen — «удлинить, продлить», draw — «рисовать»; с canvas так не говорят.

nuance.text: Before starting, the artist covered the whole [[canvas]] with a thin layer of grey paint.
nuance.explanationRu: До начала работы картины ещё нет — есть только холст, canvas. Picture — уже готовое изображение.

reverse.text: The children drew a [[picture]] of their house with crayons.
reverse.explanationRu: Детский рисунок карандашами — picture. Canvas — холст для живописи маслом или картина на нём.

fixIt.text: The gallery has just bought a huge [[cloth]] by a young Italian painter.
fixIt.explanationRu: Картину-полотно по-английски называют canvas. Cloth — ткань вообще, о картине так не говорят.

reply.context: At an art fair, a friend points at a huge oil painting: "Can you imagine that on our living-room wall?"
options: Only if we paint the wall with canvas first.
The canvas is, I must respectfully submit, of excessive dimensions.
It's a gorgeous canvas, but it's twice the size of our wall!
reply.explanationRu: Canvas — картина на холсте, третий ответ естественный. Первый делает из canvas краску, второй звучит как официальный доклад, а не разговор с другом.

words.definitionEn: the power or practical ability of a person, machine or organisation to do something
words.senseNote: Чаще всего о технике, организациях и странах: the capabilities of a system, military capability.
words.situation: Describing what a new phone, a company or a country's army is really able to do.

examples.text: For such a cheap phone, it has impressive night-vision [[capabilities]].
Opening offices in Asia is beyond the company's current [[capabilities]].
The lab now has the [[capability]] to sequence a full genome in a single day.

texts: The project will test the team's [[capabilities]] to the limit.
Few people use all the [[capabilities]] of their smartphones.
The hospital is expanding its research [[capabilities]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Способности к музыке или языкам — a talent / a gift for. Capability — возможности системы, организации или человека выполнить задачу.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Nuclear capability — способность страны создать ядерное оружие. Possibility и opportunity — «вероятность» и «шанс», talent — природный дар; с nuclear так не говорят.

nuance.text: The main selling point of the new watch is its sleep-tracking [[capability]].
nuance.explanationRu: Capability — что устройство умеет делать (следить за сном). Capacity — объём или вместимость (память, зал), к функциям часов это не подходит.

reverse.text: The new stadium has a [[capacity]] of sixty thousand people.
reverse.explanationRu: Вместимость стадиона — capacity. Capability — возможности и умения, а не число мест.

fixIt.text: My old laptop doesn't have the [[possibility]] to run modern video games.
fixIt.explanationRu: Possibility — вероятность, шанс. О том, что умеет техника, говорят capability: doesn't have the capability to.

wordFormation.text: Few experts doubt the country's [[capability]] to build its own satellites.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Can our current website handle online payments, or do we need a new one?"
options: Its capability is about twenty gigabytes, so we're fine.
It doesn't have that capability yet, but a plug-in could add it.
Please be advised that a capability assessment will be conducted in due course.
reply.explanationRu: Capability — умение системы что-то делать, второй ответ точный. В первом capability спутано с capacity (объём), третий — канцелярская отписка, а не ответ коллеге.

rewrite.original: The company is not able to deliver so many orders in one week.
rewrite.frame: Delivering so many orders in one week is beyond the company's ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Beyond someone's capabilities — «за пределами возможностей».

words.definitionEn: an economic system in which businesses are privately owned and run for profit
words.situation: Discussing an economy where private companies, not the state, own most businesses and compete for profit.

examples.text: After 1991, many Eastern European countries switched from central planning to [[capitalism]].
Supporters of [[capitalism]] say that competition drives innovation and keeps prices low.
The film is a dark satire of [[capitalism]], set in a company where workers are ranked by profit.

texts: The course looks at how [[capitalism]] developed in eighteenth-century Britain.
Even its critics admit that [[capitalism]] has created enormous wealth.
Is modern [[capitalism]] compatible with protecting the planet?

badCollocation.noteRu: Перед существительным нужно прилагательное: a capitalist country, a capitalist economy. Capitalism — название самой системы.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Экономическая система — capitalism (free-market capitalism). Capital — деньги, капитал; capitalization — рыночная стоимость компании; profitability — прибыльность.

nuance.text: Under [[capitalism]], most shops and factories belong to private owners.
nuance.explanationRu: Capitalism — экономическая система: «при капитализме». Capital — деньги или имущество для бизнеса (или столица), «при капитале» не живут.

reverse.text: The start-up needs more [[capital]] to hire new engineers.
reverse.explanationRu: Деньги для развития бизнеса — capital. Capitalism — система, её нельзя привлечь или потратить.

fixIt.text: In the 1990s the country moved from a planned economy to free-market [[capitalist]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Нужно название системы — существительное capitalism. Capitalist — «капиталист» или прилагательное «капиталистический».

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: Students on the course compare [[capitalism]] with other economic systems.

reply.context: In a seminar, the tutor asks: "What do you see as the main strength of a market economy?"
options: I'd say capitalism is good at encouraging innovation, though it can increase inequality.
I'd say capitalism, because the capital city usually has the best jobs.
Capitalism totally rocks, dude. Money, money, money!
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ корректно использует capitalism и звучит взвешенно. Во втором capitalism спутано со столицей (capital city), третий слишком развязный для семинара.

words.definitionEn: based on or supporting an economy of private business and profit
words.situation: Describing a country, economy or society where private companies compete and make profits for their owners.

examples.text: In a [[capitalist]] economy, most businesses are owned by private individuals rather than the state.
The novel shows the dark side of [[capitalist]] society through the eyes of a delivery driver.
The country's rapid shift to a [[capitalist]] system created a new class of very rich businessmen.

texts: The magazine is openly critical of the [[capitalist]] system.
Advertising lies at the heart of [[capitalist]] culture.
The two countries had very different economies: one [[capitalist]], the other communist.

badCollocation.noteRu: Капиталовложения — capital investment. Capitalist значит «капиталистический» (о системе, обществе, стране), а не «капитальный».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Перед system нужно прилагательное capitalist. Capitalism — существительное, capital — капитал или столица, capitalized — «написанный с заглавной буквы».

nuance.text: Most [[capitalist]] countries still provide free schooling for all children.
nuance.explanationRu: Capitalist описывает экономическую систему страны в целом. Commercial — «коммерческий», о бизнесе, товарах и прибыли; страну так не называют.

reverse.text: Despite bad reviews, the film was a huge [[commercial]] success.
reverse.explanationRu: Коммерческий успех фильма — commercial success. Capitalist описывает систему, а не прибыльность отдельного проекта.

fixIt.text: In a [[capitalism]] economy, prices are set mainly by supply and demand.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед economy нужно прилагательное capitalist. Capitalism — существительное, название системы.

words.definitionEn: the goods that a ship, plane or truck carries
words.situation: Talking about the goods loaded onto a ship or plane and transported to another country.

examples.text: The ship was carrying a [[cargo]] of frozen fish when it ran aground off the coast.
Most of the airline's profits now come from [[cargo]], not passengers.
Dock workers spent the whole night unloading the [[cargo]] from the container ship.

texts: Customs officers searched the [[cargo]] for hidden drugs.
A [[cargo]] ship blocked the canal for six days.
The truck lost part of its [[cargo]] on the motorway.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Груз ответственности» — the burden of responsibility. Cargo — только настоящий груз на корабле, самолёте или грузовике.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Грузовое судно — a cargo ship. Load — груз в кузове или нагрузка, weight — вес, burden — тяжкое бремя; со ship они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The plane carries both passengers and [[cargo]], such as mail and fresh flowers.
nuance.explanationRu: Cargo — коммерческий груз: почта, товары, цветы. Luggage — личные вещи пассажиров (чемоданы, сумки), почта к ним не относится.

reverse.text: Please don't leave your [[luggage]] unattended anywhere in the station.
reverse.explanationRu: Чемоданы и сумки пассажиров — luggage. Cargo — груз для перевозки, а не личные вещи.

fixIt.text: The plane was carrying forty tonnes of [[load]], mostly medicine and food.
fixIt.explanationRu: Груз самолёта или судна — cargo. Load — «груз, нагрузка» в общем смысле и обычно исчисляемое: a load of.

reply.context: Your friend, who works at the port, texts: "Can't meet tonight, sorry. A ship came in late."
options: No worries. Is the cargo coming to dinner with us instead?
Acknowledged. Kindly confirm the cargo discharge schedule.
No worries. Are you stuck unloading cargo all night?
reply.explanationRu: Cargo — груз с судна, третий ответ естественный. Первый говорит о грузе как о человеке, второй звучит как служебная записка, а не сообщение другу.

words.definitionEn: one of the separate sections of a train in which passengers travel
words.senseNote: Выбрано британское значение «пассажирский вагон» (в американском — car); значения «карета» и «доставка груза» не рассматриваем.
words.situation: Looking for your seat on a long train journey, or complaining that part of the train is overcrowded.

examples.text: Our seats were in the last [[carriage]], so we had to walk the whole length of the platform.
Passengers complained that the train had only four [[carriages]] during the morning rush hour.
Could you keep your voice down? This is the quiet [[carriage]].

texts: The first-class [[carriage]] was almost empty.
We found two free seats in the next [[carriage]].
A man in our [[carriage]] was playing loud music on his phone.

badCollocation.noteRu: Грузовой вагон — goods wagon (брит.) или freight car (амер.). Carriage — вагон для пассажиров.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Тихий вагон в британском поезде — the quiet carriage. Wagon — грузовой вагон, cabinet — шкаф или правительство, chamber — зал или палата.

nuance.text: The [[carriage]] was so long that it had over sixty seats and two toilets.
nuance.explanationRu: Carriage — весь вагон целиком. Compartment — купе, небольшое закрытое отделение внутри вагона; шестидесяти мест и двух туалетов в купе не бывает.

reverse.text: We had a sleeping [[compartment]] to ourselves on the night train.
reverse.explanationRu: Отдельное купе в ночном поезде — compartment. Carriage — целый вагон, а не купе на двоих.

fixIt.text: The train was so full that I had to stand in the [[wagon]] all the way to Leeds.
fixIt.explanationRu: Пассажирский вагон в британском английском — carriage (в американском — car). Wagon — грузовой вагон, это ложный друг.

words.definitionEn: a company that transports passengers or goods, especially an airline
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «перевозчик, авиакомпания»; значения «носитель инфекции» и «авианосец» не рассматриваем.
words.situation: Choosing which airline or transport company to fly or ship with, often comparing prices and service.

examples.text: Budget [[carriers]] often charge extra for seat selection and hand luggage.
The national [[carrier]] has cancelled all flights to the region because of the storm.
We switched to a cheaper [[carrier]] for our deliveries, but parcels now arrive late.

texts: Which [[carrier]] are you flying with?
The [[carrier]] lost two of our parcels last month.
The country's biggest [[carrier]] is planning to buy fifty new planes.

badCollocation.noteRu: Носильщик в отеле или на вокзале — porter. Carrier — компания-перевозчик, например авиакомпания.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Бюджетная авиакомпания — a low-cost carrier. Transporter — транспортёр (машина), conveyor — конвейер, porter — носильщик.

nuance.text: Our [[carrier]] cancelled the flight and put us on a train instead.
nuance.explanationRu: Carrier — перевозчик, крупная транспортная компания (авиакомпания). Courier — курьер, который доставляет посылки и документы; рейсы он не отменяет.

reverse.text: A [[courier]] brought the signed contract to our office by bike.
reverse.explanationRu: Человек, который привёз документы на велосипеде, — courier. Carrier — компания-перевозчик, а не курьер.

fixIt.text: Before booking, check which [[transporter]] actually operates the flight.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перевозчик, который выполняет рейс, — carrier. Transporter — машина или платформа для перевозки, а не авиакомпания.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: Passengers can claim compensation from the [[carrier]] if a flight is delayed by over three hours.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Why is your flight to Rome so cheap?"
options: It's with a budget carrier — he's carrying my suitcase for free!
It's with a budget carrier, so I'm only allowed one small bag.
The carrier's pricing strategy is predicated upon ancillary revenue streams.
reply.explanationRu: Budget carrier — бюджетная авиакомпания, второй ответ естественный. В первом carrier понято как человек-носильщик, третий звучит как доклад экономиста, а не ответ другу.

words.definitionEn: to build a career, role or position for yourself through hard work
words.senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение carve out (a career, a niche) — «добиться, завоевать своим трудом», а не «вырезать из дерева».
words.situation: Someone works hard for years to win a special position or place for themselves in their field.

examples.text: After years of hard work, she [[carved]] out a successful career as a translator.
The small firm has [[carved]] out a niche in eco-friendly packaging.
The young striker has quickly [[carved]] out a place for himself in the national team.

texts: It takes years to [[carve]] out a reputation in this industry.
Small shops must [[carve]] out a niche to survive against online giants.
She moved to Berlin to [[carve]] out a new life for herself.

badCollocation.noteRu: Разработать план — draw up или work out a plan. Carve out — «завоевать, выкроить» себе нишу, место или карьеру.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Занять свою нишу — carve out a niche (буквально «вырезать»). Find a niche возможно, но без out; make out и take out значат совсем другое.

nuance.text: It took her ten years to [[carve]] out a name for herself in fashion.
nuance.explanationRu: Carve out a name, a niche — завоевать своим трудом. Cut out значит «вырезать ножницами» или «исключить», для карьеры не подходит.

reverse.text: I [[cut]] out the article and stuck it on the fridge.
reverse.explanationRu: Вырезать статью из газеты ножницами — cut out. Carve — резать по дереву или камню, а в переносном смысле — завоёвывать себе место.

fixIt.text: Through sheer talent, the young chef [[cut]] out a place for herself among the city's top cooks.
fixIt.explanationRu: Cut out — вырезать ножницами или исключить. Завоевать себе место своим трудом — carve out.
