reply.context: At a networking event, someone asks: "How did you end up running your own design studio?"
options: I carved the studio out of wood myself, actually.
I spent ten years freelancing and slowly carved out a niche in book covers.
Yo, I just carved out, like, a niche thingy, innit.
reply.explanationRu: Carve out a niche — завоевать свою нишу, второй ответ точный. Первый понимает carve буквально (вырезать из дерева), третий слишком жаргонный для делового знакомства.

words.definitionEn: a person who is killed or injured in a war or an accident
words.senseNote: Casualties — и погибшие, и раненые, а не только погибшие.
words.situation: News reports say how many people were killed or hurt in a crash, flood or battle.

examples.text: The train crash caused dozens of [[casualties]], most of them with minor injuries.
The region suffered heavy [[casualties]] in the floods of 1953.
Thanks to the new speed limit, the number of [[casualties]] on the town's roads has fallen by a third.

texts: Rescue teams are still counting the [[casualties]] after the earthquake.
Hospitals were ready to receive [[casualties]] from the crash site.
Luckily, there were no [[casualties]] when the old bridge collapsed.

badCollocation.noteRu: Жертвы болезни или эпидемии — victims или deaths. Casualties — пострадавшие в войне, аварии или катастрофе.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Большие потери — heavy casualties. Big, strong и hard с casualties не сочетаются: «тяжёлые» потери по-английски именно heavy.

nuance.text: The earthquake caused heavy [[casualties]] in the old part of the city.
nuance.explanationRu: Heavy casualties — большие потери (убитые и раненые). С victims так не говорят: victim — жертва преступления, болезни или обмана.

reverse.text: She was the [[victim]] of an online scam and lost all her savings.
reverse.explanationRu: Жертва мошенничества — victim. Casualty — только убитый или раненый в войне, аварии, катастрофе.

fixIt.text: The hurricane caused many [[sacrifices]] among the island's population.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Жертвы» катастрофы — casualties (или victims). Sacrifice — жертва в смысле самопожертвования или жертвоприношения.

reply.context: Your colleague reads a headline aloud: "Bus overturns on mountain road."
options: Oh no. Was it a casualty, or did someone do it on purpose?
Pray, might one enquire as to the casualty figures?
Oh no. Were there any casualties?
reply.explanationRu: Were there any casualties? — естественный вопрос о пострадавших. В первом casualty спутано со «случайностью», второй звучит архаично и вычурно.

rewrite.original: Nobody was killed or injured in the fire.
rewrite.frame: There were no ____ in the fire.
rewrite.explanationRu: No casualties — «никто не погиб и не пострадал».

words.definitionEn: a long series of bad things, such as mistakes or failures
words.senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение «череда (ошибок, бед)», а не базовое «каталог товаров».
words.situation: A report or review describes one mistake or disaster after another, all in one long list.

examples.text: The official report described the hospital's response as a [[catalogue]] of errors.
Our holiday was a [[catalogue]] of disasters: lost bags, a flooded hotel and food poisoning.
The team's season has been a [[catalogue]] of injuries, defeats and bad luck.

texts: The inquiry uncovered a [[catalogue]] of failures at the company.
Her complaint letter was a long [[catalogue]] of grievances.
His career has been a [[catalogue]] of missed chances.

badCollocation.noteRu: В переносном смысле catalogue — череда неудач: a catalogue of errors, of disasters. Про победы говорят a string of victories или a run of wins.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Череда ошибок — a catalogue of errors (также series или string of errors). Menu, brochure и diary так не употребляются.

nuance.text: Critics called the new stadium project a [[catalogue]] of disasters.
nuance.explanationRu: A catalogue of disasters — образно «сплошная череда бед». List — список на бумаге; назвать сам проект «списком катастроф» по-английски нельзя.

reverse.text: Don't forget to make a shopping [[list]] before you go.
reverse.explanationRu: Список покупок — shopping list. Catalogue — каталог товаров или (перен.) череда неудач, а не записка перед походом в магазин.

fixIt.text: The builder's work was a [[row]] of costly mistakes, from leaking pipes to crooked walls.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Ряд ошибок» — не a row (ряд предметов в линию), а a catalogue of mistakes.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How was the wedding? I heard it didn't go exactly to plan."
options: It was a catalogue of disasters: the cake fell over and the band got lost.
It was lovely — the catalogue of the bride's dress was beautiful.
It was, as it were, a catalogue of unfortunate occurrences, I daresay.
reply.explanationRu: A catalogue of disasters — «сплошные неприятности», первый ответ естественный. Во втором catalogue бессмысленно, третий звучит вычурно и старомодно.

rewrite.original: The project had one serious problem after another.
rewrite.frame: The project was a ____ of serious problems.
rewrite.explanationRu: Череда проблем — a catalogue of problems.

words.definitionEn: to provide what a particular group of people needs or wants
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение cater for / cater to — «быть рассчитанным на, удовлетворять запросы»; значение «обеспечивать питание на банкете» не рассматриваем.
words.situation: A hotel, school or shop is designed to give a particular type of customer exactly what they need.

examples.text: The resort [[caters]] mainly for families with young children, so it's not ideal for a quiet break.
Our school [[caters]] for students with a wide range of learning needs.
Streaming services now [[cater]] to every taste, from Korean dramas to nature documentaries.

texts: The menu doesn't [[cater]] for vegetarians at all.
These courses [[cater]] to complete beginners.
Small hotels can [[cater]] for guests' individual needs.

badCollocation.noteRu: После cater нужен предлог: cater to (или for) the needs of students.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Быть рассчитанным на любой вкус — cater to (или for) every taste. Предлоги at, with и on с cater в этом значении не используются.

nuance.text: The new gym [[caters]] for older people, with gentle classes and extra-wide changing rooms.
nuance.explanationRu: Cater for — быть рассчитанным на какую-то группу: занятия и раздевалки для пожилых. Care for — лично ухаживать за больным или пожилым человеком.

reverse.text: She gave up work to [[care]] for her elderly father.
reverse.explanationRu: Ухаживать за пожилым отцом — care for. Cater for значило бы «обслуживать» или «кормить», как ресторан.

fixIt.text: The menu at the new café [[cares]] for vegans and people with food allergies.
fixIt.explanationRu: Меню не может «ухаживать» (care for) за людьми. Быть рассчитанным на веганов и аллергиков — cater for.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Is that new hotel by the station any good for a family weekend?"
options: Not really — it caters mostly for business travellers, so there's nothing for kids.
Yes, the staff will cater for your kids at night, like babysitters.
The establishment caters, one presumes, to a clientele of a corporate nature.
reply.explanationRu: Cater for — быть рассчитанным на определённых гостей, первый ответ точный. Во втором cater спутано с care for (присматривать), третий слишком вычурный для разговора с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The magazine is written mainly for people who love gardening.
rewrite.frame: The magazine ____ people who love gardening.
rewrite.explanationRu: Быть рассчитанным на какую-то аудиторию — cater for / cater to.

words.definitionEn: cows and bulls that are kept on a farm for their meat or milk
words.senseNote: Одно значение; слово всегда во множественном числе: the cattle are grazing.
words.situation: A farmer moves cows from one field to another or sells them for beef.

examples.text: In summer the farmers take their [[cattle]] up to the mountains to graze.
With no grass left after the drought, the [[cattle]] had to be fed on expensive hay.
Most of the beef sold in the country comes from [[cattle]] raised on grass, not grain.

texts: Thousands of [[cattle]] died during the long, dry summer.
The [[cattle]] were grazing peacefully by the river.
The family has raised beef [[cattle]] on this land for a century.

badCollocation.noteRu: Cattle — только множественное число: many cattle, the cattle are. Одну корову называют a cow.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Herd — стадо крупных животных: a herd of cattle. У кур — flock, у волков — pack, у рыб — shoal или school.

nuance.text: The farmer sold all his [[cattle]] but kept the sheep and the chickens.
nuance.explanationRu: Cattle — только коровы и быки. Livestock — весь домашний скот, включая овец и кур, поэтому «продал весь скот, но оставил овец» звучит противоречиво.

reverse.text: The farm keeps a lot of [[livestock]]: sheep, pigs, goats and chickens.
reverse.explanationRu: Овцы, свиньи и куры — это livestock, скот вообще. Cattle — только крупный рогатый скот.

fixIt.text: The floods killed hundreds of [[cattles]] in the north of the country.
fixIt.explanationRu: Cattle уже означает множественное число и никогда не принимает -s: hundreds of cattle.

words.definitionEn: great care taken to avoid danger, risks or mistakes
words.senseNote: Значение «осторожность» в сочетаниях уровня C1: exercise caution, urge caution, err on the side of caution.
words.situation: Experts advise people to be very careful before making a risky decision or trusting early results.

examples.text: Experts urged [[caution]], saying the early results of the drug trial were promising but limited.
Treat any email asking for your password with extreme [[caution]].
The roads are icy this morning, so drivers should proceed with [[caution]].

texts: When in doubt, err on the side of [[caution]].
Investors are showing more [[caution]] after last year's losses.
Doctors advise [[caution]] when mixing these two medicines.

badCollocation.noteRu: С большой осторожностью — with great (или extreme) caution. Big с caution не сочетается.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Проявлять осторожность — exercise caution (или show caution). Do, make и keep с caution не сочетаются.

nuance.text: If you're not sure the mushrooms are safe, err on the side of [[caution]] and don't eat them.
nuance.explanationRu: Err on the side of caution — устойчивое выражение «лучше перестраховаться». Care в нём не используется: care — забота или аккуратность.

reverse.text: Bye, and take [[care]] on the way home!
reverse.explanationRu: Take care — «береги себя», дружеское прощание. Take caution так не говорят.

fixIt.text: Hikers are advised to exercise [[carefulness]] on the narrow mountain path after heavy rain.
fixIt.explanationRu: Со словом exercise сочетается caution: exercise caution. Carefulness — редкое слово, в таких предупреждениях его не используют.

wordFormation.text: A [[cautious]] investor would never put all her savings into one company.

rewrite.original: You should be very careful when you use this app.
rewrite.frame: This app should be used with ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Use with caution — «пользоваться с осторожностью».

words.definitionEn: careful to avoid risks, and not willing to act or decide quickly
words.senseNote: Значение то же, что на уровне B1; уровень C1 — в сочетаниях cautious optimism, a cautious welcome, be cautious about.
words.situation: Someone avoids taking risks, waits for more information and does not rush into a decision.

examples.text: After losing money in the last crash, she's become very [[cautious]] about investing.
The union gave a [[cautious]] welcome to the new pay offer, saying details still had to be agreed.
Doctors are [[cautious]] about letting him go home so soon after the operation.

texts: Scientists are [[cautious]] about drawing conclusions from one study.
The bank took a [[cautious]] approach and kept interest rates unchanged.
She's a [[cautious]] driver who never goes over the speed limit.

badCollocation.noteRu: Бытовое «Осторожно, горячо!» — Careful, it's hot! Cautious описывает человека или подход, а не предупреждение.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Сдержанно одобрить — give a cautious welcome. Careful, attentive и prudent в этом сочетании не используются.

nuance.text: The company gave a [[cautious]] estimate of five percent growth, and the real figure was much higher.
nuance.explanationRu: Cautious estimate — осторожный, заниженный «с запасом» прогноз. Careful estimate — тщательно рассчитанный; он не объясняет, почему реальность оказалась намного лучше.

reverse.text: Be [[careful]] not to spill coffee on the keyboard.
reverse.explanationRu: Be careful not to spill — бытовое «смотри не пролей». Cautious так не используется: оно о нежелании рисковать.

fixIt.text: The two leaders expressed [[careful]] optimism about the peace talks.
fixIt.explanationRu: Осторожный, сдержанный оптимизм — cautious optimism. Careful optimism так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: Analysts are [[cautiously]] optimistic about the economy next year.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "The new client wants us to start work before the contract is signed. What do you think?"
options: I'd be cautious — let's start right away and forget about the contract.
One would be well advised to adopt a cautious stance, would one not?
I'd be cautious — let's get the contract signed first.
reply.explanationRu: Cautious — не рисковать без гарантий, третий ответ логичен. Первый противоречит сам себе, второй звучит чопорно и неестественно для разговора с коллегой.

words.definitionEn: to stop happening, existing or doing something
words.situation: An official notice says that a service, company or activity will officially stop.

examples.text: The company [[ceased]] trading in 2019 after years of heavy losses.
By the end of the war, the old empire had [[ceased]] to exist.
Payments will [[cease]] if you fail to report a change in your income.

texts: The factory [[ceased]] production last spring.
Fighting finally [[ceased]] after three days of talks.
The rain [[ceased]], and the sun came out over the hills.

badCollocation.noteRu: Остановить машину — stop the car. Cease — «прекратить» деятельность или существование, а не физически остановить.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Прекратить существование — cease to exist. Stop to do значит «остановиться, чтобы что-то сделать», а finish и end с инфинитивом не употребляются.

nuance.text: His patience with difficult customers never [[ceases]] to amaze me.
nuance.explanationRu: Never ceases to amaze — «не перестаёт удивлять». Stops to amaze — ошибка: stop to do значит «остановиться, чтобы сделать»; можно never stops amazing me.

reverse.text: Could you [[stop]] tapping your pen? I'm trying to concentrate.
reverse.explanationRu: В живой речи просят stop. Cease звучит как официальный документ, в такой просьбе оно неуместно.

fixIt.text: We regret to announce that this bus service will [[quit]] on 1 March.
fixIt.explanationRu: Quit — «бросить, уволиться», о человеке. Об официальном прекращении работы сервиса — cease.

wordFormation.text: The agreement called for an immediate [[cessation]] of hostilities.

reply.context: Your landlord emails: "The noise from your flat after midnight must stop."
options: Sure, bro, the noise will totally cease, chill.
Understood. The late-night parties will cease — sorry for the trouble.
Understood. I'll cease the washing machine after midnight, then.
reply.explanationRu: Cease уместно в вежливом ответе на официальное письмо: вечеринки прекратятся. Cease the washing machine — ошибка (нужно turn off), а первый ответ слишком фамильярный.

rewrite.original: The small airline went out of business in 2020.
rewrite.frame: The small airline ____ operations in 2020.
rewrite.explanationRu: Прекратить работу — cease operations.

words.definitionEn: making you feel trapped and anxious, especially in a small or crowded space
words.senseNote: Здесь — о месте или обстановке; о человеке (I'm claustrophobic) — «страдающий клаустрофобией».
words.situation: You describe a tiny windowless room, a stuck lift or a small community where you feel trapped.

examples.text: The cabin on the night train was so [[claustrophobic]] that I spent most of the journey in the corridor.
Almost the whole film takes place in one small, dark flat, which gives it a [[claustrophobic]] feel.
Some patients find the scanner [[claustrophobic]], so the hospital offers music and a mirror to help them relax.

texts: Six of us shared a [[claustrophobic]] little office above the shop.
Everyone knew her business, and she found village life [[claustrophobic]].
The lift was tiny and [[claustrophobic]], so I took the stairs instead.

badCollocation.noteRu: После suffer from нужно существительное: suffer from claustrophobia. Claustrophobic — прилагательное: a claustrophobic lift.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Гнетущую, давящую атмосферу называют claustrophobic. Narrow, compact и small описывают размер предмета или помещения, а не атмосферу.

nuance.text: The room wasn't small, but with no windows it felt strangely [[claustrophobic]].
nuance.explanationRu: Cramped — тесный, где физически мало места. Claustrophobic — давящий, вызывающий желание выбраться. Комната здесь не маленькая, поэтому cramped противоречит смыслу.

fixIt.text: Being stuck in a broken lift for an hour was a truly [[claustrophobia]] experience.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед существительным experience нужно прилагательное: a claustrophobic experience. Claustrophobia — существительное, название самой фобии.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: People with [[claustrophobia]] often avoid lifts, tunnels and crowded trains.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "Shall we book the little meeting room on the fourth floor for tomorrow's workshop?"
options: Great idea — it's so claustrophobic that there'll be plenty of room for all twelve of us.
I'd rather not. With twelve of us and no windows, it'll feel pretty claustrophobic.
Please be informed that the aforementioned room is of a claustrophobic nature.
reply.explanationRu: Claustrophobic — тесный и давящий, это минус, а не «много места». Третий вариант звучит как официальное уведомление, а не ответ коллеге.

words.definitionEn: to keep holding on to a belief, hope or position you are afraid to lose
words.senseNote: Здесь — переносное значение (cling to hope, cling to power); в прямом смысле cling — крепко вцепиться в кого-то или что-то.
words.situation: Someone refuses to let go of power, an old belief or a fading hope, even when it seems unwise.

examples.text: Long after the divorce, he [[clung]] to the hope that she would one day come back.
Despite falling sales, the director is still [[clinging]] to a strategy she believes will work.
When life feels chaotic, many people [[cling]] to familiar routines that make them feel safe.

texts: Some politicians [[cling]] to power long after voters have lost faith in them.
It's natural to [[cling]] to hope when someone you love goes missing.
Older staff sometimes [[cling]] to methods they learned decades ago.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Цепляться за» — cling to (или cling on to), а не for: cling to power, cling to hope.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Держаться за власть вопреки всему — cling to power. Grab, grasp и catch значат «схватить» и с to в этом смысле не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Terrified of being alone, she [[clung]] to a relationship that was making her miserable.
nuance.explanationRu: Cling to — держаться за что-то из страха потерять, даже во вред себе. Stick to — придерживаться плана, правил или диеты; к отношениям, за которые держатся от страха, не подходит.

reverse.text: If you want to see results, you have to [[stick]] to the plan for at least a month.
reverse.explanationRu: Придерживаться плана, диеты или правил — stick to. Cling to звучит как отчаянная хватка за то, что ускользает, и для совета не подходит.

fixIt.text: Afraid of losing control, the company's ageing founder [[stuck]] to power until the board forced him out.
fixIt.explanationRu: Держаться за власть из страха её потерять — cling to power. Stick to — придерживаться плана или правил, с power не сочетается.

reply.context: A colleague writes: "The old booking system is slow and everyone hates it, but the boss won't let us replace it."
options: Kindly note that the manager is clinging to legacy infrastructure, as previously communicated.
Typical. He clings to every new app the moment it comes out.
Typical. He's clinging to it because he built it himself years ago.
reply.explanationRu: Cling to — упорно держаться за старое, а не хвататься за всё новое. Первый вариант — канцелярит, коллеге в чате так не пишут.

words.definitionEn: relating to the direct examination and treatment of patients
words.senseNote: Здесь — медицинское значение; clinical также значит «холодный, бесстрастный» (a clinical tone).
words.situation: Doctors and researchers talk about work with real patients, such as testing new drugs or diagnosing illness.

examples.text: The new drug will go through three years of [[clinical]] trials before it reaches pharmacies.
After ten years in the lab, she missed [[clinical]] work with real patients.
Her doctor explained that everyday sadness is very different from [[clinical]] depression.

texts: Student nurses spend months on [[clinical]] placements in busy hospitals.
The vaccine has now passed its final [[clinical]] trial.
The test result has little [[clinical]] significance, so don't worry.

badCollocation.noteRu: Больница при медицинском вузе — teaching hospital или university hospital; clinical hospital — калька с русского «клиническая больница».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Испытания лекарств на пациентах — clinical trials. Clinic — существительное (клиника), medicine trials так не говорят, а cynical значит «циничный».

nuance.text: Before approval, every new treatment must pass strict [[clinical]] tests on patients.
nuance.explanationRu: Clinical — связанный с обследованием и лечением пациентов: clinical tests, clinical trials. Medicinal — целебный, лечебный: medicinal herbs, medicinal properties.

reverse.text: Many common garden plants have [[medicinal]] properties.
reverse.explanationRu: Целебные свойства растений — medicinal properties. Clinical относится к работе врачей с пациентами, а не к свойствам трав.

fixIt.text: Before a new medicine is approved, it must pass several stages of [[clinic]] testing.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед существительным testing нужно прилагательное: clinical testing. Clinic — существительное: поликлиника или частная клиника.

wordFormation.text: The hospital is known for combining research with excellent [[clinical]] care.

reply.context: A friend who works as a nurse tells you: "I'm thinking of leaving the ward for an office job in hospital management."
options: Really? Won't you miss the clinical side — actually looking after patients?
Really? Won't you miss the clinical side — all the budgets and meetings?
Kindly elaborate on the rationale for your clinical-to-administrative transition.
reply.explanationRu: Clinical — связанный с лечением пациентов, а не с бюджетами и совещаниями. Третий вариант звучит как анкета отдела кадров, а не разговор с другом.

words.definitionEn: a feeling that a painful experience has truly ended, so you can move on
words.senseNote: Здесь — эмоциональное значение (need closure); базовое значение — закрытие предприятия или дороги (factory closure, road closure).
words.situation: After a breakup, a loss or a long court case, someone finally feels able to put it behind them.

examples.text: Clearing out her late mother's flat was painful, but it gave her some [[closure]].
Breaking up by text gave neither of them [[closure]], so they finally met for coffee.
The official apology gave the victims' families the sense of [[closure]] they had waited decades for.

texts: After the divorce, I just wanted [[closure]], not revenge.
Therapy helped him find [[closure]] after his brother's death.
The final episode gave fans the [[closure]] they had hoped for.

badCollocation.noteRu: Closure не «делают»: говорят get, find или need closure, а также bring someone closure.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Чувство, что тяжёлая история позади, — a sense of closure. End, finish и closing просто значат «конец» и в этом выражении не используются.

nuance.text: Being fired without any explanation left him angry, and he never really got [[closure]].
nuance.explanationRu: Closure — внутреннее ощущение, что тяжёлая история закончилась и можно жить дальше. Conclusion — вывод или заключительная часть доклада; о чувствах так не говорят.

reverse.text: In the [[conclusion]], the authors suggest three ways to reduce costs.
reverse.explanationRu: Заключительная часть текста — conclusion. Closure — о внутреннем чувстве завершённости у человека, а не о разделе отчёта.

fixIt.text: Honestly, I just want to see him once more, say goodbye and get some [[completeness]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Эмоциональная «завершённость» — closure: get some closure. Completeness — полнота (данных, списка), о чувствах после расставания так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: Some people write letters they never send, just to get a little [[closure]].

reply.context: A friend texts: "My ex wants to meet up and talk things through. Should I go?"
options: Go! Closure is great — you two might even get back together.
Please be advised that closure may be obtained by attending the meeting.
Only if you want closure. If you're secretly hoping to get back together, maybe don't.
reply.explanationRu: Closure — ощущение, что история закончена и её можно отпустить, а не шанс всё вернуть. Второй вариант звучит как официальное письмо, а не ответ другу.

words.definitionEn: a small group of similar things or people that are close together
words.situation: You describe several similar things, like houses, stars or cases of an illness, grouped closely together.

examples.text: A small [[cluster]] of white houses sits on the hillside above the harbour.
Doctors noticed an unusual [[cluster]] of flu cases among staff at one office.
The old docks now host a [[cluster]] of tech start-ups and design studios.

texts: On a clear night you can see a bright [[cluster]] of stars.
Tiny white flowers grow in a dense [[cluster]] at the end of each stem.
The hotel is a [[cluster]] of wooden cabins beside the lake.

badCollocation.noteRu: Большое «скопление людей» — a crowd. Cluster — небольшая группка людей или предметов, стоящих рядом.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Звёздное скопление — a cluster of stars. Flock говорят о птицах и овцах, pack — о волках или картах, pile — о куче вещей.

nuance.text: Scientists have identified a [[cluster]] of genes linked to the disease.
nuance.explanationRu: Cluster — нейтральное, в том числе научное слово для группы похожих объектов рядом. Bunch — разговорное («пучок», «куча»), в научном тексте звучит небрежно.

reverse.text: He came home with a [[bunch]] of flowers from the market.
reverse.explanationRu: Букет или связка, которую держат в руках (цветов, ключей), — a bunch. Cluster — группа предметов, которые растут или стоят рядом.

fixIt.text: Astronomers have discovered a new [[accumulation]] of young stars in our galaxy.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Скопление» звёзд, домов или случаев болезни — cluster. Accumulation — постепенное накопление (пыли, долгов, опыта), а не группа объектов рядом.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

rewrite.original: Several small houses stood close together near the river.
rewrite.frame: A small ____ stood near the river.
rewrite.explanationRu: Несколько домов, стоящих рядом, — a cluster of houses.

words.definitionEn: a group of parties or organisations that join together for a shared aim
words.situation: Several political parties or groups agree to work together, often to form a government or fight for a cause.

examples.text: Since no party won a majority, three of them formed a [[coalition]] to run the country.
A [[coalition]] of charities and local businesses is campaigning to save the town library.
The two countries joined an international [[coalition]] to fight plastic pollution in the oceans.

texts: The [[coalition]] collapsed after the two parties disagreed over taxes.
Environmental groups have joined the [[coalition]] against the new airport.
Critics say the ruling [[coalition]] has no clear plan for the economy.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Коалиция из двух партий» — a coalition of two parties; предлог from здесь не подходит.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Коалицию создают глаголом form (а также build или join). Make, do и take с coalition не сочетаются.

nuance.text: After weeks of talks, the new [[coalition]] government was finally sworn in.
nuance.explanationRu: Правительство из нескольких партий — coalition government, это устойчивое сочетание. Alliance — союз, чаще стран или компаний и надолго; alliance government не говорят.

reverse.text: Several airlines have joined an [[alliance]] so that passengers can collect points with any of them.
reverse.explanationRu: Долгосрочный союз компаний или стран — alliance (airline alliance). Coalition — чаще временное объединение партий или групп ради конкретной цели.

fixIt.text: Most experts expect a [[coalitional]] government after Sunday's election.
fixIt.explanationRu: Правительство из нескольких партий — coalition government: существительное coalition работает как определение. Форма coalitional почти не используется.

rewrite.original: After the election, two parties agreed to govern the country together.
rewrite.frame: After the election, two parties formed ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Совместное правление нескольких партий — a coalition (government).

words.definitionEn: on, near or connected with the land beside the sea
words.senseNote: У слова одно значение; здесь оно показано в типичных для C1 сочетаниях (coastal erosion, coastal waters).
words.situation: You talk about towns, roads, waters or wildlife on the land right next to the sea.

examples.text: Rising sea levels are putting many [[coastal]] communities at risk of flooding.
We spent the weekend walking a [[coastal]] path with amazing views of the cliffs.
Fishing and tourism are the main sources of income in this [[coastal]] region.

texts: Winter storms have caused serious [[coastal]] erosion in the east.
Dolphins are often spotted in these [[coastal]] waters in summer.
The old [[coastal]] road winds past fishing villages and quiet beaches.

badCollocation.noteRu: Береговая охрана — the coastguard (или coast guard), без -al. Coastal значит «прибрежный»: coastal waters, coastal towns.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Прибрежные воды — coastal waters. Seaside говорят о курортах и отдыхе (a seaside town), beachy — разговорное «пляжный», coasting — от глагола «катиться по инерции».

nuance.text: Engineers are building new [[coastal]] defences to protect the town from storms.
nuance.explanationRu: Coastal — нейтральное, географическое «прибрежный»: coastal defences, coastal erosion. Seaside связано с отдыхом у моря (a seaside holiday, a seaside town) и к защитным сооружениям не подходит.

fixIt.text: House prices in [[marine]] towns have risen sharply since remote working became common.
fixIt.explanationRu: Города на побережье — coastal towns. Marine — «морской» в биологическом смысле: marine life, marine biology.

cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

wordFormation.text: The ferry stops at every small [[coastal]] village along the way.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Where should we go for a quiet weekend away in October?"
options: I would recommend a coastal locality offering adequate accommodation facilities.
How about that little coastal town we drove through? Long walks, fresh fish, no crowds.
How about a coastal village high in the mountains, far from the sea?
reply.explanationRu: Coastal — у моря, поэтому «в горах, далеко от моря» — противоречие. Первый ответ звучит как отчёт турагентства, а не совет другу.

words.definitionEn: connected with thinking, learning, remembering and understanding
words.situation: Psychologists and doctors describe mental abilities such as memory, attention and problem-solving, and how they change with age.

examples.text: Regular exercise may help to slow [[cognitive]] decline in older adults.
Puzzles and board games support young children's [[cognitive]] development in a playful way.
Constant notifications increase our [[cognitive]] load and make it harder to concentrate.

texts: Lack of sleep affects your [[cognitive]] performance the next day.
Brain-training apps claim to boost your [[cognitive]] abilities in minutes a day.
The patient showed no signs of [[cognitive]] impairment after the fall.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Познавательный» фильм или передача — educational или informative. Cognitive — научный термин о мышлении: cognitive skills, cognitive decline.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Ухудшение памяти и мышления — cognitive decline. Mind и thinking — существительные и в этой роли не используются, а intelligent — «умный» о человеке.

nuance.text: She studied [[cognitive]] science, which combines psychology, linguistics and computing.
nuance.explanationRu: Cognitive — научный термин о процессах мышления, отсюда название дисциплины cognitive science. Mental — общее «психический, умственный»: mental health, mental illness.

reverse.text: Talking openly about [[mental]] health at work is becoming more common.
reverse.explanationRu: Психическое здоровье — mental health. Cognitive относится только к мышлению и памяти, а не к эмоциональному состоянию человека.

fixIt.text: Memory, attention and reasoning are all [[psychic]] abilities that can be trained.
fixIt.explanationRu: Psychic — «экстрасенсорный» (psychic powers). Память, внимание и логика — cognitive abilities, то есть познавательные способности.

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: Researchers are studying how poor sleep affects [[cognition]] in teenagers.

words.definitionEn: to happen at the same time as something else
words.senseNote: Здесь — «совпадать по времени»; о мнениях или интересах (our views coincide) — «совпадать, сходиться».
words.situation: Two events happen on the same day or at the same moment, by chance or because someone planned it.

examples.text: The strike was timed to [[coincide]] with the start of the tourist season.
My holiday [[coincides]] with the conference, so I'm afraid I can't give a talk.
The opening of the new museum [[coincided]] with the city's 800th anniversary.

texts: We planned the product launch to [[coincide]] with the trade fair.
It's rare for our days off to [[coincide]], so we hardly see each other.
The two exams [[coincide]], so I'll have to choose one.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Совпадать по времени» — просто coincide (with something); by time или in time добавлять не нужно.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Приурочить событие к другому — time something to coincide with. Match — подходить по виду, fit — по размеру, meet — встречаться; здесь они не подходят.

nuance.text: The shop's big sale was planned to [[coincide]] with payday.
nuance.explanationRu: Coincide — просто совпадать по времени, часто специально. Clash — неудачно совпасть и мешать друг другу; нарочно планировать такое странно.

fixIt.text: Our holiday dates [[matched]] with the carnival, so every hotel in town was full.
fixIt.explanationRu: Совпасть по времени — coincide with. Match значит «соответствовать, подходить» (цвета, данные) и о событиях в таком значении не используется.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B2
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: By pure [[coincidence]], my new manager grew up on the same street as me.

reply.context: Your manager emails: "Could you run the training session on the 14th?"
options: Sure — it coincides perfectly, because I'm on holiday that week.
I'd love to, but it coincides with a client visit. Would the 15th work?
Negative. A coincidence of engagements renders me unavailable.
reply.explanationRu: Coincide — совпадать по времени, поэтому «идеально совпадает, ведь я в отпуске» звучит нелепо. Третий ответ слишком резкий и канцелярский для письма руководителю.

rewrite.original: The concert and the football final are on the same evening.
rewrite.frame: The concert ____ the football final.
rewrite.explanationRu: Происходить одновременно — coincide with.

words.definitionEn: to work together with other people to create or achieve something
words.senseNote: Здесь — «сотрудничать»; collaborate with the enemy — «сотрудничать с врагом» (неодобрительно).
words.situation: People from different teams, companies or countries work together on a shared project, such as a study or an album.

examples.text: Researchers from six countries [[collaborated]] on the study, sharing their data online.
The two authors are [[collaborating]] on a novel, writing alternate chapters.
If we [[collaborate]] with the marketing team from the start, the launch will go much more smoothly.

texts: Our two departments rarely [[collaborate]], which causes a lot of confusion.
Artists and scientists will [[collaborate]] on an exhibition about climate.
Students are encouraged to [[collaborate]] rather than compete for grades.

badCollocation.noteRu: Над проектом работают вместе с предлогом: collaborate on a project; с людьми — collaborate with someone.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Тесно работать с другой командой — collaborate closely with. Combine — соединять вещи, join — присоединяться, gather — собираться; с closely with они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The two directors [[collaborated]] on the screenplay for almost three years.
nuance.explanationRu: Collaborate — вместе создавать что-то (книгу, фильм, исследование). Cooperate — содействовать, выполнять просьбы, не мешать; о совместной работе над сценарием звучит слабее.

reverse.text: The suspect refused to [[cooperate]] with the police.
reverse.explanationRu: Выполнять требования полиции, не мешать следствию — cooperate. Collaborate — совместно что-то создавать, к допросу не подходит.

fixIt.text: For her new album, she [[contributed]] with a young jazz pianist from New Orleans.
fixIt.explanationRu: Работать вместе с кем-то — collaborate with someone. Contribute — вносить вклад (contribute to something), with после него в этом смысле не ставят.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: The professor and her [[collaborator]] published their findings last week.

words.definitionEn: the process of working together with other people to produce or achieve something
words.situation: People or organisations join forces on a shared piece of work, such as research, an album or a product.

examples.text: The new range of trainers was designed in [[collaboration]] with a young fashion designer.
The discovery was the result of close [[collaboration]] between chemists and computer scientists.
The programme encourages [[collaboration]] between schools in different countries.

texts: The album was recorded in [[collaboration]] with a symphony orchestra.
Good [[collaboration]] between nurses and doctors saves lives.
The report stresses the need for international [[collaboration]] on climate.

badCollocation.noteRu: Стандартная фраза в объявлениях и письмах — thank you for your cooperation. Collaboration — совместная творческая или научная работа.

collocationTask.explanationRu: В тесном сотрудничестве с кем-то — in close collaboration with. Teamwork, unity и work в этой конструкции не используются.

nuance.text: The festival was organised in [[collaboration]] with local artists and schools.
nuance.explanationRu: Collaboration — открытая совместная работа. Collusion — тайный сговор ради нечестной цели, поэтому in collusion with local artists звучит как обвинение.

reverse.text: Two supermarket chains were fined for [[collusion]] over milk prices.
reverse.explanationRu: Незаконный сговор, например о ценах, — collusion. Collaboration — честная совместная работа, за неё не штрафуют.

fixIt.text: The new drug was developed through close [[co-working]] between scientists in Oslo and Madrid.
fixIt.explanationRu: Совместная работа учёных — collaboration. Co-working — это коворкинг, общее офисное пространство, а не сотрудничество.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: Designing the new park was a truly [[collaborative]] effort involving local residents.

reply.context: At a job interview, you're asked: "How do you usually work with other departments?"
options: I prefer collaboration, so I usually do everything alone and just report at the end.
Collaboration? Yeah, whatever works, I'm easy.
I believe in close collaboration — regular check-ins and shared goals from day one.
reply.explanationRu: Collaboration — совместная работа, а не «всё делать в одиночку». Второй ответ слишком небрежный для собеседования.

rewrite.original: The museum and a local school worked together on the exhibition.
rewrite.frame: The museum organised the exhibition in ____ a local school.
rewrite.explanationRu: Совместно с кем-то — in collaboration with.

words.definitionEn: shared, done or felt by all the members of a group together
words.situation: Everyone in a team, community or country shares a decision, a responsibility, a memory or an effort.

examples.text: The failure of the project was a [[collective]] responsibility, not the fault of one manager.
Old photographs and songs help to keep a nation's [[collective]] memory alive.
Workers won better pay through [[collective]] action rather than individual complaints.

texts: We made a [[collective]] decision to cancel the trip.
When the results came in, there was a [[collective]] sigh of relief in the office.
The team celebrated its [[collective]] success with a dinner.

badCollocation.noteRu: Общее фото — a group photo. Collective говорят о решениях, ответственности и действиях: collective responsibility.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Все разом облегчённо выдохнули — a collective sigh of relief, устойчивое выражение. Rest, calm и comfort с sigh of не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The whole nation felt a [[collective]] sense of pride after the team's victory.
nuance.explanationRu: Collective — общий для всей большой группы: a collective sense of pride. Joint — совместный для нескольких конкретных участников: a joint account, a joint statement.

reverse.text: My partner and I opened a [[joint]] bank account after the wedding.
reverse.explanationRu: Общий счёт двух людей — a joint account. Collective говорят о целом коллективе или обществе, а не о паре.

fixIt.text: The union called for [[collected]] action to protect jobs at the factory.
fixIt.explanationRu: Совместные действия, например профсоюза, — collective action. Collected значит «собранный, спокойный» или «собранный в одном месте».

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: The five of us are [[collectively]] responsible for the budget.

reply.context: At a team meeting, your manager says: "The client is unhappy with the report. How did this happen?"
options: It was a collective failure — Mark did the whole thing by himself.
Honestly, it was a collective failure. We all rushed it, so we should all fix it.
Collective culpability is hereby acknowledged by the undersigned.
reply.explanationRu: Collective — общий для всей группы, поэтому «коллективная ошибка одного человека» — противоречие. Третий ответ звучит как юридический документ, а не ответ на встрече.

rewrite.original: Everyone in the team is responsible for the result.
rewrite.frame: The result is the team's ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Общая ответственность группы — collective responsibility.

words.definitionEn: an accident in which a moving vehicle, ship or person hits another
words.senseNote: Здесь — физическое столкновение; в переносном смысле — столкновение идей или интересов (a collision of cultures).
words.situation: Two cars, ships, planes or people crash into each other, usually by accident.

examples.text: Three people were injured in a [[collision]] between a bus and a lorry on the motorway.
The goalkeeper was taken to hospital after a [[collision]] with an opposing player.
Scientists believe the moon formed after a [[collision]] between the young Earth and another planet.

texts: The ship's radar should have prevented the [[collision]].
Luckily, nobody was hurt in the [[collision]] at the crossroads.
Two cyclists had a minor [[collision]] on the narrow path.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Конфликт интересов» — a conflict of interest; о споре мнений — a clash. Collision — прежде всего физическое столкновение.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Лобовое столкновение — a head-on collision (или head-on crash). Collapse — обрушение, contact — контакт, incident — происшествие; с head-on они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The two ships were on a [[collision]] course until the captain changed direction.
nuance.explanationRu: On a collision course — на курсе, который ведёт к столкновению. Crash course — ускоренный интенсивный курс обучения, совсем другое значение.

reverse.text: Before the trip, I did a two-week [[crash]] course in Spanish.
reverse.explanationRu: Ускоренный курс обучения — crash course. Collision course — курс, ведущий к столкновению, к учёбе не относится.

fixIt.text: Nobody was hurt in this morning's [[clash]] between a taxi and a delivery van.
fixIt.explanationRu: Столкновение машин — collision (или crash). Clash — стычка между людьми или конфликт мнений, о ДТП так не говорят.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: The pilot's quick reaction prevented a mid-air [[collision]].

reply.context: A friend texts: "Sorry I'm late — there's been an accident on the bridge and nothing's moving."
options: Please provide a full written account of the collision upon arrival.
Oh no, a collision! Was it a very long argument?
Oh no, I hope nobody was hurt in the collision. Take your time.
reply.explanationRu: Collision — физическое столкновение машин, а не спор. Первый ответ звучит как требование страховой компании, а не как ответ другу.

words.definitionEn: connected with the rule of one country over another land and its people
words.senseNote: Здесь — о колониальном правлении и его эпохе; в США colonial также называют архитектурный стиль XVII–XVIII веков.
words.situation: You talk about the time when a powerful country ruled another territory, or what that time left behind.

examples.text: Many of the region's roads and railways were built in the [[colonial]] era.
The country gained independence in 1962 after almost a century of [[colonial]] rule.
The old town is full of elegant [[colonial]] buildings with wooden balconies and shutters.

texts: The museum tells the story of the city's [[colonial]] past.
Spain and Portugal were major [[colonial]] powers in the sixteenth century.
The hotel is a beautiful [[colonial]] mansion surrounded by gardens.

badCollocation.noteRu: Территория под чужим управлением — a colony (a former British colony). Colonial — прилагательное: colonial rule, colonial buildings.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Под колониальным управлением — under colonial rule. Management и leadership — о руководстве компанией или командой, command — о военном командовании.

nuance.text: Many local languages were banned in schools during the [[colonial]] period.
nuance.explanationRu: Colonial — связанный с колониями и их управлением: так говорят о прошлом бывшей колонии. Imperial — связанный с империей или императором: an imperial palace, the imperial family.

reverse.text: Tourists queue for hours to visit the [[imperial]] palace.
reverse.explanationRu: Дворец императора — imperial palace. Colonial относится к колониям и колониальному правлению, а не к императорской семье.

fixIt.text: The port grew rich from the sugar trade during the [[colonist]] era.
fixIt.explanationRu: Нужно прилагательное: the colonial era — колониальная эпоха. Colonist — существительное, «колонист, поселенец».

wordFormation.text: Many streets in the capital still have their old [[colonial]] names.

rewrite.original: For two hundred years, the island was ruled by a European country.
rewrite.frame: For two hundred years, the island was under ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Под управлением другой страны — under colonial rule.

words.definitionEn: a journalist who writes a regular opinion piece for a newspaper, magazine or website
words.situation: Someone writes a regular article in the same newspaper, sharing opinions about politics, food, money or life.

examples.text: As a food [[columnist]], she eats out four nights a week and writes about it every Sunday.
In this week's piece, the paper's political [[columnist]] criticises the new housing policy.
The magazine's advice [[columnist]] receives hundreds of letters about love and family problems every week.

texts: She started as a sports reporter and is now a weekly [[columnist]].
The [[columnist]] apologised for a joke that offended many readers.
Every newspaper needs a sharp [[columnist]] who isn't afraid to annoy people.

badCollocation.noteRu: Колумнист пишет колонки в газете, журнале или онлайн. На радио и ТВ обозревателя называют commentator или presenter.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Колумнист, который пишет о политике, — a political columnist: нужно прилагательное. Politician — политик, politic — «благоразумный», politically — наречие.

nuance.text: Every Saturday, the [[columnist]] shares her strong opinions on modern parenting.
nuance.explanationRu: Columnist — автор регулярной колонки, где главное — его мнение. Correspondent — корреспондент, который сообщает новости с места событий или по своей теме.

reverse.text: Our Tokyo [[correspondent]] sends this report from the scene of the earthquake.
reverse.explanationRu: Журналист, который передаёт новости с места событий, — correspondent. Columnist пишет авторские колонки с мнением, а не репортажи.

fixIt.text: She's the magazine's technology [[observer]] and writes a new piece every week.
fixIt.explanationRu: Автор регулярной колонки — columnist. Observer — наблюдатель (например, на выборах), журналистов-обозревателей так не называют.

cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

wordFormation.text: After years as a reporter, he became a [[columnist]] with his own weekly page.

words.definitionEn: to take action to reduce or stop something harmful, such as crime or disease
words.senseNote: Здесь — «бороться с проблемой»; в прямом смысле combat — сражаться с противником, а существительное combat — «бой».
words.situation: Governments, doctors or companies take serious action against a problem like crime, disease, fraud or loneliness.

examples.text: The city has hired more police officers to [[combat]] rising street crime.
Doctors say regular exercise is one of the best ways of [[combating]] stress.
The council runs weekly lunches to [[combat]] loneliness among older residents.

texts: New laws are needed to [[combat]] the spread of fake news.
Scientists are developing new drugs to [[combat]] resistant bacteria.
The campaign aims to [[combat]] bullying in secondary schools.

badCollocation.noteRu: Combat — бороться против чего-то, без предлога: combat crime. «Бороться за» что-то — fight for: fight for equal rights.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Бороться с распространением — combat (или fight, tackle) the spread. Struggle и compete требуют предлога (with, against), а win значит «выиграть».

nuance.text: The city launched a campaign to [[combat]] litter in its parks.
nuance.explanationRu: Combat — активно бороться с проблемой, чтобы её стало меньше. Resist — сопротивляться давлению или соблазну (resist change, resist temptation); с мусором так не говорят.

reverse.text: I couldn't [[resist]] the temptation to have another slice of cake.
reverse.explanationRu: Не устоять перед соблазном — can't resist the temptation. Combat — бороться с общественной проблемой, а не с желанием съесть торт.

fixIt.text: The new government has promised to [[fight with]] corruption at every level.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Бороться с коррупцией» — combat (или fight) corruption, без with. Fight with someone значит «драться или ссориться с кем-то».

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

reply.context: At a residents' meeting, someone asks: "What is the council actually doing about all the graffiti?"
options: We're combating it by giving everyone free spray paint.
We're combating it with faster clean-ups and legal walls where artists can paint.
Yeah, we're kinda combating it, like, sort of.
reply.explanationRu: Combat — бороться с проблемой, чтобы её стало меньше, а бесплатная краска только добавит граффити. Третий ответ слишком небрежный для официальной встречи.

words.definitionEn: to begin or start, especially in official situations
words.situation: An official notice, contract or announcement says when work, a ceremony or a legal process will start.

examples.text: Construction of the new bridge will [[commence]] in early spring, subject to planning permission.
The ceremony will [[commence]] at 11 a.m., and guests are asked to be seated by 10.45.
Successful candidates will [[commence]] employment on 1 September.

texts: Boarding will [[commence]] thirty minutes before departure.
Please do not [[commence]] the exam until you are told to.
Repairs to the roof will [[commence]] once the rain stops.

badCollocation.noteRu: Commence — официальное слово. О бытовых делах говорят start или begin: start the washing-up.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Начать судебный процесс — commence (или start, bring) legal proceedings. Make, do и set с proceedings не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The anniversary celebrations will [[commence]] with a parade through the old town.
nuance.explanationRu: Commence — начинаться (официально). Commemorate — чтить память о событии или человеке, например commemorate the victims; начаться с парада им нельзя.

reverse.text: A statue was put up to [[commemorate]] the town's most famous poet.
reverse.explanationRu: Увековечить память — commemorate. Commence значит «начинать(ся)» и к памятнику не подходит.

fixIt.text: According to the official notice, the hearing will [[kick off]] at 10 a.m. in Courtroom 2.
fixIt.explanationRu: В официальном объявлении kick off звучит слишком разговорно. Здесь нужно формальное commence.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: The [[commencement]] of the new contract has been delayed until June.

reply.context: At a formal conference, the chair turns to you and asks: "Is the panel ready to begin?"
options: Yes, we're ready to commence whenever you are.
Yes, we commenced an hour ago, so we're just about to start.
Yeah, let's get this show on the road, mate!
reply.explanationRu: Commence значит «начинать», поэтому «начали час назад и вот-вот начнём» — бессмыслица. Третий ответ слишком фамильярный для официальной конференции.

words.definitionEn: a live description of a match, race or ceremony for listeners or viewers
words.senseNote: Здесь — живой репортаж (football commentary); commentary также значит «комментарий к тексту» или «критический взгляд» (a commentary on modern life).
words.situation: Someone describes a football match, a race or a royal wedding live for people who are watching or listening.

examples.text: I prefer to watch the match with the sound off, because the [[commentary]] is so annoying.
We followed the race on the car radio, listening to the live [[commentary]] from the track.
My aunt kept up a running [[commentary]] on everything we passed during the drive.

texts: The [[commentary]] on tonight's final will be available in three languages.
You can switch off the [[commentary]] and just hear the crowd.
She has done the radio [[commentary]] for the marathon for twenty years.

badCollocation.noteRu: Комментарий под постом или статьёй — a comment: leave a comment. Commentary — репортаж или развёрнутый разбор.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Непрерывно комментировать происходящее — keep up a running commentary. Comment, report и speech с running в этом значении не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Millions of fans listened to the radio [[commentary]] as the final went into extra time.
nuance.explanationRu: Commentary — непрерывный репортаж о событии в эфире. Comment — отдельное замечание или реплика; радиорепортаж так не называют.

reverse.text: The minister refused to make any [[comment]] on the rumours.
reverse.explanationRu: Отдельное высказывание или заявление — comment: make a comment, no comment. Commentary — развёрнутый репортаж или разбор.

fixIt.text: The radio [[reportage]] of the match was so exciting that I forgot to eat.
fixIt.explanationRu: Репортаж о матче в прямом эфире — commentary. Reportage — журналистские материалы или фоторепортаж, о трансляции матча так не говорят.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: The TV [[commentary]] was so biased that I switched over to the radio.

reply.context: A friend messages: "My TV's broken, so we'll have to follow the final on the radio. Still coming over?"
options: Sure! And afterwards we can read the commentary under the club's post.
Of course! Radio commentary is actually more exciting — you imagine everything.
I shall attend, provided the commentary is of an acceptable standard.
reply.explanationRu: Отзывы под постом — comments, а не commentary. Commentary — живой репортаж, как на радио. Третий ответ звучит чопорно и официально.

words.definitionEn: an expert who discusses news or events on TV, radio or in newspapers
words.senseNote: Здесь — эксперт, который обсуждает события в СМИ (a political commentator); в спорте commentator ещё и ведёт прямой репортаж.
words.situation: An expert appears on the news or writes in the press to explain and give opinions on current events.

examples.text: On election night, TV channels invited [[commentators]] to explain what the results meant.
According to several financial [[commentators]], house prices could fall sharply next year.
The former footballer now works as a TV [[commentator]], analysing matches after they finish.

texts: She is a respected [[commentator]] on Middle Eastern politics.
The [[commentator]] predicted a crisis that never came.
He's a regular [[commentator]] on the evening news.

badCollocation.noteRu: Спортивный комментатор — a sports commentator: в роли определения обычно sports с -s (sports news, sports car).

collocationTask.explanationRu: Эксперт по какой-то теме — a commentator on something: нужен предлог on. In, at и about в этом сочетании не используются.

nuance.text: The channel invited a [[commentator]] to explain the new tax rules to viewers.
nuance.explanationRu: Commentator — эксперт, которого приглашают в эфир или публикуют в газете. Commenter — любой, кто оставил комментарий в интернете.

reverse.text: One angry [[commenter]] wrote that the article was full of mistakes.
reverse.explanationRu: Автора комментария под статьёй называют commenter. Commentator — эксперт или ведущий репортажа в СМИ.

fixIt.text: The [[politologist]] on the evening news said the result was no surprise.
fixIt.explanationRu: Эксперта, который обсуждает политику в СМИ, называют political commentator или analyst. Слово politologist в английском почти не используется.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: Some political [[commentators]] believe the new party could win seats next year.

reply.context: Your colleague says: "Did you see that economist on TV last night? She explained the budget really clearly."
options: Yes, she's a great commentator — she never gives her opinion on anything.
Affirmative. The commentator's discourse was of satisfactory quality.
Yes, she's one of the few commentators who actually make economics interesting.
reply.explanationRu: Commentator — эксперт, который как раз высказывает мнение о событиях. Второй ответ звучит как протокол или робот, а не разговор с коллегой.

words.definitionEn: the business of buying and selling goods and services, especially on a large scale
words.senseNote: У слова одно значение — торговля как сфера деятельности; для C1 важны сочетания e-commerce и the Chamber of Commerce.
words.situation: People talk about trade and business activity in general, such as online shopping or trade between countries.

examples.text: For centuries, the river was the main route for [[commerce]] between the coast and the interior.
The internet has transformed [[commerce]]: you can now buy almost anything without leaving home.
She is studying [[commerce]] and hopes to work in international banking.

texts: The Chamber of [[Commerce]] opposes the new parking charges.
Ports have always been centres of [[commerce]] and culture.
The minister for trade and [[commerce]] will visit the factory on Monday.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Заниматься коммерцией» — be in business или trade. Commerce — торговля как сфера, её не «делают».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Торговля и промышленность — commerce and industry. Commercial — прилагательное или рекламный ролик, merchandise — товары для продажи.

nuance.text: Most small shops now earn more from electronic [[commerce]] than from walk-in customers.
nuance.explanationRu: Commerce — торговля как сфера деятельности, отсюда устойчивое electronic commerce (e-commerce). Trade — обмен товарами, особенно между странами: foreign trade, a trade deal.

reverse.text: The two countries signed a new [[trade]] agreement last week.
reverse.explanationRu: Торговое соглашение между странами — trade agreement. Commerce в таких сочетаниях не используется.

fixIt.text: Cross-border [[commercial]] between the two countries doubled after the new bridge opened.
fixIt.explanationRu: Торговля — commerce. A commercial — рекламный ролик на ТВ или радио, а commercial как прилагательное значит «коммерческий».

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B2
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: The film was a huge [[commercial]] success but got terrible reviews.

words.definitionEn: the different parts, substances or people that something is made up of
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «состав» (из чего что-то состоит); «сочинение» и «музыкальное произведение» — другие, более базовые значения.
words.situation: You describe which substances, parts or kinds of people something consists of, and in what proportions.

examples.text: Scientists analysed the [[composition]] of the rock samples to find out which minerals they contained.
The new board has a more balanced [[composition]], with equal numbers of men and women.
The [[composition]] of the class has changed: half the students now come from abroad.

texts: Experts studied the [[composition]] of the paint to date the old portrait.
The ethnic [[composition]] of the neighbourhood has changed a lot since the 1990s.
Any change to the [[composition]] of the committee needs a vote by all members.

badCollocation.noteRu: О еде и блюдах говорят ingredients: What are the ingredients? Composition звучит как химический анализ.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Из чего состоит вещество — chemical composition. Construction — строительство, compilation — сборник, arrangement — расположение или договорённость.

nuance.text: In terms of its [[composition]], air is roughly 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.
nuance.explanationRu: Composition — из чего состоит вещество и в каких пропорциях. Structure — как части устроены и связаны; проценты газов — это состав, а не строение.

reverse.text: The steel [[structure]] of the bridge is designed to move slightly in strong winds.
reverse.explanationRu: Каркас, конструкция моста — structure. Composition говорит о веществах и пропорциях, а не о том, как собрана конструкция.

fixIt.text: The [[staff]] of the jury, nine men and three women, was criticised by the defence.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Состав» группы людей — composition (или makeup). Staff — сотрудники организации, у присяжных их нет.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B1
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: Changes in the [[composition]] of the workforce mean that most employees are now over fifty.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "They've announced the new project team: six engineers and not a single designer."
options: Nice, I love that composition — the melody is really catchy.
That's a strange team composition for a project that's all about design.
The composition of the aforementioned team is hereby acknowledged as suboptimal.
reply.explanationRu: Composition здесь — состав команды. В первом ответе слово понято как музыкальное произведение, третий звучит канцелярски для рабочего чата.

words.definitionEn: to weaken something important, such as safety or quality, or put it at risk
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «ставить под угрозу, подрывать» (compromise security); базовое «идти на компромисс» (B2) не отрабатывается.
words.situation: Careless actions or weak points make safety, security, quality or trust less reliable or put them in danger.

examples.text: Clicking on that link may have [[compromised]] your account, so change your password now.
Managers were warned that cutting staff training would [[compromise]] safety at the plant.
Accepting gifts from the companies they write about could [[compromise]] a journalist's independence.

texts: Months of treatment had left her immune system badly [[compromised]].
Investors fear the bank's reputation has been [[compromised]] by the scandal.
Police believe the witness's safety may already have been [[compromised]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Жизнь человека ставят под угрозу глаголами endanger или put at risk. Compromise — о безопасности, качестве, репутации, независимости.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Безопасность, качество, репутацию подрывают глаголом compromise. Spoil — испортить (вечер, еду), hurt и injure — ранить, причинить боль.

nuance.text: A single stolen laptop could [[compromise]] the security of the whole company.
nuance.explanationRu: Compromise — ослабить, поставить под угрозу (безопасность, качество). Violate — нарушить закон, правило или права; украденный ноутбук ничего не нарушает, он создаёт угрозу.

reverse.text: The factory was fined for [[violating]] health and safety regulations.
reverse.explanationRu: Правила и законы нарушают — violate. Compromise относится к самой безопасности или качеству, а не к правилам.

fixIt.text: One weak password can [[break]] the security of the entire network.
fixIt.explanationRu: Break security так не говорят: безопасность ставят под угрозу — compromise (или нарушают — breach).

cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B2
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

reply.context: Your IT manager emails: "Someone logged into your work account from another country last night."
options: Great, so we've finally compromised on the new password rules?
Kindly be advised that my account is compromised henceforth.
Oh no, so my account has been compromised? I'll change my password right away.
reply.explanationRu: Compromised account — взломанный аккаунт, его безопасность под угрозой. В первом ответе слово понято как «договориться», второй звучит как нелепая канцелярская отписка.

rewrite.original: Poor maintenance has put the safety of the old bridge at risk.
rewrite.frame: The safety of the old bridge ____ by poor maintenance.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the safety has been compromised.

words.definitionEn: to calculate a figure or result, especially with a machine or a formula
words.situation: You work out an exact number or result, usually with software, a formula or large amounts of data.

examples.text: Using wind and temperature data, the model [[computes]] how far the smoke is likely to spread.
The app [[computes]] how much tax you owe from the receipts you upload.
In the exam you may use a calculator to [[compute]] the averages, but you must show your method.

texts: The final score is [[computed]] from the judges' marks and the public vote.
Your pension is [[computed]] on the basis of your last three years' salary.
The distance to the star was [[computed]] from measurements of its brightness.

badCollocation.noteRu: Людей и предметы просто считают — count the guests. Compute — вычислять результат по формуле или данным.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Среднее, вероятность, стоимость вычисляют — compute (или calculate). Count — пересчитывать предметы, solve — решать задачу, number — нумеровать.

nuance.text: Every night the system [[computes]] the average delivery time for each region.
nuance.explanationRu: Count — пересчитывать предметы по одному (count the boxes). Compute — вычислять результат по данным или формуле: среднее, вероятность, стоимость.

reverse.text: Can you [[count]] how many chairs we have in the hall?
reverse.explanationRu: Стулья в зале просто пересчитывают — count. Compute звучит так, будто нужна сложная формула.

fixIt.text: The forecasting software [[counts]] the probability of rain for every hour of the day.
fixIt.explanationRu: Вероятность не пересчитывают по одному, как предметы (count), а вычисляют — computes.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B2
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Not attested in EFLLex's textbook corpus; general-English frequency from wordfreq.

wordFormation.text: Modern weather forecasts depend on huge amounts of [[computation]].

words.definitionEn: to hide something or someone, or to keep a fact or feeling secret
words.situation: Someone deliberately keeps an object, a fact or an emotion out of sight so that others will not notice it.

examples.text: She [[concealed]] the letter inside a book so that her flatmates wouldn't find it.
The director was accused of [[concealing]] important evidence from the police.
He laughed at the joke to [[conceal]] the fact that he hadn't understood it.

texts: Good make-up can [[conceal]] the signs of a sleepless night.
The report was written to [[conceal]] the real cost of the project.
He turned away to [[conceal]] the tears in his eyes.

badCollocation.noteRu: Секрет хранят — keep a secret. Conceal — скрывать факты, чувства, улики: conceal the truth.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Скрывать правду от кого-то — conceal (или hide) the truth from someone. Close и lock — закрывать дверь или замок, save — спасать или копить.

nuance.text: The old house has a narrow staircase [[concealed]] behind a bookcase.
nuance.explanationRu: Conceal — спрятать так, чтобы не было видно (за шкафом). Disguise — замаскировать под что-то другое: a door disguised as a bookcase. С behind подходит только conceal.

reverse.text: He [[disguised]] his voice so the caller wouldn't recognise him.
reverse.explanationRu: Голос не прячут, а меняют, чтобы не узнали, — disguise. Conceal значит убрать с глаз или скрыть факт.

fixIt.text: For months the manager [[covered]] the real sales figures from the rest of the team.
fixIt.explanationRu: Cover — накрыть сверху. Скрыть информацию от кого-то — conceal something from someone (или cover up).

wordFormation.text: The [[concealment]] of the test results led to a public inquiry.

reply.context: In a meeting, your boss asks: "Why didn't the client hear about the delay from us?"
options: We concealed the delay to them in detail in yesterday's email.
We never meant to conceal it — we only found out about the delay this morning.
It was never our intention to conceal the aforementioned delay from the esteemed client.
reply.explanationRu: Conceal — скрывать информацию, второй ответ естественный. В первом conceal ошибочно значит «сообщить», третий звучит напыщенно для обычного разговора.

words.definitionEn: to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true or that you were wrong
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «неохотно признать правоту»; значения «пропустить гол» и «уступить (территорию, право)» не отрабатываются.
words.situation: After arguing or resisting for some time, you finally admit that the other person has a point.

examples.text: After weeks of criticism, the minister finally [[conceded]] that the new rules had been introduced too quickly.
Afterwards, the coach honestly [[conceded]] that his team had been lucky to win.
"Fine, you might be right," she [[conceded]], still looking annoyed.

texts: Even his critics [[concede]] that he is a brilliant negotiator.
I [[concede]] that my first draft was far too long.
Most scientists now [[concede]] that the early data was misleading.

badCollocation.noteRu: Concede не употребляется с with: говорят concede that или concede a point, а «согласиться с кем-то» — agree with someone.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Признать поражение — concede defeat (или admit, accept defeat). Agree требует with или to, allow — разрешать, grant — предоставлять.

nuance.text: In the final debate, the candidate [[conceded]] that her opponent had made a fair point.
nuance.explanationRu: Concede — признать правоту оппонента в споре. Confess — сознаться в чём-то плохом или постыдном; признать чужой хороший аргумент не стыдно, поэтому confess звучит странно.

reverse.text: After hours of questioning, he [[confessed]] to the robbery.
reverse.explanationRu: Сознаться в преступлении — confess to a crime. Concede — признать правоту или поражение; «concede to the robbery» не говорят.

fixIt.text: After a long argument, my brother finally [[gave in]] that I had been right all along.
fixIt.explanationRu: Give in — сдаться, уступить; после него не ставят that. Признать, что кто-то прав, — concede that.

reply.context: During debate practice, your opponent says: "You have to admit my figures are more recent than yours."
options: Fair enough, I'll concede that point, but my main argument still stands.
No way, I concede your figures completely — they're simply wrong.
I hereby formally concede, pursuant to the aforementioned statistical data.
reply.explanationRu: Concede a point — признать правоту в одном вопросе. Во втором ответе concede ошибочно значит «отвергать», третий звучит как юридический документ.

rewrite.original: Although he didn't want to, Tom admitted that his sister was right.
rewrite.frame: Tom reluctantly ____ was right.
rewrite.explanationRu: Reluctantly concede that — неохотно признать, что кто-то прав.

words.definitionEn: to form an idea or plan in your mind, or to imagine something
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «задумать, представить себе»; значение «зачать ребёнка» не отрабатывается.
words.situation: Someone comes up with an original plan in their head, or manages to picture something in their mind.

examples.text: The festival was [[conceived]] by two students who wanted to bring live music to their town.
I can't [[conceive]] of a better way to spend a Sunday than walking in the hills.
Ten years ago, nobody could have [[conceived]] that the small start-up would become a global company.

texts: The bridge was [[conceived]] as a symbol of the city's new confidence.
The novel was [[conceived]] during a long train journey across Canada.
The project was badly [[conceived]] and ran out of money within a year.

badCollocation.noteRu: После conceive не ставят about: говорят conceive of something или conceive a plan, а «думать о проблеме» — think about a problem.

collocationTask.prompt: It's hard to ___ of a world without music.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Conceive of something — представить себе что-то. После imagine, invent и suppose предлог of не ставят: imagine a world.

nuance.text: Two engineers [[conceived]] the plan for a floating solar farm on the old reservoir.
nuance.explanationRu: Conceive a plan — придумать и продумать план или проект. Imagine — представить картинку в голове, часто нереальную; «imagine a plan» звучит странно.

reverse.text: Close your eyes and [[imagine]] you're lying on a warm beach.
reverse.explanationRu: Представить себе картинку — imagine. Conceive — книжное слово про идеи и планы, в такой просьбе не подходит.

fixIt.text: She first [[invented]] the plan for the charity while she was working as a nurse abroad.
fixIt.explanationRu: Invent — изобрести устройство или способ. План или проект задумывают — conceive a plan.
