wordFormation.text: It is [[conceivable]] that prices will fall again next year, though few experts expect it.

rewrite.original: It was impossible for me to imagine life without my children.
rewrite.frame: I couldn't ____ life without my children.
rewrite.explanationRu: Conceive of something — представить себе что-то (книжно).

words.definitionEn: an idea or understanding of what something is like or should be
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «представление, понимание» (a conception of justice); значение «зачатие» не отрабатывается.
words.situation: You describe how a person, group or culture understands what something is, means or ought to be.

examples.text: Young children have a very different [[conception]] of time: for them, a week can feel endless.
Our [[conception]] of what counts as a family has changed a great deal over the last fifty years.
The new manager's [[conception]] of teamwork seemed to mean everyone simply agreeing with her.

texts: Each generation has its own [[conception]] of success.
Her [[conception]] of a relaxing holiday involves climbing three mountains.
The film questions our [[conception]] of what makes a hero.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Концепция» продукта или бренда — concept: a marketing concept. Conception — чьё-то представление о чём-то.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Узкое представление об успехе — a narrow conception of success. Conceit — самомнение, concession — уступка, conscience — совесть.

nuance.text: The study challenges the popular [[conception]] of teenagers as lazy and selfish.
nuance.explanationRu: Conception — представление людей о ком-то или чём-то (the popular conception of teenagers). Concept — сама идея или замысел (a new café concept); здесь речь о взглядах.

reverse.text: The restaurant's [[concept]] is simple: you pay only for the time you spend there.
reverse.explanationRu: Замысел, «концепция» бизнеса или продукта — concept. Conception — чьё-то представление о чём-то, к ресторану не подходит.

fixIt.text: Medieval maps show that people then had a very limited [[presentation]] of how big the world was.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Представление о чём-то» — conception (или idea), а не presentation: presentation — это доклад или показ.

wordFormation.text: Our [[conception]] of privacy has changed since everyone started carrying a smartphone.

rewrite.original: People today understand childhood very differently from people in the past.
rewrite.frame: Our ____ childhood is very different from that of people in the past.
rewrite.explanationRu: A conception of something — представление о чём-то.

words.definitionEn: something that you agree to give up or allow in order to reach an agreement
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «уступка» (make concessions); значения «льготная скидка» и «право на торговлю» не отрабатываются.
words.situation: During a negotiation or dispute, one side gives up part of what it wanted so that both sides can agree.

examples.text: After a week of strikes, management made several [[concessions]], including shorter shifts and a pay rise.
Letting my sister choose where we went on holiday was a big [[concession]] on my part.
In the trade talks, neither country was willing to offer [[concessions]] on farming.

texts: Working from home on Fridays was a small [[concession]], but staff appreciated it.
The new law was widely seen as a [[concession]] to farmers.
Watching her favourite film again was my only [[concession]] all weekend.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Пойти на уступки» — make concessions; калька go on concessions неверна.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Идти на уступки — make concessions. Do, take и put с concession не сочетаются.

nuance.text: As a [[concession]] to local residents, the airport will stop night flights.
nuance.explanationRu: Concession — то, что одна сторона уступает другой (a concession to residents). Compromise — договорённость, где уступают обе стороны; «a compromise to someone» не говорят.

reverse.text: After hours of arguing, the two partners finally reached a [[compromise]].
reverse.explanationRu: Прийти к компромиссу — reach a compromise: уступают обе стороны. Concession делают (make), а не «достигают».

fixIt.text: To end the strike, the government made an important [[compromise]] to nurses on pay.
fixIt.explanationRu: Compromise — взаимное соглашение. То, что одна сторона даёт другой, — concession: make a concession to someone.

cefrEvidence.label: B2
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

wordFormation.text: Every [[concession]] we made seemed to encourage the other side to demand more.

reply.context: Your flatmate says: "OK, you can have the bigger room, but then you pay a bit more rent."
options: Thanks, but I don't need a concession — I'm not a student any more.
Your concession is hereby accepted; the relevant documentation will follow.
That's quite a concession — thanks! I'm happy to pay a bit extra.
reply.explanationRu: Здесь concession — уступка соседа по квартире. В первом ответе слово понято как льготная скидка для студентов, второй звучит как официальное письмо.

rewrite.original: Neither side was willing to give up anything to reach an agreement.
rewrite.frame: Neither side was willing to ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Идти на уступки — make concessions.

words.definitionEn: to say publicly and strongly that something or someone is morally wrong
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «публично осуждать»; значения «приговаривать (к наказанию)» и «признавать здание непригодным» не отрабатываются.
words.situation: Leaders, groups or organisations publicly declare that an action or statement is completely unacceptable.

examples.text: Several charities [[condemned]] the decision to cut funding for mental health services.
The company quickly [[condemned]] the manager's comments and said they did not reflect its values.
Many people [[condemn]] fast fashion, but they still buy cheap clothes every season.

texts: The attack was [[condemned]] by religious leaders of every faith.
His remarks were widely [[condemned]] as offensive and out of date.
Testing cosmetics on animals has long been [[condemned]] by many scientists.

badCollocation.noteRu: Condemn — резкое публичное осуждение серьёзных поступков. За опоздание друга можно разве что criticise или tell off.

collocationTask.prompt: The decision was widely ___ by teachers.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Решение или поступок «широко осуждают» — widely condemned. Blame и accuse говорят о людях (blame someone for), judge — оценивать или судить.

nuance.text: The football club [[condemned]] the fans' behaviour and promised to ban those responsible.
nuance.explanationRu: Condemn — публично осудить поступок как недопустимый. Blame — считать кого-то виноватым в чём-то: blame someone for something; без for фраза не работает.

reverse.text: Don't [[blame]] yourself: the accident wasn't your fault.
reverse.explanationRu: Винить себя — blame yourself. Condemn — публичное моральное осуждение, для утешения друга слишком резко.

fixIt.text: Human rights groups sharply [[judged]] the arrest of the two journalists.
fixIt.explanationRu: Публично и резко «осудить» — condemn. Judge — оценивать или судить, со sharply так не говорят.

cefrEvidence.label: B2

wordFormation.text: The plan to close the library drew strong [[condemnation]] from parents and teachers.

reply.context: A friend texts: "The mayor called the vandalism in the park 'completely unacceptable'."
options: Good. It's right that she condemned it so clearly.
Really? Why would she condemn the park? It's lovely.
One must concur that the mayor's condemnation was wholly appropriate.
reply.explanationRu: Condemn — публично осудить поступок: мэр осудила вандализм. Во втором ответе слово отнесено к самому парку, третий звучит слишком книжно для переписки с другом.

rewrite.original: Environmental groups strongly criticised the plan, calling it dangerous.
rewrite.frame: Environmental groups ____ as dangerous.
rewrite.explanationRu: Condemn something as dangerous — осудить что-то, назвав опасным.

words.definitionEn: to train someone over time to behave, think or react in a particular way
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «приучать, формировать поведение» (be conditioned to do something); значение «ухаживать (за волосами)» не отрабатывается.
words.situation: Repeated experience, training or advertising makes people or animals automatically behave or think in a certain way.

examples.text: In the experiment, the dogs were [[conditioned]] to expect food whenever they heard a bell.
We have been [[conditioned]] by advertising to believe that newer always means better.
Years of early shifts have [[conditioned]] her to wake up at five, even on holiday.

texts: Many of us are [[conditioned]] to check our phones the moment we wake up.
Soldiers are [[conditioned]] to obey orders without questioning them.
Girls were once [[conditioned]] to believe that science was not for them.

badCollocation.noteRu: Привычку вырабатывают — develop или form a habit. Condition относится к людям и животным: condition someone to do something.

collocationTask.prompt: We are ___ to believe that being busy means being successful.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Be conditioned to do something — быть приученным к чему-то, часто незаметно. После be used to нужен -ing, adapted — приспособленный, addicted — зависимый.

nuance.text: Years of strict schooling had [[conditioned]] him to raise his hand before speaking.
nuance.explanationRu: Condition — незаметно «запрограммировать» поведение (школа, опыт, реклама). Accustom — приучить к условиям: accustomed to the noise; с to raise не сочетается.

reverse.text: After a month in Norway, we had become [[accustomed]] to the long summer evenings.
reverse.explanationRu: Привыкнуть к обстановке — become accustomed to. Condition — выработать реакцию или поведение, к летним вечерам не подходит.

fixIt.text: Most of us have been [[adjusted]] to see a suntan as a sign of good health.
fixIt.explanationRu: Adjust — настраивать или приспосабливаться. «Нас приучили так думать» — we have been conditioned to see или think.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: Social [[conditioning]] teaches many boys to hide their feelings.

reply.context: A friend says: "I feel guilty whenever I take a day off, even when I'm ill."
options: Maybe your flat needs conditioning — it's far too hot in there.
It would appear that you have undergone a process of behavioural conditioning.
I think we've been conditioned to see rest as laziness. It isn't.
reply.explanationRu: Be conditioned to — быть «приученным» что-то чувствовать или думать. Первый ответ путает с кондиционером, второй звучит как научная статья, а не разговор с другом.

words.definitionEn: to give someone an official honour, degree or right, or to give an advantage
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «присваивать, предоставлять» (confer a degree on someone); значение «совещаться» (confer with colleagues) не отрабатывается.
words.situation: A university, state or other authority officially gives someone a title, degree or right, or something brings an advantage.

examples.text: The university will [[confer]] an honorary degree on the author at next month's ceremony.
Citizenship [[confers]] certain rights, such as the right to vote and to hold a passport.
Speaking several languages can [[confer]] a real advantage in the job market.

texts: The title was [[conferred]] on him for services to medicine.
Membership of the club [[conferred]] a certain status on the whole family.
The degrees were [[conferred]] at a small ceremony in the college chapel.

badCollocation.noteRu: Confer не берёт два дополнения подряд: не confer someone a title, а confer a title on someone.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ an honorary degree on the singer
collocationTask.explanationRu: Почётную степень присваивают — confer a degree on someone (или bestow). Appoint — назначать на должность, donate — жертвовать, assign — поручать.

nuance.text: In the past, owning land [[conferred]] enormous social status on a family.
nuance.explanationRu: Confer — официально дать статус, право или преимущество (confer on). Award — вручить приз, премию или оценку (award to); статус не вручают как награду.

reverse.text: She was [[awarded]] first prize in the national poetry competition.
reverse.explanationRu: Приз на конкурсе вручают — award. Confer — торжественно присвоить звание, степень или право, а не приз.

fixIt.text: Last year the academy [[assigned]] an honorary title on the retired professor.
fixIt.explanationRu: Assign — поручить задание или назначить номер. Звание присваивают — confer a title on someone.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

reply.context: A friend messages: "My old university is giving my grandmother an honorary doctorate!"
options: Wow! Will she confer with them about it first?
Kindly convey my felicitations upon the conferring of said doctorate.
Amazing! When do they confer it? I'd love to be at the ceremony.
reply.explanationRu: Confer a doctorate — присвоить почётную степень. В первом ответе confer with понято как «совещаться», второй звучит как старинное официальное письмо.

rewrite.original: The university gave her an honorary degree in 2019.
rewrite.frame: An honorary degree ____ in 2019.
rewrite.explanationRu: Пассив с предлогом on: a degree was conferred on her.

words.definitionEn: a formal statement in which someone admits that they have committed a crime
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «признание вины» (sign a confession); личное «признание» (I have a confession to make) и «исповедь» не отрабатываются.
words.situation: Police or a court get a statement from a suspect in which he or she admits committing the crime.

examples.text: The suspect signed a [[confession]] after twelve hours of questioning.
The judge ruled that his [[confession]] could not be used because police had threatened him.
The detective series ends when the butler makes a full [[confession]] to the theft.

texts: Police say the [[confession]] matches the evidence found at the scene.
She later withdrew her [[confession]], claiming she had been confused and exhausted.
Without a [[confession]], the case against him is surprisingly weak.

badCollocation.noteRu: Признание делают — make a confession (или sign, give a full confession); do здесь не подходит.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Признаться — make a confession (или give, sign a confession). Do, take и say с confession не сочетаются.

nuance.text: After ten hours of questioning, the suspect finally made a full [[confession]].
nuance.explanationRu: Русское «признание» бывает разным: признание вины — confession, признание заслуг — recognition. На допросе делают confession.

reverse.text: The scientist finally received [[recognition]] for her work on the vaccine.
reverse.explanationRu: Признание заслуг, известность — recognition. Confession — признание вины, к научной работе не подходит.

fixIt.text: The court heard that his [[acknowledgement]] had been obtained under pressure.
fixIt.explanationRu: Признание вины в суде или полиции — confession. Acknowledgement — подтверждение получения или благодарность.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

cefrEvidence.label: B2
cefrEvidence.note: Lower label for the same word+POS in another list (usually a more basic sense).

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: After three days, the police finally got a [[confession]] from the driver.

reply.context: Watching a crime drama, your friend says: "I can't believe the neighbour did it all along!"
options: Me neither. And his confession in the last scene was so calm and cold.
Me neither. The police even gave him a confession for being so helpful.
Indeed, his confession constitutes a legally admissible statement of guilt.
reply.explanationRu: Confession — признание вины, первый ответ естественный. Во втором confession ошибочно значит «награда», третий звучит как протокол, а не разговор у телевизора.

words.definitionEn: the way in which the parts of something are arranged or set up
words.situation: You describe how the parts of a room, vehicle, machine or computer system are arranged or set up.

examples.text: The airline changed the seating [[configuration]] so that each plane can carry twenty more passengers.
Before installing the update, save a copy of your current network [[configuration]].
The two molecules contain the same atoms, but in a different [[configuration]].

texts: The hall can be used in almost any [[configuration]], from rows of chairs to small tables.
Engineers tested a new wing [[configuration]] in the wind tunnel.
The default [[configuration]] works well for most home users.

badCollocation.noteRu: О форме лица, тела или предмета говорят shape. Configuration — расположение частей техники или системы.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Расположение кресел — seating configuration (или seating plan). Construction — строительство, consideration — рассмотрение, confirmation — подтверждение.

nuance.text: The IT team keeps a record of the [[configuration]] of every server in the building.
nuance.explanationRu: Configuration — общее устройство системы: какие части и как они собраны и настроены. Setting — один параметр, который можно менять: яркость, громкость.

reverse.text: Turn up the brightness [[setting]] if the screen looks too dark.
reverse.explanationRu: Отдельный параметр, например яркость, — setting. Configuration — устройство системы целиком.

fixIt.text: Two laptops that look identical may run differently if their hardware [[composition]] is different.
fixIt.explanationRu: Как собран и настроен компьютер — hardware configuration. Composition — химический состав или состав группы людей.

cefrEvidence.label: C1
cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

wordFormation.text: Incorrect [[configuration]] is the most common cause of network problems in small offices.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Why is the meeting room full of round tables today?"
options: They've changed the configuration of the tables, so they're rounder now.
They've changed the configuration for the workshop. It'll be back to rows tomorrow.
The configuration has been modified pursuant to the facilitator's specifications.
reply.explanationRu: Configuration — расстановка мебели в зале, второй ответ естественный. В первом слово понято как форма столов, третий звучит как инструкция, а не ответ коллеге.

words.definitionEn: to limit an activity or problem to a particular place, group or subject
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «ограничивать рамками» (be confined to, confine yourself to); значение «держать взаперти» не отрабатывается.
words.situation: Something happens only in one place, group or topic, or you deliberately keep it within those limits.

examples.text: The problem is not [[confined]] to big cities; many small towns are struggling too.
Please [[confine]] your questions to the topic of today's talk.
This rare frog is [[confined]] to a single valley in the mountains.

texts: Luckily, the damage was [[confined]] to the kitchen.
His interests are not [[confined]] to football; he also paints.
For centuries, the plant was [[confined]] to a few gardens in Japan.

badCollocation.noteRu: Ограничивать себя в еде — cut down on sugar или limit yourself. Confine yourself to — ограничиться чем-то: confine yourself to two questions.

collocationTask.prompt: The virus was largely ___ to older patients.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Be confined to — ограничиваться чем-то, встречаться только там. Closed, locked и shut — про двери и помещения, а не про рамки явления.

nuance.text: Let's [[confine]] the discussion to the budget and leave staffing until next week.
nuance.explanationRu: Confine — ограничить рамками: confine the discussion to the budget. Confide — доверить тайну: confide in someone. Слова похожи, но значения разные.

reverse.text: She [[confided]] in her sister that she was thinking of leaving her job.
reverse.explanationRu: Поделиться секретом, довериться — confide in someone. Confine значит «ограничить».

fixIt.text: In the past, the disease was [[restrained]] to a few remote villages.
fixIt.explanationRu: Restrain — сдерживать, удерживать силой. «Ограничивалась несколькими деревнями» — was confined to.

words.definitionEn: a statement or piece of evidence showing that something is definitely true
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «подтверждение факта» (official confirmation, confirmation of a theory), а не базовое «подтверждение бронирования».
words.situation: An official statement, a test or new evidence shows that something people suspected is definitely true.

examples.text: The club has given no official [[confirmation]] that the coach is leaving.
The new data provide strong [[confirmation]] of a theory first proposed in the 1960s.
Her silence was all the [[confirmation]] I needed that something was seriously wrong.

texts: We're still waiting for [[confirmation]] from the lab.
The news came as [[confirmation]] of what everyone had suspected.
Police are seeking [[confirmation]] of the man's identity.

badCollocation.noteRu: Подтверждение дают или получают — give, receive, get confirmation; do здесь не подходит.

collocationTask.prompt: We are still awaiting ___ from the ministry.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Ждать официального подтверждения — await confirmation. Confrontation — столкновение, consolation — утешение, conversation — разговор.

nuance.text: We have received [[confirmation]] that the samples arrived safely at the lab.
nuance.explanationRu: Confirmation — подтверждение, что что-то правда или точно произойдёт. Approval — одобрение, разрешение; то, что образцы доехали, — факт, его подтверждают.

reverse.text: Children under sixteen need their parents' [[approval]] to join the trip.
reverse.explanationRu: Разрешение родителей — approval. Confirmation подтверждает факт, а не даёт разрешение.

fixIt.text: The rumours about the merger received official [[proof]] on Friday morning.
fixIt.explanationRu: Слухи официально подтверждают — receive official confirmation. Proof — доказательство, его не «получают официально».

wordFormation.text: Independent [[confirmation]] of the findings is expected within weeks.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "I heard the office is moving to the city centre. Is that true?"
options: Only if the boss gives her confirmation. She hasn't decided yet.
That's the rumour, but we haven't had any official confirmation yet.
Affirmative. Confirmation of said relocation is pending, as per protocol.
reply.explanationRu: Official confirmation — официальное подтверждение факта. В первом ответе confirmation ошибочно значит «разрешение», третий звучит как военный рапорт.

rewrite.original: Nobody has officially confirmed the date of the concert yet.
rewrite.frame: There has been no ____ of the concert date yet.
rewrite.explanationRu: Official confirmation — официальное подтверждение.

words.definitionEn: to behave or think in the same way as most people in a group or society
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «вести себя как все, следовать нормам группы» (pressure to conform); значение «соответствовать стандартам» не отрабатывается.
words.situation: People change their behaviour, clothes or opinions to match what their group or society expects.

examples.text: Teenagers often feel huge pressure to [[conform]], even when it means hiding who they really are.
At my old firm, anyone who refused to [[conform]] to the long-hours culture was quietly sidelined.
Her paintings never [[conformed]] to the fashions of the time, which is why critics ignored her.

texts: In a small village, there is strong pressure to [[conform]].
Schools should teach children to think, not just to [[conform]].
Some people [[conform]] simply because they are afraid of standing out.

badCollocation.noteRu: Conform всегда с предлогом: conform to (или with) the rules; без предлога — ошибка.

collocationTask.prompt: strong pressure to ___ to social norms
collocationTask.explanationRu: Подстраиваться под нормы — conform to social norms. Obey, follow и respect берут дополнение без to: obey the rules.

nuance.text: He dyed his hair green partly because he refused to [[conform]].
nuance.explanationRu: Conform — вести себя как все, подстраиваться под нормы группы. Obey — выполнять приказ или закон, и ему нужно дополнение: obey the law, obey your parents.

reverse.text: Drivers must [[obey]] the speed limit near schools.
reverse.explanationRu: Соблюдать закон или правило — obey the speed limit. Conform требует to и говорит скорее о социальных нормах.

fixIt.text: People who [[correspond]] to what society expects are rarely criticised.
fixIt.explanationRu: Correspond to — соответствовать (о фактах, данных). Вести себя так, как ждёт общество, — conform to.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

wordFormation.text: Critics say the school values [[conformity]] more than creativity.

reply.context: A friend says: "My new company expects everyone to wear a suit, even on Fridays."
options: Will your suit conform? Maybe get it taken in a bit.
Will you conform, or keep wearing jeans and see what happens?
One is obliged to conform to the sartorial expectations of one's employer.
reply.explanationRu: Conform — подстроиться под правила и нормы, второй ответ естественный. В первом conform ошибочно значит «подходить по размеру», третий звучит слишком напыщенно.

words.definitionEn: to face a difficult problem or situation and start dealing with it
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение «смело встретить проблему, взяться за неё» (confront a problem, confront your fears); значение «выяснять отношения с кем-то» не отрабатывается.
words.situation: Instead of avoiding a difficult problem, fear or truth, you face it directly and deal with it.

examples.text: The new government must [[confront]] the housing crisis instead of blaming the previous one.
Therapy helped her [[confront]] her fear of flying after years of avoiding planes.
Sooner or later, the company will have to [[confront]] the fact that its main product is out of date.

texts: Doctors are [[confronted]] with difficult choices every day.
Many small farms are [[confronted]] with rising costs and falling prices.
She finally [[confronted]] the grief she had been avoiding for years.

badCollocation.noteRu: В активе confront без предлога: confront a problem. With нужен только в пассиве: be confronted with a problem.

collocationTask.prompt: Doctors are often ___ with impossible choices.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Столкнуться с трудностью — be confronted (или faced) with. Collide, crash и bump — физическое столкновение машин или предметов.

nuance.text: Instead of running away, she decided to [[confront]] her fear of public speaking.
nuance.explanationRu: Confront — сознательно встретить проблему лицом к лицу. Encounter — случайно столкнуться с чем-то; решить «encounter» свой страх нельзя.

reverse.text: On our walk through the forest, we [[encountered]] a family of deer.
reverse.explanationRu: Случайно встретить кого-то в пути — encounter. Confront — встретить проблему или человека с вызовом, к оленям на прогулке не подходит.

fixIt.text: Sooner or later, every manager has to [[oppose]] the problem of staff burnout.
fixIt.explanationRu: Oppose — выступать против идеи или решения. Смело взяться за проблему — confront a problem.

wordFormation.text: Try to avoid a [[confrontation]] with your manager in front of the whole team.

reply.context: A friend says: "I keep putting off opening my bank statements. I'm scared to see how bad it is."
options: Good idea. Confront it for a few more months and it'll go away by itself.
One must confront one's pecuniary obligations with fortitude.
I get it, but you'll feel better once you confront it. Let's look together.
reply.explanationRu: Confront — смело взглянуть проблеме в лицо, третий ответ естественный. В первом confront ошибочно значит «избегать», второй звучит напыщенно.

rewrite.original: Sooner or later, you have to deal with your problems instead of running away from them.
rewrite.frame: Sooner or later, you have to ____ instead of running away from them.
rewrite.explanationRu: Confront a problem — смело взяться за проблему.

words.definitionEn: an angry argument or conflict between people or groups who strongly disagree
words.situation: Two people or groups face each other angrily because they strongly disagree, and a fight or row seems likely.

examples.text: She avoided a [[confrontation]] with her boss by raising the issue calmly in an email.
Police stood between the two groups of fans to prevent a violent [[confrontation]].
Every family dinner turned into a [[confrontation]] about politics, so we stopped meeting.

texts: The minister wants to avoid a [[confrontation]] with the unions.
After months of tension, a [[confrontation]] between the neighbours seemed unavoidable.
The film builds slowly towards a final [[confrontation]] between the two brothers.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Столкновение мнений» — a clash of opinions (или views). Confrontation — открытый конфликт людей или групп.

collocationTask.prompt: The police wanted to avoid a direct ___ with the protesters.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Прямое столкновение — a direct confrontation. Confession — признание вины, consultation — совещание, congregation — прихожане.

nuance.text: Security had to step in when a [[confrontation]] broke out between two passengers at the gate.
nuance.explanationRu: Confrontation — прямое столкновение людей лицом к лицу. Controversy — общественный спор, полемика вокруг решения; у выхода на посадку такой не «вспыхивает».

reverse.text: The decision to cancel the festival caused a lot of [[controversy]] online.
reverse.explanationRu: Бурные споры в обществе и в сети — controversy. Confrontation — стычка конкретных людей или групп лицом к лицу.

fixIt.text: There was a short [[collision]] between two groups of fans outside the stadium.
fixIt.explanationRu: Collision — столкновение машин или предметов. Стычка людей — confrontation.

wordFormation.text: His [[confrontational]] style makes every meeting feel like a battle.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Should I tell Mark in front of everyone that his report was full of mistakes?"
options: Yes, a confrontation would be a lovely way to thank him.
I'd avoid a public confrontation. Talk to him privately first.
Confrontation is contraindicated; kindly pursue a bilateral dialogue.
reply.explanationRu: Avoid a confrontation — избежать открытого конфликта, второй ответ естественный. В первом confrontation понято как что-то приятное, третий звучит как канцелярский жаргон.

rewrite.original: The two leaders argued angrily in front of the cameras.
rewrite.frame: There was an angry ____ in front of the cameras.
rewrite.explanationRu: A confrontation between — открытое столкновение между кем-то.

words.definitionEn: to feel pleased with yourself about something you have done well or achieved
words.senseNote: Выбрано значение congratulate yourself (on something) — гордиться собой, хвалить себя; базовое «поздравлять кого-то» (B1) не отрабатывается.
words.situation: After a success or a smart decision, you privately feel proud and satisfied with what you did.

examples.text: When it started pouring, we [[congratulated]] ourselves on bringing umbrellas.
The team [[congratulated]] themselves on finishing the project two weeks early, but then the client changed everything.
Don't [[congratulate]] yourself too soon: the hardest part of the course is still ahead.

texts: She quietly [[congratulated]] herself on staying calm during the interview.
The organisers [[congratulated]] themselves on selling every single ticket.
He [[congratulated]] himself on finding such a cheap flat so close to the centre.

collocations: [[congratulate]] ourselves on a job well done

badCollocation.noteRu: По-английски congratulate on, а не with: congratulate yourself on a success.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Гордиться собой, «похвалить себя» за успех — congratulate yourself on something. Greet и welcome — приветствовать, celebrate — праздновать.

nuance.text: After parking perfectly on the first try, he [[congratulated]] himself on his driving.
nuance.explanationRu: Congratulate yourself on — порадоваться конкретному успеху (удачно припарковался). Pride yourself on — постоянно гордиться своим качеством: she prides herself on being punctual.

reverse.text: Our restaurant [[prides]] itself on using only local ingredients.
reverse.explanationRu: Постоянное качество, которым гордятся, — pride yourself on. Congratulate yourself — о радости от конкретного успеха.

fixIt.text: After the exam, I [[greeted]] myself on not panicking once.
fixIt.explanationRu: Greet — приветствовать. Похвалить себя за успех — congratulate yourself on something.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "We've hit our sales target a week early!"
options: Oh no, that's terrible. We should congratulate ourselves on the mistake.
Brilliant! We can definitely congratulate ourselves on that one.
Kindly accept this acknowledgement that self-congratulation is warranted.

rewrite.original: I felt very proud of myself for finishing the marathon.
rewrite.frame: I ____ on finishing the marathon.
rewrite.explanationRu: Congratulate yourself on something — гордиться собой за что-то.

words.definitionEn: the people attending a religious service, or the regular members of a church
words.situation: You talk about the people who come together in a church, mosque or synagogue to worship.

examples.text: The [[congregation]] stood and sang as the bride walked down the aisle.
Over the past twenty years, the church's [[congregation]] has shrunk to fewer than thirty people.
Members of the mosque's [[congregation]] take turns cooking meals for homeless people.

texts: The whole [[congregation]] rose to its feet for the final hymn.
The new vicar greeted each member of the [[congregation]] at the door.
Some of the [[congregation]] had travelled for hours to attend the funeral.

badCollocation.noteRu: Зрители на матче — crowd; congregation — только люди на богослужении.

collocationTask.prompt: The priest turned to address the ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Людей на службе в церкви называют congregation. Consultation — совещание, conversation — разговор, concentration — сосредоточенность.

nuance.text: At the end of the service, the priest blessed the [[congregation]].
nuance.explanationRu: Congregation — люди на богослужении, они молятся, а не смотрят шоу. Audience — зрители или слушатели концерта, спектакля, лекции.

reverse.text: The [[audience]] applauded for five minutes after the concert.
reverse.explanationRu: Публика на концерте — audience; congregation — только о прихожанах на службе.

fixIt.text: The [[public]] in the church stood up when the choir began to sing.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Публика» в церкви — congregation. Public — общество в целом, а не люди на службе.

words.definitionEn: the quality that makes people believe and trust someone or something
words.situation: You judge whether a person, news source or organisation deserves to be trusted and believed.

examples.text: After the scandal, the newspaper struggled to rebuild its [[credibility]] with readers.
Missing three deadlines in a row did little for my [[credibility]] as a project manager.
Relying on outdated statistics seriously undermines the [[credibility]] of your argument.

texts: The witness lost all [[credibility]] when her story changed.
Support from real doctors gave the campaign instant [[credibility]].
Constant U-turns have damaged the government's [[credibility]] on the economy.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Моё доверие к другу» — my trust in a friend. Credibility — это то, насколько верят вам самим, а не ваше доверие к другим.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Lend credibility to — делать версию или теорию убедительнее. Trust, belief и reliance — чувства того, кто верит; их не «одалживают» теории.

nuance.text: The minister's [[credibility]] suffered badly after the leaked emails.
nuance.explanationRu: Credibility — способность вызывать доверие: министру теперь верят меньше. Credulity — излишняя доверчивость, это про того, кто верит, а не про того, кому верят.

reverse.text: Online scammers rely on the [[credulity]] of their victims.
reverse.explanationRu: Мошенники пользуются доверчивостью жертв — это credulity. Credibility — заслуживает ли доверия сам говорящий.

fixIt.text: The fake story seriously damaged the newspaper's [[trust]] among readers.
fixIt.explanationRu: Доверие, которое вызывает газета, — её credibility. The newspaper's trust звучит так, будто это газета кому-то доверяет.

wordFormation.text: Several scientists questioned the [[credibility]] of the study's results.

reply.context: A colleague asks before a pitch: "Should we mention that our founder used to run a big bank?"
options: Yes, investors will value his credibility to take big risks.
Definitely. It would give us much more credibility with investors.
Affirmative. Such a fact shall duly augment our credibility in the eyes of investors.
reply.explanationRu: Credibility — доверие, которое вызывает человек или компания. В первом варианте его спутали со «способностью», третий звучит как канцелярит, а не живая речь коллеги.

rewrite.original: After the scandal, voters stopped believing anything the mayor said.
rewrite.frame: After the scandal, the mayor ____ with voters.
rewrite.explanationRu: Потерять доверие избирателей — lose credibility with voters.

words.definitionEn: convincing enough for people to believe or trust
words.situation: You decide that a story, a witness or a piece of evidence is convincing enough to accept as true.

examples.text: So far there is no [[credible]] evidence that the drug causes memory loss.
We need a [[credible]] plan for cutting costs before we speak to the board.
Honestly, his excuse about the traffic just wasn't very [[credible]].

texts: The film's plot is hardly [[credible]], but it's great fun.
Journalists must check that every source they quote is [[credible]].
The opposition has failed to offer a [[credible]] alternative.

badCollocation.noteRu: О надёжном друге говорят reliable или trustworthy friend. Credible — о словах, доказательствах и источниках, которым можно верить.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Credible witness — свидетель, словам которого можно верить. Credulous, trusting и believing значат «доверчивый»: так говорят о том, кто сам легко верит.

nuance.text: After checking every detail, the lawyer found the witness's story perfectly [[credible]].
nuance.explanationRu: Credible — правдоподобный, заслуживающий доверия. Creditable — достойный похвалы (a creditable performance); о правдивости рассказа так не говорят.

reverse.text: Finishing fourth against such strong rivals was a [[creditable]] result.
reverse.explanationRu: Результат, за который можно похвалить, — creditable. Credible значит «правдоподобный», к спортивному итогу не подходит.

fixIt.text: The police did not find the suspect's alibi [[trustful]], so they questioned him again.
fixIt.explanationRu: Trustful — «доверчивый», это о человеке. Правдоподобное алиби, которому можно верить, — credible.

cefrEvidence.note: The list labels the headword and part of speech, not individual senses.

wordFormation.text: After two failed projects, she can hardly [[credibly]] promise to finish on time.

reply.context: Your manager asks: "What do you make of the supplier's promise to deliver everything by Monday?"
options: I think they're too credible. They'll believe anything we tell them.
I hereby state that the supplier's assurance is not deemed credible by myself.
Honestly, it doesn't sound very credible, given how late they were last time.
reply.explanationRu: Credible — «правдоподобный», а не «доверчивый» (это credulous), поэтому первый ответ неверен. Второй звучит как протокол, а не как ответ руководителю.

words.definitionEn: to appear or increase slowly, almost without anyone noticing
words.senseNote: Здесь — «закрадываться, незаметно появляться или расти» (doubts crept in, prices crept up); буквальное «красться» не рассматривается.
words.situation: A doubt, an error or a rising number appears gradually, before anyone really notices it.

examples.text: A few spelling mistakes had [[crept]] into the final version of the report.
As the deadline got closer, doubts began to [[creep]] in about whether we could finish.
Unemployment has [[crept]] up to its highest level in five years.

texts: Over the years, a note of bitterness [[crept]] into his letters.
Costs [[crept]] up month after month until the project was over budget.
Doubt [[crept]] in the moment she read the contract.

badCollocation.noteRu: Creep — медленно и незаметно. О резком росте говорят shoot up или soar, а не creep up sharply.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Сомнения «закрадываются» — creep in. Crawl — ползти физически, step и walk — шагать; с сомнениями они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Without anyone noticing, a few errors had [[crept]] into the data.
nuance.explanationRu: Creep into — незаметно проникнуть (об ошибках, сомнениях, нотках в голосе). Crawl — ползти или еле тащиться (о младенцах, пробках); к ошибкам не подходит.

fixIt.text: Somehow a few serious errors [[penetrated]] into the final report.
fixIt.explanationRu: Penetrate — проникать сквозь что-то физически. Об ошибках и сомнениях, которые появляются незаметно, говорят crept in(to).

reply.context: A friend texts: "I felt ready for the exam last week, but now I'm starting to panic."
options: That's normal. Doubts always creep in the night before.
Don't worry, your marks will creep up really fast if you revise tonight.
It is to be expected that apprehension shall creep in prior to examinations.
reply.explanationRu: Creep in — о сомнениях, которые незаметно подкрадываются. Creep up значит «медленно расти», поэтому really fast противоречит глаголу. Третий ответ слишком официален для друга.

words.definitionEn: a detailed assessment that examines the strengths and weaknesses of something
words.situation: Someone carefully examines a book, theory, design or policy and explains its strengths and weaknesses in detail.

examples.text: Her essay offers a sharp [[critique]] of how social media shapes political debate.
The design workshop ends with a group [[critique]], where everyone comments on each other's work.
Two economists have published a fierce [[critique]] of the new tax rules.

texts: Her book is a powerful [[critique]] of consumer culture.
Each student must write a 500-word [[critique]] of a published study.
The architect welcomed the panel's honest [[critique]] of his design.

badCollocation.noteRu: Критиковать человека — criticise someone. Разбор работы или идеи пишут или предлагают: write/offer a critique of something.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Scathing critique — беспощадный, уничтожающий разбор; это устойчивое сочетание. Burning, boiling и hurting с critique не употребляют.

nuance.text: For homework, write a two-page [[critique]] of the story, covering both its strengths and weaknesses.
nuance.explanationRu: Critique — развёрнутый разбор с плюсами и минусами, это жанр работы. Criticism — неодобрение и упрёки; написать такой разбор словом criticism не получится.

reverse.text: The coach faced heavy [[criticism]] after the team's third defeat in a row.
reverse.explanationRu: Когда человека ругают, это criticism (face criticism). Critique — разбор работы или идеи, а не упрёки.

fixIt.text: Our professor asked us to write a short [[recension]] of the article's methods.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Рецензия» — не recension (это редакция старого текста), а critique или review.

words.definitionEn: simple and rough, without much detail, skill or accuracy
words.senseNote: Здесь — «грубый, примитивный, приблизительный» (a crude estimate); значения «сырой» (crude oil) и «пошлый» (crude jokes) не рассматриваются.
words.situation: You describe a method, estimate or object that is basic and rough rather than careful or precise.

examples.text: This is only a [[crude]] estimate, but the repairs could cost around ten thousand pounds.
Early humans made [[crude]] tools from stone and bone.
Measuring intelligence with a single test is a rather [[crude]] method.

texts: The first prototype was [[crude]], but it worked.
Even a [[crude]] sketch will help the builders understand your idea.
Income alone is a [[crude]] measure of how well people actually live.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Грубить официанту» — be rude to the waiter. Crude не описывает невежливое обращение: это «примитивный» или «пошлый».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Приблизительная оценка — a crude (или rough) estimate. Rude, harsh и cruel описывают грубое или жестокое обращение с людьми, а не неточность.

nuance.text: The map was [[crude]], but it showed us the way to the lake.
nuance.explanationRu: Crude — сделанный кое-как, примитивный. Rude — невежливый: так говорят о людях и их поведении, а не о картах и методах.

reverse.text: It was [[rude]] of him to leave without saying goodbye.
reverse.explanationRu: Невежливый поступок — rude. Crude о поведении значит «пошлый, вульгарный», а уйти не попрощавшись — просто невежливо.

fixIt.text: By a [[coarse]] estimate, about a third of the budget was wasted.
fixIt.explanationRu: Coarse — грубый на ощупь (ткань, песок). «Грубая», то есть приблизительная, оценка — a crude estimate.

wordFormation.text: The figures were [[crudely]] calculated, so treat them with caution.

words.definitionEn: to gradually lose strength and fall apart or fail
words.senseNote: Здесь — переносное «рушиться, разваливаться» (о планах, союзах, уверенности); буквальное «крошиться» не рассматривается.
words.situation: A plan, a relationship, an organisation or someone's confidence slowly weakens and then collapses completely.

examples.text: The empire began to [[crumble]] after decades of war and corruption.
Her confidence [[crumbled]] when the interviewer asked about the gap in her CV.
Their twenty-year business partnership is [[crumbling]] under the pressure of constant arguments.

texts: The alliance [[crumbled]] after only two years.
My resolve [[crumbled]] as soon as I smelled the fresh bread.
All her hopes [[crumbled]] when the second job offer was withdrawn.

badCollocation.noteRu: Стакан или чашка разбиваются — break или smash. Crumble — медленно рассыпаться: старые стены, печенье, надежды.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Crumble under pressure — сломаться, не выдержать давления. Crush — раздавить что-то, crash — разбиться, scatter — разбежаться в разные стороны.

nuance.text: Over the next ten years, the old trading empire slowly [[crumbled]].
nuance.explanationRu: Crumble — рассыпаться, постепенно разрушаться. Crumple — сминаться (бумага, кузов машины при ударе); к империям и планам не подходит.

reverse.text: He [[crumpled]] the letter into a ball and threw it away.
reverse.explanationRu: Бумагу сминают — crumple. Crumble — крошить хлеб или рассыпаться; скомкать письмо так нельзя.

fixIt.text: Their marriage slowly [[crushed]] under the weight of money problems.
fixIt.explanationRu: Crush — раздавить что-то, этому глаголу нужно дополнение. Брак, который постепенно распадается, crumbles.

corpusEvidence.note: Normalised frequency in graded EFL materials; a candidate signal, not a CEFR label.

reply.context: A friend messages: "So how's the new startup going?"
options: Brilliant! Sales have crumbled up to twice what we expected.
The enterprise is crumbling, as per my previous correspondence.
Not great, honestly. The team started to crumble after our main investor pulled out.
reply.explanationRu: Crumble — разваливаться, терять силу, поэтому с ростом продаж оно не сочетается. As per my previous correspondence — канцелярский оборот, другу так не пишут.

words.definitionEn: to defeat an opponent completely or stop resistance by force
words.senseNote: Здесь — «разгромить, подавить» (crush the opposition, crush a protest); буквальное «раздавить, смять» не рассматривается.
words.situation: One side beats its rivals so completely, or ends resistance so forcefully, that the other side has no chance.

examples.text: Our local team [[crushed]] last year's champions five goals to nil.
The giant retailer used low prices to [[crush]] smaller competitors.
The ruling party was [[crushed]] in the election, losing half its seats.

texts: Nobody expected the underdogs to [[crush]] the favourites.
The authorities tried to [[crush]] every sign of protest.
Big chains can easily [[crush]] a small family business.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Подавить зевок» — stifle или suppress a yawn. Crush — о полном разгроме соперника или жёстком подавлении протеста.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Crushing defeat — сокрушительное поражение, устойчивое сочетание. Pressing — срочный, breaking — экстренный (о новостях), squeezing с defeat не сочетается.

nuance.text: The champion [[crushed]] her opponent in straight sets.
nuance.explanationRu: Crush — разгромить соперника. Crash — разбиться или врезаться (crash into something); crash an opponent не говорят.

reverse.text: A lorry [[crashed]] into the bridge late last night.
reverse.explanationRu: Врезаться — crash into. Crush требует прямого дополнения: раздавить или разгромить кого-то.

fixIt.text: In the final, the favourites [[suppressed]] the visitors 6-0.
fixIt.explanationRu: Suppress — подавлять протест, эмоции или информацию. Разгромить соперника в игре — crush.

reply.context: After the match, a teammate says: "Can you believe we won 7-1?"
options: I know! They crushed us so badly that we won easily.
I know! We absolutely crushed them. They never stood a chance.
Indeed, our side has comprehensively crushed the opposing party.
reply.explanationRu: Crush — разгромить. В первом ответе смысл перевёрнут: если разгромили вас, вы не могли легко выиграть. Третий звучит как газетный отчёт, а не как слова товарища по команде.

rewrite.original: The ruling party lost the election very badly.
rewrite.frame: The ruling party ____ in the election.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the party was crushed — партию разгромили.

words.definitionEn: a small solid piece of a substance with flat sides and a regular shape
words.senseNote: Здесь — «кристалл» (кристаллы соли, льда); значение «хрусталь» (crystal glasses) не рассматривается.
words.situation: You describe tiny solid pieces with regular flat sides that form in salt, sugar, ice or snow.

examples.text: When seawater evaporates, it leaves behind white [[crystals]] of salt.
Under a microscope, you can see that every snowflake is made of tiny ice [[crystals]].
If you cool the sugar solution slowly, larger [[crystals]] will form in the jar.

texts: Frost left delicate ice [[crystals]] on the window.
Some people believe that [[crystals]] have healing powers.
Geologists found rare purple [[crystals]] inside the rock.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Кристально чистая вода» — crystal-clear water. Просто crystal water так не говорят.

collocationTask.prompt: Crystals ___ when the liquid cools slowly.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Кристаллы образуются — crystals form (или grow). Make и create требуют дополнения, а do здесь вообще не подходит.

nuance.text: Each snowflake is a six-sided ice [[crystal]] with its own unique pattern.
nuance.explanationRu: Crystal — частица правильной формы с гранями: снежинка — ледяной кристалл. Grain — просто крупинка (песка, соли, риса), форма тут не важна.

reverse.text: There was a [[grain]] of sand stuck in my eye.
reverse.explanationRu: Песчинка — a grain of sand. Crystal подчёркивает правильную форму с гранями, про песчинку в глазу так не говорят.

fixIt.text: On frosty mornings, tiny ice [[floes]] sparkle on every blade of grass.
fixIt.explanationRu: Ice floe — льдина, плавающая в воде. Крошечные льдинки инея на траве — ice crystals.

wordFormation.text: As the water evaporates, the salt slowly begins to [[crystallise]].

words.definitionEn: extremely popular with a small group of devoted fans rather than with everyone
words.senseNote: Прилагательное: a cult film, cult status — «культовый»; существительное cult («секта, культ») не рассматривается.
words.situation: A film, band, book or show is loved passionately by a devoted group of fans, though not by the mass audience.

examples.text: The film flopped at the box office but later became a [[cult]] classic.
Decades after it was cancelled, the sci-fi series still has [[cult]] status among fans.
The tiny noodle bar near the station has become a [[cult]] favourite with local chefs.

texts: The director is a [[cult]] figure in Korean cinema.
This odd little podcast has a small but loyal [[cult]] audience.
Their first album is now a [[cult]] classic among collectors.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Культовое место» в городе — обычно an iconic или a legendary place. Cult — о фильмах, книгах и группах с преданными поклонниками.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Cult status — статус культового фильма или книги. Worship — поклонение, sect — секта, hobby — увлечение; со status в этом смысле не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Few people saw it in cinemas, but among horror fans the film has [[cult]] status.
nuance.explanationRu: Cult — культовый в узком кругу преданных фанатов. Iconic — всем известный символ; фильму, который мало кто видел, это не подходит.

reverse.text: The Eiffel Tower is one of the most [[iconic]] buildings in the world.
reverse.explanationRu: Всемирно узнаваемый символ — iconic. Cult описывает то, что обожает узкий круг поклонников, а не то, что знают все.

fixIt.text: The show was cancelled after one season, but it has since gained a [[cultural]] following online.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Культовый» — cult: a cult following, a cult film. Cultural значит «культурный, связанный с культурой».

reply.context: A friend asks: "Have you heard of the film Night Harbour? Hardly anyone saw it when it came out."
options: Yes! It flopped at first, but now it's a real cult classic.
Yes, it's a cult film. Absolutely everyone in the country has seen it.
Affirmative. The aforementioned motion picture enjoys cult status among connoisseurs.
reply.explanationRu: Cult film — фильм, который обожает узкий круг фанатов, а не вся страна, поэтому второй ответ противоречит смыслу. Третий звучит как пародия на официальный отчёт.

words.definitionEn: to deliberately develop a relationship, skill, image or attitude over time
words.senseNote: Здесь — «развивать, налаживать» (cultivate contacts, an image); базовое «возделывать землю, выращивать» не рассматривается.
words.situation: Someone patiently builds useful contacts, a public image or a habit through steady, deliberate effort.

examples.text: She spent years [[cultivating]] contacts in the film industry before starting her own company.
The mayor has carefully [[cultivated]] an image as an ordinary person who takes the bus.
Parents can [[cultivate]] a love of reading by sharing books with their children every night.

texts: Politicians work hard to [[cultivate]] the support of young voters.
It takes months to [[cultivate]] a habit of daily exercise.
Smart startups [[cultivate]] close ties with their first customers.

badCollocation.noteRu: Ребёнка воспитывают — raise или bring up a child. Cultivate — развивать качества, связи или образ, а не растить детей.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Cultivate an image — целенаправленно создавать образ. Educate — обучать людей, raise — растить детей или поднимать, breed — разводить животных.

nuance.text: Over the years, the lawyer has [[cultivated]] a reputation as a tough negotiator.
nuance.explanationRu: Cultivate a reputation — сознательно создавать репутацию. Grow — выращивать растения или расти самому; с reputation в этом смысле звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: Tomatoes [[grow]] best in a warm, sunny spot.
reverse.explanationRu: Растения растут сами — grow. Cultivate — действие человека: он что-то выращивает или развивает.

fixIt.text: It took her years to [[raise]] such a loyal network of clients.
fixIt.explanationRu: Raise — растить детей или поднимать что-то. Сеть клиентов и полезные связи целенаправленно выстраивают — cultivate.

reply.context: At a networking event, a new colleague asks: "How did you win so many clients in your first year?"
options: I just cultivated them. I sent the same cold email to ten thousand people.
Mostly by cultivating relationships. I stayed in touch even when there was no deal on the table.
One endeavours to cultivate one's clientele assiduously, as one ought.
reply.explanationRu: Cultivate — терпеливо развивать отношения, а массовая рассылка писем — противоположность этому. Третий ответ звучит напыщенно и старомодно.

rewrite.original: Over many years, he deliberately built up friendships with influential people.
rewrite.frame: Over many years, he ____ friendships with influential people.
rewrite.explanationRu: Cultivate friendships — сознательно выстраивать полезные связи.

words.definitionEn: to criticise someone or something strongly and publicly
words.senseNote: Здесь — публично осуждать. Реже denounce значит «донести на кого-то» или «денонсировать договор».
words.situation: A leader, group or public figure says openly that an action, law or person is wrong or shameful.

examples.text: Human rights groups [[denounced]] the new law as an attack on free speech.
In an angry post, the footballer [[denounced]] the racist abuse he had received after the match.
Two senior surgeons publicly [[denounced]] the plan to cut night staff, calling it dangerous.

texts: It is easy to [[denounce]] greed while quietly enjoying its benefits.
The minister was forced to [[denounce]] the comments made by his own adviser.
Few writers dared to [[denounce]] the regime while it was still in power.

badCollocation.text: [[denounce]] someone to five years in prison
badCollocation.noteRu: Суд приговаривает — sentence someone to five years. Denounce — публично осуждать, а не выносить приговор.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Denounce someone as a traitor — публично заклеймить предателем. Accuse требует of (accuse of treason), blame — for, а betray значит «предать».

nuance.text: The charity [[denounced]] the company's treatment of its workers as shameful.
nuance.explanationRu: Denounce — публично осуждать чужие действия. Renounce — официально отказываться от своего: титула, гражданства, убеждений.

reverse.text: He [[renounced]] his citizenship and moved abroad for good.
reverse.explanationRu: От гражданства, титула или наследства отказываются: renounce. Denounce — осуждать, а не отказываться.

fixIt.text: Several MPs publicly [[judged]] the decision to close the children's hospital.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Публично осудить» решение — denounce (или condemn). Judge — «оценивать, судить», осуждения в нём нет.

wordFormation.text: The report ends with a fierce [[denunciation]] of the way refugees are treated.

reply.context: A friend texts: "Did you see what the mayor said about the graffiti on the war memorial?"
options: Yes, he denounced that the memorial will be cleaned by Friday.
Yeah, he denounced it as a disgrace, and fair enough, really.
Indeed. I hereby formally denounce the aforementioned graffiti.
reply.explanationRu: Denounce something as a disgrace — публично осудить, как мэр осудил вандализм. «Denounced that» в значении «объявил» — ошибка (нужно announced), а третий ответ звучит как официальный документ.

words.definitionEn: packed with complex ideas or information and therefore hard to understand
words.senseNote: Базовое значение (B2) — густой, плотный: dense fog, a dense forest. Здесь — о тексте, перегруженном сложными идеями.
words.situation: You describe a book, report or lecture that contains so many difficult ideas that it is slow and tiring to get through.

examples.text: The first chapter is so [[dense]] that I had to read every paragraph twice.
The contract is written in [[dense]] legal language that most clients never read properly.
The novel is beautiful but [[dense]], so it's not one to read on the beach.

texts: His prose is [[dense]] but rewarding if you take your time.
The slides were too [[dense]] to read from the back of the room.
Academic writing does not have to be [[dense]] to be serious.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Плотный график» — a busy, tight или packed schedule. Dense так не говорят: это о тексте, лесе или тумане.

collocationTask.prompt: The article is ___ with technical terms.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Dense with — о тексте, где очень много терминов или идей. Full требует of (full of terms), а busy и tight с текстом так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: This paper is far too [[dense]] for first-year students to follow.
nuance.explanationRu: Dense о тексте — насыщенный сложными идеями, трудный для понимания. Thick о книге — просто толстая, со множеством страниц; сложность текста так не описывают.

fixIt.text: The lecture was so [[saturated]] that I couldn't follow the main argument.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Насыщенная» лекция — dense. Saturated — «пропитанный влагой» или «перенасыщенный» (о рынке), к лекции не подходит.

wordFormation.text: The book is so [[densely]] written that even experts read it slowly.

reply.context: A classmate asks: "Is the book on the reading list worth starting this weekend?"
options: It's quite dense, so you'll probably finish it in an hour.
Its prose is of considerable density; weekend perusal is inadvisable.
It's brilliant but pretty dense, so give yourself a few quiet evenings.
reply.explanationRu: Dense — трудный для чтения из-за обилия идей, поэтому нужно время. Прочитать такую книгу за час — противоречие, а второй ответ слишком книжный для разговора.

words.definitionEn: how many people or things there are in an area of a given size
words.senseNote: Здесь — плотность населения, застройки, пикселей. В физике density — плотность вещества (масса на единицу объёма).
words.situation: You compare how crowded cities or regions are by counting people or buildings per square kilometre.

examples.text: The island has one of the highest population [[densities]] in Europe.
Planners want to increase housing [[density]] near train stations instead of building on farmland.
The new phone screen has a higher pixel [[density]], so photos look much sharper.

texts: Traffic [[density]] peaks between eight and nine in the morning.
The city's [[density]] makes public transport cheap to run.
Areas of low [[density]] are expensive to serve by bus.

badCollocation.noteRu: Плотность бывает high или low, а не big или small: a high population density.

collocationTask.explanationRu: О плотности говорят high или low: a high population density. Big, strong и wide с density не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The city has a population [[density]] of 8,000 people per square kilometre.
nuance.explanationRu: Показатель «сколько людей на квадратный километр» — density. Concentration — скопление в одном месте: a concentration of shops in the centre.

reverse.text: There is a large [[concentration]] of tourists around the cathedral.
reverse.explanationRu: Скопление людей в одном месте — concentration. Density — показатель на единицу площади, и large density не говорят.

fixIt.text: This district has the highest population [[thickness]] in the country, so parking is a nightmare.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Плотность населения» — population density. Thickness — толщина предмета (стены, льда), к населению не подходит.

wordFormation.text: The high [[density]] of housing here leaves little room for parks.

rewrite.original: An enormous number of people live in every square kilometre of the city.
rewrite.frame: The city has an extremely high ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Число жителей на единицу площади — population density.

words.definitionEn: the state of needing someone or something so much that you cannot manage without them
words.situation: A country, company or person cannot manage without the money, help or supplies that someone else provides.

examples.text: The country is trying to reduce its [[dependence]] on imported gas.
Nicotine creates a strong physical [[dependence]], which is why quitting is so hard.
Moving abroad forced her to overcome her [[dependence]] on her parents for every decision.

texts: Too much [[dependence]] on spellcheckers can weaken your writing skills.
Bad harvests exposed the region's [[dependence]] on imported grain.
The start-up's [[dependence]] on a single investor worried its staff.

badCollocation.noteRu: После dependence нужен предлог on: dependence on parents. «From» — калька с «зависимость от».

collocationTask.explanationRu: С предлогом on сочетается dependence (или reliance). Addiction и attachment требуют to, а confidence — in.

nuance.text: Young children's [[dependence]] on their parents is completely natural.
nuance.explanationRu: Dependence — естественная потребность в ком-то: дети в родителях, страна в импорте. Addiction — болезненное пристрастие к наркотикам или играм; о детях звучит абсурдно.

reverse.text: Her [[addiction]] to online shopping left her deep in debt.
reverse.explanationRu: Пагубная страсть к шопингу, играм или телефону — addiction to. Dependence звучит здесь слишком нейтрально, и предлог to с ним не используется.

fixIt.text: The region's [[reliability]] on tourism made the pandemic especially painful.
fixIt.explanationRu: Reliability — надёжность. «Зависимость от туризма» — dependence (или reliance) on tourism.

wordFormation.text: Many small towns have an unhealthy [[dependence]] on a single employer.

reply.context: Your manager asks: "Seventy per cent of our income comes from one client. Should we worry?"
options: Yes, that kind of dependence on one client is risky if they ever leave.
Not really, our dependence means we're free to choose any client we like.
Totally, mate, the whole dependence thing is well dodgy.
reply.explanationRu: Dependence on one client — зависимость от одного клиента, и это риск. Во втором ответе dependence перепутано с independence, а третий слишком фамильярен для разговора с руководителем.

words.definitionEn: to represent or show someone or something in art, film or writing
words.situation: A painting, novel or film shows people, places or events in a particular way.

examples.text: The mural [[depicts]] fishermen bringing in their catch at dawn.
Early novels often [[depicted]] city life as dirty and dangerous.
In the advert, the bank is [[depicted]] as a friendly neighbour who is always there to help.

texts: It is hard to [[depict]] grief without becoming sentimental.
The game's designers wanted to [[depict]] the city exactly as it looked in 1920.
Children were asked to [[depict]] their family using only three colours.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Изобразить удивление» (притвориться) — pretend to be surprised или fake surprise. Depict — изображать в картине, фильме или книге.

collocationTask.prompt: The film ___ him as a lonely genius.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Depict somebody as something — изображать кого-то каким-то в фильме или книге. Draw — рисовать, outline — кратко излагать, а images как глагол здесь не подходит.

nuance.text: The documentary [[depicts]] daily life on a remote Scottish island.
nuance.explanationRu: Depict — изображать в фильме, книге, на картине. Picture (глагол) — представлять себе в воображении: I can't picture him as a boss.

reverse.text: I can't [[picture]] myself living in such a big city.
reverse.explanationRu: «Представить себя» в воображении — picture yourself. Depict — изображать в произведении, а не мысленно.

fixIt.text: The fresco on the ceiling [[describes]] scenes from the life of a local saint.
fixIt.explanationRu: Describe — рассказывать словами. Фреска или картина изображает: depicts.

wordFormation.text: Critics praised the film's honest [[depiction]] of life in a care home.

rewrite.frame: The film ____ a dangerous place.
rewrite.explanationRu: Конструкция depict something as something — изображать что-то каким-то.

words.definitionEn: to move soldiers, police or equipment into position so that they are ready to act
words.senseNote: В IT deploy значит «выкатывать, запускать» программу; здесь — о войсках, полиции и спасателях.
words.situation: Soldiers, police officers or rescue teams are sent to an area and put in position, ready for action.

examples.text: Hundreds of extra police officers were [[deployed]] in the city centre for the final.
Within hours of the earthquake, the government [[deployed]] rescue teams with sniffer dogs.
Around two thousand troops will be [[deployed]] to the region as part of the peace mission.

texts: The government may [[deploy]] the army if the floods get worse.
Mountain rescue services now [[deploy]] drones to search for missing hikers.
It takes about ten minutes to [[deploy]] the flood barriers.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Развернуть дискуссию» — start или open a debate. Deploy — развернуть войска, полицию или технику.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Войска на границу направляют: deploy (или send) troops to the border. Place и put требуют at или on, а locate значит «найти» или «располагать».

nuance.text: The navy [[deployed]] two ships to protect the fishing fleet.
nuance.explanationRu: Оба глагола переводятся «развернуть», но deploy — направить силы или технику на позицию, а unfold — развернуть что-то сложенное: карту, письмо, одеяло.

reverse.text: She [[unfolded]] the letter and began to read.
reverse.explanationRu: Развернуть сложенный лист, карту или скатерть — unfold. Deploy — только о войсках, полиции и технике.

fixIt.text: The government has [[located]] two thousand extra troops along the border.
fixIt.explanationRu: Разместить войска — deploy (или station) troops. Locate значит «найти» или «располагать» (здание), а не перебрасывать силы.

reply.context: In a planning meeting for a big outdoor concert, the event manager asks: "How are we handling security at the gates?"
options: We'll deploy the fans at each gate so they can find their seats faster.
Security personnel shall be deployed in accordance with the aforementioned protocols.
We'll deploy extra stewards at every gate as soon as the crowds start arriving.
reply.explanationRu: Deploy stewards — расставить охрану по местам, это верно. Зрителей не deploy, их пропускают, а второй ответ звучит как канцелярский документ, а не реплика на совещании.

words.definitionEn: the process of putting new technology or systems into use on a large scale
words.senseNote: Также — развёртывание войск (troop deployment); здесь — внедрение технологий, сетей и систем.
words.situation: A company or government starts using new equipment or software widely, for example across a whole country.

examples.text: The [[deployment]] of faster mobile networks has been slow in rural areas.
Cheaper batteries could speed up the [[deployment]] of solar power in poorer countries.
After a smooth [[deployment]], all staff were using the new booking system within a week.

texts: Large-scale [[deployment]] of the software begins in March.
Wind farm [[deployment]] has doubled in the past five years.
The app's [[deployment]] was delayed by a last-minute security bug.

badCollocation.noteRu: Новый закон или правила вводят: the introduction of a new law. Deployment — внедрение техники, сетей и программ.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Внедрение техники — deployment. Placement — размещение (стажёра, рекламы), occupation — профессия или оккупация, appointment — назначение или встреча.

nuance.text: The [[deployment]] of charging stations along motorways is behind schedule.
nuance.explanationRu: Implementation — выполнение плана, решения или закона. Deployment — физическое внедрение техники: станций, сетей, дронов.

reverse.text: The [[implementation]] of the peace agreement will take years.
reverse.explanationRu: Соглашение, реформу или решение выполняют: implementation. Deployment — про технику и системы, а не про договорённости.

fixIt.text: The [[implantation]] of AI tools in our hospitals is happening faster than expected.
fixIt.explanationRu: Внедрение технологий — deployment (или introduction). Implantation — имплантация в медицине, к программам и системам не подходит.

rewrite.frame: The ____ the new software in all offices began in June.
rewrite.explanationRu: После deployment нужен предлог of: the deployment of the software.

words.definitionEn: to leave a layer of sand, mud or minerals on something, as water does
words.senseNote: Базовое значение (B2) — класть деньги на счёт. Здесь — о реке, воде, ветре: оставлять слой ила, песка, осадка.
words.situation: A river, flood or hard water leaves behind a layer of mud, sand or minerals on a surface.

examples.text: Each spring the river floods and [[deposits]] a layer of rich mud that makes the fields fertile.
Hard water [[deposits]] limescale inside your kettle, which is why it turns white over time.
Excess fat is often [[deposited]] around the waist and hips as we get older.

texts: Glaciers [[deposit]] huge rocks far from where they started.
Strong winds can [[deposit]] desert sand on cars hundreds of miles away.
The tides [[deposit]] seaweed and plastic along the beach every morning.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Отложить встречу» — postpone или put off a meeting. Deposit «откладывает» только слой ила, песка или осадка.

collocationTask.prompt: The flood ___ a thick layer of mud in the streets.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Река или наводнение deposit (или leave) слой ила. Place — аккуратно класть, settle — оседать, deliver — доставлять.

nuance.text: The river [[deposits]] fine sand along its banks.
nuance.explanationRu: Deposit — река или вода оставляет осадок: The river deposits sand. Settle — сам осадок оседает: The sand settles at the bottom.

fixIt.text: Every year the river [[postpones]] a thick layer of silt on the surrounding fields.
fixIt.explanationRu: Русское «откладывать» — это и postpone (отложить встречу), и deposit (отложить осадок). О реке и иле — только deposit.

wordFormation.text: Rivers shape the landscape through erosion and [[deposition]].

reply.context: Your flatmate asks: "Why is there white stuff all over the inside of the kettle?"
options: It's limescale. The water round here deposits it every time you boil it.
Calcium carbonate is deposited from the aqueous solution upon heating.
It's limescale. The kettle deposits the water when it gets too hot.
reply.explanationRu: Вода deposit (оставляет) накипь — верно. Чайник не «откладывает воду», а второй ответ звучит как учебник химии, а не разговор с соседом.

rewrite.original: The river left layers of fine sand along its banks.
rewrite.frame: Layers of fine sand ____ along the river's banks.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: sand was deposited, layers were deposited.

words.definitionEn: to prevent someone from having something they need, or to take it away
words.situation: Someone is not allowed to have something they need, such as sleep, food, freedom or education.

examples.text: Constant noise from the building site [[deprived]] us of sleep for weeks.
Millions of girls around the world are still [[deprived]] of a basic education.
Cutting the art classes would [[deprive]] students of their only creative outlet.

texts: The long delay [[deprived]] fans of the chance to see the final race.
Children [[deprived]] of affection often struggle to trust adults later.
Without the grant, the village would be [[deprived]] of its only library.

badCollocation.noteRu: Deprive всегда с of: deprive people of their rights. «From» — ошибка по аналогии с prevent from.

collocationTask.prompt: I've been ___ of sleep all week.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Be deprived of sleep — быть лишённым сна, недосыпать. Lack употребляют без of (I lack sleep), а missed и lost так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Plants [[deprived]] of light soon turn yellow and die.
nuance.explanationRu: Deprive of — лишать необходимого, часто из-за обстоятельств. Deny — отказать в чём-то (решение людей), и без of: denied a visa.

reverse.text: She was [[denied]] a visa because of a mistake on her form.
reverse.explanationRu: Отказать в визе, доступе или праве — deny somebody something. «Deprived a visa» — ошибка: и смысл другой, и нужен был бы предлог of.

fixIt.text: The long drought has [[lost]] farmers of their main source of income.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Лишить кого-то чего-то» — deprive somebody of something. Lose — «лишиться, потерять» самому, конструкции lose somebody of нет.

wordFormation.text: Sleep [[deprivation]] makes it much harder to concentrate at work.

reply.context: A colleague says: "I've been working till two in the morning every night this week."
options: Your sleep deprivation is regrettable and has been duly noted.
No wonder you look exhausted. You've deprived yourself of sleep all week.
Wow, you must feel really deprived of work at the moment.
reply.explanationRu: Deprive yourself of sleep — лишать себя сна, это как раз про коллегу. «Deprived of work» — нехватка работы, а у коллеги её слишком много; первый ответ звучит как официальное письмо.

rewrite.original: The noise outside stopped us from sleeping all night.
rewrite.frame: The noise outside ____ sleep all night.
rewrite.explanationRu: Deprive somebody of something — лишить кого-то чего-то.

words.definitionEn: the person ranked just below a manager or leader, who replaces them when they are away
words.senseNote: В некоторых странах deputy — депутат парламента, но главное значение — заместитель: deputy director, deputy head.
words.situation: You talk about the person who ranks just below the boss and takes over when the boss is absent.

examples.text: When the director is away, her [[deputy]] chairs the weekly meetings.
As [[deputy]], she runs the school whenever the head teacher is away.
The mayor was ill, so his [[deputy]] opened the new bridge instead.

texts: She was promoted to [[deputy]] editor after only two years.
The head of department and her [[deputy]] both interviewed me.
The [[deputy]] manager approved my holiday request this morning.

badCollocation.noteRu: Члена британского парламента называют MP (Member of Parliament). Deputy — прежде всего «заместитель».

collocationTask.prompt: She's the ___ head of our school.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Заместитель директора британской школы — deputy head. Vice бывает в vice-president или vice-chancellor, но не с head; second и under так не говорят.

nuance.text: While the head teacher is on maternity leave, her [[deputy]] is running the school.
nuance.explanationRu: Deputy — заместитель: замещает руководителя и принимает решения. Assistant — помощник, выполняет поручения, но не руководит вместо начальника.

fixIt.text: Please send any urgent questions to the [[substitute]] manager while I'm on holiday.
fixIt.explanationRu: Заместитель руководителя — deputy manager. Substitute — замена (запасной игрок, учитель на один урок), а не должность.
